patches.title: Unwrap the plugin tool envelope in MCP gateway responses
patches.problem: For a paperclip_plugin tool the gateway service returned the dispatcher envelope {pluginId, toolName, result: {content, data}}. The MCP route (server/src/routes/tool-gateway.ts) looked for data at the envelope level and answered structuredContent: null, with the whole envelope as text and isError: false even when the plugin refused. The Claude Code 2.1.322 MCP client rejects such a result whole ("structuredContent expected record, received null"), so every plugin tool (router, Discord Notifier, agent-ledger) was unusable for agents on the Claude engine (Dev Unity run 03ff8ab1, 13 Nov 2026). Codex 0.166.0 tolerated it and handed its agents the envelope as text.
patches.reason: Taken as is from the open upstream fix rather than a studio patch: the service returns the plugin's own result; the route sets structuredContent only for an object data, uses the plugin content as text, and turns a plugin error into isError: true with its message; the native Runner treats a plugin error the same way.

The Studio Secretary answers Fahd, whose Discord messages make him the responsible user of her runs (run-preparation.ts resolveResponsibleUserIdForRunSeed, comment author); Fahd never opens the board, so the Notion Reader connection, per_user with Amyne's grant only, stayed unusable for her (run aee047cf, 13 Nov 2026).
patches.reason: Amyne decided the Secretary reads Notion with his access (studio decision V185, 13 Nov 2026). Sharing the connection with the company is not acceptable: its finalize step rebinds the app profile to every active catalog entry (78, of which 39 write or destructive) for every agent. A second connection would start with its whole catalog enabled. A delegation names one owner, one grant, one connection and one agent, and changes no profile, policy or catalog.

patches.title: Short commands (ssh, git) start from a small helper process, not from the server process
patches.problem: On Linux, Node starts a child with fork, and the kernel copies the page tables of the calling process on the calling thread. The server starts every short ssh and git command itself. Production, 13 Nov 2026, 2026.1110.0-studio.12, 21:43-21:50 UTC, about 5 remote runs, read from /proc: server process 1.6 GiB resident with 31 MB of page tables; 10 process starts per second (3.0 to 3.8 ssh from the callback bridge, one per idle wait and four per agent request, and bursts of 'git -C <path> rev-parse --show-toplevel'); main thread at 44 to 55 % of one core, of which 18 to 25 points are kernel time; up to 24 ms of kernel time on the main thread per process start. The machine is 17 % busy on 8 cores: one thread is the limit. The cost grows with the memory of the server: on the morning of 13 Nov, at 2.3 GiB and 15 ssh per second, the server saturated with about 10 remote runs (STUDIO-0020 lowered the count of starts, not the cost of one start).
patches.reason: Requested by Amyne on 13 Nov 2026 (V247): a study of a solution that uses all the processors of the machine, and the improvement in a dedicated chat if it is feasible. The study (path A, step A1) selected this correction; the main session opened its implementation as a draft pull request. Merge and deployment need Amyne's explicit approval of this specific correction. No native setting changes how the server starts a process, and an adapter cannot change it. Approval: Amyne, 14 Nov 2026 (journal V256), for this correction: put the multi-core improvement in production as soon as it is ready.
patches.owner: adapter-utils short command execution (ssh.ts), server execution workspaces (runGit), server startup

patches.problem: When a prepared interactive process (codexPreparedProcess, claudePreparedProcess) has not proven its stop, the finally block of the codex_local and claude_local execute keeps the callback bridge for the provider but drops the only reference to it; only onProcessStopped clears the flag, so a cancellation without that receipt leaves the bridge poll loop running for the life of the server. Production, 14 Nov 2026: run e3dff48b-fdf2-46f4-b900-596aa4b802ae (Game Tester, TR-710, router 0.30.6 native-ssh adapter) was cancelled at 00:30:55 UTC; its bridge kept starting ssh to MAC-02 (100.80.44.46), logged transient poll failures during the MAC-02 restart at 00:32:36 and resumed at 00:33:03, with the server not restarted. The router 0.30.7 calls onProcessStopped only when the stop is proven, not when the worker is unreachable, so the server, which owns the bridge, must stop it itself. Downstream code path only: the prepared-process hooks exist only in this fork.

patches.title: The HTTP/2 callback relay on the worker exits once its host session closes
patches.problem: Production, Razer, 14 Nov 2026: paperclip-bridge-server.mjs (PID 1463) still running from run 44d28dd6 of * Dev Unity, started 13 Nov around 23:09 and ended router_provider_stop_unverified at 23:30:28 (studio.13). An answer given during the hold is set aside (deferred_issue_execution); the reconciliation takes the same path (no continuation) and the release pass re-admits the set-aside answer once: one run for the task. A pending approval requested by the assignee takes the same path. Refused with 409, hold unchanged: a question addressed to an agent only, a cancelled question, a question replaced by an agent-addressed card. With ownership-hold-readmission, deferred-execution-receipt-work, heartbeat-undispatched-execution-wait and execution-projection: 248 passed. Negative control (new cases on studio.18, 73b4ede7): the three reconciliation cases fail; the three refusals pass there too (existing behaviour). Typecheck: no error in the changed files. Review fixes: (1, 2) the release pass re-admits a held wake only behind a hold reconciled because the task waits on a person (awaitingResponseReconciliation), never behind a dependency-blocked reconciliation, workspace repair or containment: a message held behind a STUDIO-0048 reconciliation with an open blocker stays held; (3) a withdrawn wait (question cancelled, expired, withdrawn or replaced by an agent-addressed card, approval rejected) with no run of the assignee since the reconciliation is handed once to the ordinary continuation delivery (continuationDelivery pending, awaitingResponseWithdrawnAt), checked at most every five minutes while such a reconciliation waits; (4) an approval decision wakes the requester only when approved (routes/approvals.ts); a rejection takes the withdrawn path; revision_requested waits on the agent and no longer counts; (5) the answer's run carries the interaction in its context and starts in a fresh session. issue-recovery-actions.test.ts: 125 passed; with the four related files 249 passed before the last one-line fix (transaction around the hand-off). Second review fix (15 Nov): an answer is never taken for a withdrawal. The hand-off needs a proof of withdrawal dated after the reconciliation (a person's question cancelled or expired, including replaced by a newer card, but not closed by the person's comment; or an approval rejected, cancelled or sent back for revision) and no answer since (no answered, accepted or rejected question, no question closed by a comment, no approval approved, no comment by a person), no queued, claimed or held wake of the assignee on the task, and no run of the assignee on it since the reconciliation. Once such a run exists, the wait is closed as satisfied (continuationDelivery satisfied, awaitingResponseSatisfiedByRunId): the five-minute checks stop and the card reads 'Continued in another run'. New cases: an answered question whose wake is still queued, an answered question with no wake recorded yet, and a question closed by the person's comment never get a continuation; the answered path ends satisfied, naming the answer's run. issue-recovery-actions.test.ts: 128 passed. Last retouches (15 Nov): (1) an answer whose wake was lost (for example an approval decided while the requester is paused, approval.requester_wakeup_failed) no longer stops the task for good: with an answer since the reconciliation, nothing pending, no queued, claimed or held wake and no run since, the continuation is delivered once the last answer is fifteen minutes old; the source run itself never counts as a later run. The dispatcher's issue_not_in_progress cancellation on a blocked task is shown by the lot 20 bench, not by a unit test here (forcing the task blocked in the fixture does not reproduce it). Third review fixes (4ec8ac5c): a person's comment posted while a run of the assignee was working on the task is not counted as an answer (that run read it, or the comment's own wake holds the hand-offs); the five-minute check is asked only while the task is open and still assigned to the role the wait returns to. patches.migration: None. Started from the Board route (resolve of the awaiting-response hold); afterwards the scheduled check acts on its own (the withdrawn and lost-answer hand-offs and the satisfied close, every five minutes while a wait is open, for at most seven days). The STUDIO-0048 no-continuation path also applies when the blocked task has no open blocker but waits on a person: a pending question addressed to a user with continuation policy wake_assignee, a pending approval linked to the task and requested by the assignee, or an answer already set aside behind this hold (deferred_issue_execution with executionWait.recoveryActionId of this action). Evidence awaitingResponseReconciliation true; projection 'Reconciled', starts again when the answer comes. A question addressed to an agent does not count (the worker router's interruption card is one; its acceptance does not wake the assignee), nor a question to a person with policy none or wake_assignee_on_accept (a decline would leave the task stopped): such a task keeps the hold. The deferred-receipt release now also re-admits, once, a wake held behind an action reconciled with continuationDelivery not_requested, once the task has no execution blocker (same retire-then-readmit as for ownership holds); this also covers messages held behind a STUDIO-0048 reconciliation. A wait closed as satisfied keeps the release of a wake still held behind it (queue.ts accepts not_requested or satisfied). Limit: a person's comment counts as an answer, so a comment without a wake also leads to one continuation after fifteen minutes when nothing else starts the assignee. Lot 21: the awaiting path moves a task waiting on a person's question to in_progress (Board route; the request's sourceIssueStatus stays blocked, the server picks the status); approvals keep blocked. Lot 21, second review (15 Nov): the run that closes the wait is a run of the assignee that did provider work (started, without preDispatchCancellation or executionRecovery providerWorkStarted false) and that was created after the last answer; nothing closes the wait while a question or an approval is pending; the withdrawn and lost-answer hand-offs also wait while a run of the assignee on the task is queued, running or scheduled for retry; a pending continuation is re-checked at delivery and set back to not_requested if an answer, a wake or such a run came meanwhile; an answer held behind the hold merges only into a queued wake (never a claimed one); with a pending approval and an answer held behind the hold, the task goes back to in_progress; stranded-work recovery keeps a task with a pending wake_assignee question in its status while its assignee is not invokable (agent in error) instead of escalating it to blocked. Limits: after seven days the hand-offs stop and ordinary recovery takes over; while an awaiting reconciliation is open the control schedule asks for a check every five minutes (one small conditional UPDATE pair; it keeps the server from idling longer than five minutes during that time). Known remaining (bench of d3d9da4e, Q6, kept for the window of 15 Nov 2026): when a blocker is added and finished while an answer is held behind the hold, two runs can start (the dependency run, then the held answer promoted by upstream promoteDeferredWake when that run ends); the second is correct but redundant, because the merge goes only into a still-queued wake (never a claimed one). Possible later fix: in promoteDeferredWake, do not promote a held answer behind a reconciled hold (payload.executionWait.recoveryActionId) when the finishing run is the assignee's, did provider work and started after that wake was requested; coalesce it instead, with a real-path test.

patches.title: A monitor whose last allowed check was triggered, or whose timeout passed, without a next check wakes its owner once
patches.problem: Production, studio.17, 14 Nov 2026, TR-915 (Game Integrator): an external-service monitor (TeamCity Debug, maxAttempts 3, timeoutAt 23:31:41Z, recoveryPolicy escalate_to_board) ran its third check at 23:01:37 and then ended silently: no next check, state triggered 3/3, no comment, no activity, no wake. The limit handling (heartbeat/scheduling.ts, issueMonitorLimitClearReason and clearIssueMonitorAndRecover) runs only when a scheduled check falls due with nextAttemptCount above maxAttempts, while rescheduling is refused once attemptCount reaches maxAttempts ('Monitor bounds are already exhausted', issue-execution-policy.ts); the timeout acts only on a scheduled check too. So the attempt limit was unreachable and every recovery policy dead after the last check. Three roles (Game Integrator, CEO on TR-978, Infra Manager on TR-969) then searched for an automatic Board escalation and asked the owner for a way to reach Paperclip support.

patches.validation: Linux, Node 24.22.2, embedded PostgreSQL. issue-monitor-scheduler.test.ts with scheduling.test.ts: 90 passed. Thirteen STUDIO-0049 cases: the TR-915 state (triggered 3/3, no next check, no monitor in the policy, last check received by the assignee) under escalate_to_board and under wake_owner gives one admitted owner wake (run id recorded), then the cleared state, one comment ('last allowed check was triggered (3/3)', 'This monitor will schedule no further check.', 'There is no Paperclip support to contact; ask the Board with a question on this task.'), issue.monitor_exhausted, issue.monitor_recovery_wake_queued and, for that policy only, issue.monitor_escalated_to_board; a later tick after the woken run wakes nobody and posts nothing. A paused agent: nothing cleared, no comment, no admitted run, one issue.monitor_deferred over two ticks; after the agent resumes, the next tick settles it once. A timed-out monitor without a next check is settled timeout_exceeded. A run scheduled for retry, queued or running (linked by issue_id), a pending question and a pending approval linked to the task each leave the monitor triggered with no wake or comment, and the first tick after it clears settles it. A reassigned task (the last check went to another agent) and a trigger older than 24 h wake nobody. nextIssueMonitorAt returns the timeout of a triggered monitor that has no next check. From a real final check (third due check triggered by the tick), once the fixture run's artefacts are cleared (no-disposition run: task blocked, open recovery action), the next tick wakes the owner once; the blocked state itself is left alone by design. scheduling.test.ts updated for the exhausted counter. Negative control (the new cases on the studio.18 code, 73b4ede7): all thirteen fail. Typecheck: no error in the changed files. Independent review of head 5bbe0f95 (drafts/reveil-questions/revue-independante-pr52.md): G1, G2, M1 to M5, m1, m2, m3 (stated here), m5 fixed; m4 accepted (one candidate scan a minute at most, JSONB without an index); left untested: two server instances racing (the clear is a conditional update keyed by lastTriggeredAt and the wake key is shared) and the native-run guard (same condition as the existing due-check path). Second review pass (head e55bcde8): R1 a monitor still unsettled 24 h after its last trigger or timeout (wake never admitted, or a guard that never clears) is now ended once without the idle guards, up to 7 days old: state cleared, a comment saying the owner could not be woken and why (task busy, or wake not admitted), issue.monitor_exhausted with wake not_admitted, no wake; R2 the assignee link compares the agent of the latest check wake of the task written up to 15 min after lastTriggeredAt (slow ticks); R3 the instruction also travels in the wake payload (monitorRecoveryInstruction); R4 a held wake is retried at most every 15 min per task; R5 create_recovery_issue reuses an open recovery task instead of replaying its creation; R6 record path and unused test value fixed. issue-monitor-scheduler.test.ts with scheduling.test.ts: 93 passed, with new cases for the 24 h exit (task busy; wake not admitted) and a check wake written 5 min late. Left: an agent with wakeOnDemand false (its skipped rows are now at most four an hour per task), and a cut between wake and clear (the next pass reuses the admitted wake under the same key). Third pass: a monitor ended past 24 h with no held-wake record says only that it ended before Paperclip could settle it and that nobody was woken (reason not_attempted), which covers exhaustions older than the install; tasks tried in the last 15 min are excluded in the selection query, so more than 50 held wakes cannot starve newer ones. 93 passed.
patches.migration: None. The monitor tick also looks, once a minute at most, at every visible open task (in_progress or in_review, assigned to an agent only) whose monitor is triggered with no next check and no monitor left in the policy, and either attemptCount >= maxAttempts with the last trigger less than 24 h old, or a timeoutAt passed less than 24 h ago, provided the current assignee received the last check (a wake keyed issue-monitor:<task>:... within ten minutes before the trigger). It acts only while nothing is running or waiting on the task: no run queued, running or scheduled for retry (by issue_id, native issue, issueId or taskId), no execution or checkout run, no held wake (deferred_issue_execution), no open recovery action, no pending question, no pending approval linked to the task, and no review stage waiting on a person. It wakes the assignee first (issue_monitor_recovery, idempotency key issue-monitor-recovery:<task>:<clearReason>:<lastTriggeredAt>; a wake already admitted under that key is reused); with create_recovery_issue it creates or reuses the child recovery task instead. Only once that follow-up is admitted does it, in one transaction, clear the monitor state (max_attempts_exhausted or timeout_exceeded), post a comment saying what to do and that there is no Paperclip support (ask the Board with a question on the task), and log issue.monitor_exhausted, issue.monitor_escalated_to_board for that policy and issue.monitor_recovery_wake_queued. If the wake cannot be admitted (paused or non-invokable agent, blocked budget, execution hold, task changed), nothing is cleared: issue.monitor_deferred is logged at most once an hour and the next tick tries again with the same key. Once per exhausted monitor: the cleared state is no longer a candidate, so a role that re-arms nothing is not woken again. nextIssueMonitorAt also returns a time for such candidates and the timeout of a triggered monitor that has no next check. Deliberate policy difference: with escalate_to_board, the scheduled path (a due check past its bounds) only comments, while this catch-up also wakes the owner, so a monitor never ends without its owner being told. Known cost: the candidate scan reads issues by JSONB fields without a dedicated index, at most once a minute while a candidate waits. Past 24 h without an admitted wake (up to 7 days), the monitor is ended once with a comment saying its owner could not be woken and why, and issue.monitor_exhausted (wake not_admitted); older states are left alone. A held wake is retried at most every 15 minutes per task. Before installing, count the tasks in this state in production (read-only query kept in the studio workspace review notes). Known limit (bench, lot 19, 15 Nov 2026): when the agent is paused, the existing pause handling opens a stranded_assigned_issue action and blocks the task (Board card); this catch-up only looks at in_progress or in_review tasks, so it does not act then. On resume the existing issue_wakes_missed_during_pause wake starts the role, and a disposition repair (deliberate_wait_without_target) may follow and keep the catch-up away (open recovery action): the role is woken and the Board was told, but without this patch's 'what to do' comment; the monitor stays triggered until the 24 h exit writes its note, provided the task is back in_progress or in_review within 7 days. No case found where neither the role nor the Board is told.

patches.title: An ssh lease probe that cannot connect is a transient environment failure, retried with the existing budget
patches.problem: Production, 15 Nov 2026, TR-999: the Feedback Manager's assignment run (server ssh environment QA-C) failed in 12 s with setup_failed, 'Failed to acquire lease for environment "QA-C" (ssh)', ssh stderr 'ssh: connect to host 100.121.114.90 port 22: Connection timed out', before any provider work; the stranded-task recovery blocked the task one second later. The bounded retry of transient lease failures (environment_provider_unavailable) only reads structured evidence (HTTP status or a network errno); ssh exits 255 with no code, so a briefly unreachable machine was a permanent setup failure.
patches.reason: Requested by the studio setup session (15 Nov 2026), after the TR-999 analysis.

upstreamSearch.details: No counterpart: upstream treats any ssh exit 255 during lease acquisition as a setup failure.

patches.validation: Linux, Node 24.22.2. adapter-utils: ssh-connect-failure.test.ts (the TR-999 stderr and five other connection failures map to ETIMEDOUT, ECONNREFUSED or ENETUNREACH; permission denied, host key verification, name resolution and connection reset keep no code; the code needs ssh's exit 255) with ssh-command-managed and ssh-fixture: 44 passed (review retouch: a failure after the remote command printed something keeps no code). server: environment-provider-unavailable-error.test.ts, 39 passed, with a new case: an ssh lease probe error carrying the attached cause is read as transient (ETIMEDOUT), a permission-denied one is not. Negative control: the new adapter-utils cases fail on the studio.18 ssh.ts (function absent). Typecheck adapter-utils: no error. Review retouch (15 Nov): heartbeat-process-recovery.test.ts, new case: an ssh lease probe that could not connect is retried once (scheduled bootstrap retry), then the successor run succeeds; with the two neighbouring lease-retry cases, 3 passed. Second retouch: ssh-command-managed.test.ts checks that runSshCommand hands ssh the caller's LANG and LC_ALL unchanged (with and without stdin); adapter-utils ssh-connect-failure, ssh-command-managed, ssh-fixture and execution-target: 68 passed. Typecheck adapter-utils and server: no error.
patches.migration: None. runSshCommand (used by ensureSshWorkspaceReady, the ssh lease probe) attaches, to an ssh failure with exit 255, an empty stdout (nothing ran remotely, so a remote command that already started is never retried) and a stderr line says the connection never happened, a cause with the matching network code (connect timed out / operation timed out / banner exchange timed out -> ETIMEDOUT; connection refused -> ECONNREFUSED; no route to host / network unreachable -> ENETUNREACH). The existing classifier (readTransientEnvironmentProviderFailure, which walks causes) then makes it environment_provider_unavailable, retried with the bounded bootstrap budget and, if still failing, blocked with the 'provider temporarily unavailable, no agent work started' card. Authentication, host key and name resolution failures are unchanged (not retried). The error message itself is unchanged. The ssh environment is left unchanged (no forced locale): the default client config of the Paperclip server sends LANG and LC_* (/etc/ssh/ssh_config, SendEnv LANG LC_*) and macOS machines accept them, so a forced LC_ALL would reach the remote command; OpenSSH sets only LC_CTYPE itself, and the server has only the C, C.utf8, POSIX and en_US.utf8 locales, so the connection diagnostics stay in English. The retry budget is unchanged (2 attempts, 30 s then 60 s): a machine asleep longer ends on the 'provider unavailable, no work started' card, and waking it is an infrastructure matter.

Negative control, the same test file on fb1ad740's code: 50 fail, 8 pass (the eight kept behaviours: a person's exception in a mixed batch, the bounded run once a blocker is cancelled, a comment written while the assignee's dependency run is running, an issue never blocked, an old trace, a person's comment, the card, an unblocked issue). Three mutants: with the backstop removed, 9 backstop cases fail; with the old base branch restored, the case of the blocker fails; with the ready wakes sent again after a native decision done, the case of the parent fails and paperclip-control-plane-port fails in the three cases the bench found. paperclip-control-plane-port in full: 96/96. Native runtime, completion, decision, issue service and recovery files that were missing from the neighbours, 30 files: 29 pass (1318 cases), none fails, one is skipped whole by its own conditions (recovery-deadline-acceptance, 19 cases). The 38 other files found by grep (integration, chat, Slack, Dot, server start, workspace recovery) were not run here; the bench runs the whole suite on the candidate. Usual neighbours in full, 44 files and 2122 cases: 41 files pass in full. heartbeat-stale-queue-invalidation and heartbeat-retry-scheduling fail in 13 cases, and fb1ad740's code alone fails in the same 13 on this machine: none fails on the head without failing on the base. heartbeat-comment-wake-batching had one case that timed out in that run ("treats the automatic run summary as fallback-only when the run already posted a comment"); run alone three times on the frozen tree, the file passes (27/27, 27/27, 27/27). tsc: no error in a changed file.

Cold review, defects found in v6 and fixed: (P1) a hand-back run on "only cancelled blockers left" is bounded and never qualified, so the backstop woke every 30 s without end, as it did while a router refused: a run now qualifies through its admission's hand-over mark, the wait between two backstop wakes doubles up to 1 h, and an issue with an active recovery action is left to its owner; (P2) the base was the run's start although the batch is computed at admission: it is now the admission time; (P3) a repeated automatic hold only moves updatedAt of the earlier request, and a run cancelled at the claim gate was dated at its creation: the trace reads requestedAt, updatedAt, finishedAt and the cancellation time; (P4) after a reassignment written by a service, without activity, the new assignee had no trace: while it has no base, a hold of any agent counts; (P5) a ready wake merged into a bounded run already running removed its mark and gave it a batch it never showed: the merge changes neither once the run started; (P6) one failing wake stopped the wakes of the following dependents: one send per dependent, each logged; (P7) the route woke on every PATCH carrying blockedByIssueIds: only when the set changed; (P8) comments read again from the margin were handed over twice: those the latest qualified runs carried are left out.

Writers of blocking relations and of done/cancelled statuses (by grep): direct wake through the one function for PATCH (blocker done, blocker set changed), the comment route's approval, DELETE of a blocker, the public MCP (it goes through PATCH), the native status decision and the decision cards (resolve_blocker, update_issue_status, cancel_issue_tree); the route's cancel keeps the STUDIO-0029 hand-back; every other writer is the backstop's (plugins, the runner's set_dependencies, recovery-action resolve, the watchdog fold, stalled review, interaction confirmation, onboarding move, quarantine restore, tree cancel, status cards, the escalation edge delete, company import). The backstop sees them by reading: recovery/work.ts loads assigned todo, in_progress and in_review issues in the stranded queue and blocked ones in the dependency queue, both call it before their own pass (heartbeat.ts); an empty blocker list reads as ready; only cancelled blockers left go through the hand-back comment; a changed assignee is covered by P4.

Each review defect, with its real-path case: non-assignee's run counted as handed over ("hands the comment to the Dev at the lift even after a non-assignee's run carried it"); cancelled plus open blocker, then the open one done ("hands the dependency back ... remaining blockers are all cancelled"); partial removal and deletion ("partial removal makes a todo/blocked issue ready", "its blocker issue is deleted"); only the last comment of a batch recorded ("holds at the claim gate the CTO comments merged in one queued run"); proof of the engine ("hands the comment over again after a run without a started engine, a run cut after its start, or a router refusal"); no signal ("notes once per series"); fixed wake key ("wakes once for each removal"); old traces ("ignores a hold trace older than the assignee's latest qualified run"); hand-over on every run ("adds nothing to the runs of an issue that was never blocked"); strict cancelled rule ("holds nothing once one unresolved blocker is cancelled"); claim exception moving the base ("marks a run passing the claim gate under an exception as bounded, with its admission as hand-over base"); cut between the hand-back comment and its wake ("wakes again a hand-back comment left without its wake"); two holds at once for the note ("writes one note when several agent comments are held at the same moment"); writers outside the function ("through one backstop pass after a direct service write", "after the runner's set_dependencies write", "wakes again on the next backstop pass when the hand-over run fails before the engine", and the mutant with the backstop removed); every edit of the set ("blocker list is emptied", "replaced by cancelled ones only"); a person's comment dropped by the wake merge ("keeps a person's comment written in the same PATCH as the blocker removal"); native decision and decision cards (five cases); swallowed failures and one failing wake ("still wakes the other dependents when the wake of one fails, and the backstop takes the lost one"); deduplication fooled by a skipped or failed wake ("wakes the hand-back comment again when its earlier wake failed, was skipped or was cancelled, not when it was delivered"); ready wake merged into a queued bounded run ("drops the bounded mode ..."), and into a running one ("still hands the held comment over when the blocker is done while a bounded run of the assignee is running"); agent-scoped trace ("sees a coalesced automatic hold as a trace after the base", "hands the held comment to a new assignee that a service write put on the issue, through the backstop"); issue.reassigned ("takes a case handoff's issue.reassigned activity as a reassignment trace"); unchanged blocker set ("sends no edit wake when a PATCH writes the same blocker set again").

Limits of these proofs: the plugin, set_dependencies and case-handoff cases make the same service writes as those callers, not the callers themselves; the failed, skipped and cancelled wake statuses of the hand-back case are set in the database; the logging of a failed wake is read in the code, not asserted.

Silences the backstop itself could create, and what prevents them: it stops only on a qualified run of the assignee after the trace (a queued wake only suspends it while alive); it cannot loop (doubling wait, 1 h at most, so a ticket whose runs never qualify is late, never silent); a cut between the hand-back comment and its wake, or after the wake, leaves the issue eligible; it does nothing while the assignee is not invocable or over budget, while a recovery action is active, or while scheduling is suppressed, and resumes after (each of these is visible elsewhere).

After the independent review of 19f8caca, by the pilot's final instruction (17 Nov 2026). (1) The blocker: the base accepted a run without the hand-over key, so a recovery run the server inserts with a fresh context became the base and the trace was settled although the comment was never shown. Only a run carrying the key qualifies now. Case: "still hands the comment over after a run inserted with a fresh context succeeded" (the runs that carry the hand-over do not record their engine start and do not qualify; the server's second disposition repair, inserted with a fresh context, succeeds with its engine started; the backstop then wakes and that run carries the comment), and a mutant that restores the old branch, on which this case fails. Limit: the fresh run of this case is the second disposition repair, not provider_quota_recovery. Effect at install, without any extra wake: no run of before carries the key, so no assignee has a base right after the install; the first hand-over of an issue after a hold reads the whole thread (the latest 20 agent comments named), and on an issue its current assignee received by a reassignment (the activity exists, however old) the first admitted run after the install carries those comments with the reassignment text, and so does each run until the first qualified one. Not counted in production. The instruction also asks for "without dependencyBlockedInteraction"; this is not applied: a bounded run that carries the key showed its batch (the hand-back on only cancelled blockers), and excluding it would bring back the backstop loop of the cold review (P1). (2) The burst at install: only holds marked by this change count; the four writers of the hold code mark it (the admission, the claim gate, the retry gate, the stale native replacement cancel), and a repeated automatic hold marks the earlier row. What silence: none, studio.21 held no agent comment. Cases: "counts no unmarked hold of before this change: no backstop wake and no hand-over on a ready issue" (the same rows with the mark are traces) and "marks a scheduled retry the dependency gate refuses, and hands its comment over at the lift"; the mark of the stale native replacement cancel has no case. (3) Holds of any agent since the base count (Dev, then Dev2, then Dev again by writers that log no activity): "hands over to a returning assignee the comment held for another assignee in between". (4) The admission has early returns that write no request (queue.ts:3035-3058) and can throw: the backstop's wait is counted on its own attempt rows, written before the wake: "keeps the backstop's wait when its wake writes no request, or throws". (5) The wait query no longer uses LIKE on the idempotency key; it reads the attempt rows of the issue over 24 h at most (a one-hour window would restart the doubling at the hourly cadence).

Moved to B20 by the pilot: the backstop stopping on a succeeded run without processStartedAt (it happens only when the onSpawn write fails; the issue is then retried hourly, visibly); an edit of the blocker set of an issue that was already ready wakes its assignee once; a hand-back on only cancelled blockers whose wake is lost, on an issue without any hold, is retried only at the next dependency change, as in STUDIO-0029. Validated by the pilot: the doubling wait of the backstop, an issue with an active recovery action or an assignee over budget left alone, the route calling the function only when the blocker set changed.

After the bench of the studio.22 candidate (17 Nov 2026, on a45e7325). The bench found three failures of the candidate alone in paperclip-control-plane-port.test.ts (child_dependency): the parent of a finished child that also blocks it had two wake requests. Cause: the native decision wakes that parent in its own transaction with issue_children_completed (status-decision-committer.ts:2434-2462); the call after commit looked for an existing wake by the issue_blockers_resolved keys, did not see it, and sent a second one. Fix: after a native decision done the function sends no ready wake (readyAlreadyWoken, set by the native caller alone); the transaction wakes the same dependents (listWakeableBlockedDependents). What silence: none more than studio.21; the transaction's wake is admitted by the native wake dispatcher with the hand-over, and the backstop wakes if it is not delivered while a comment is held. Cases, each counting the parent's wake requests for a child that blocks its parent: a native decision done (one, issue_children_completed, and that wake hands the comment over once dispatched); the same with the native wake not delivered (the backstop hands over); a native decision cancelled (one, the hand-back); the route done (one); the update_issue_status and cancel_issue_tree decisions (one each); and the route cancelling the child (one request, held, and the backstop hands the dependency back). That last case shows a silence of before this change, read in fb1ad740's code and not run on it: the route keeps one wake per agent and issue in a request, the parent's issue_children_completed wake takes the slot of the STUDIO-0029 hand-back wake and is held by the dependency gate, so on fb1ad740 the parent's assignee is never woken; with this change the backstop wakes it. The route itself is not changed (left to the next batch).

Note text (17 Nov 2026, after 981e67b6, text only). The note no longer says 'For an answer before, put a question card addressed to <assignee> on your own task.' Reason (read in the worker router by its own chat): when the assignee is a routed role (Dev Unity, Game Tester), the run of the card's addressee is refused by the router with router_ticket_not_assigned_to_agent (registry-service.js:513), before any reservation; that code is in no list of STUDIO-0059, and an addressee that is not the assignee has no recovery: a silence. The advice was therefore wrong for the routed roles; the role sheets carry the right path. The note now reads 'A comment from X waits for <blockers> to resolve before it reaches <assignee>.', with its two markers unchanged. The case 'notes once per series that an agent's comment waits, and the note wakes nobody' checks the exact text and the absence of the sentence. The comment in queue.ts says that the card path is refused when the assignee is routed (comment only). Results on the frozen tree: the file passed twice in a row (58/58, 58/58); on fb1ad740's code that case fails; tsc: no error in a changed file. The other suites were not run again: only a text, a code comment and that case changed since 981e67b6.

patches.retireWhen: Upstream restricts the dependency-blocked comment exception to people.
patches.origin: What: an agent's comment on a dependency-blocked issue does not start the assignee's run (admission and claim gate, one decision, agentCommentHeldByDependencies: only the assignee, only all-agent batches, never while any unresolved blocker is cancelled). A run that passes the claim gate under a dependency exception is marked dependencyBlockedInteraction; a dependency-resolved wake merged into a queued bounded run removes the mark. Handover (readCommentsToHandOver): the BASE of the current assignee on the issue is the time its latest qualified run was given its hand-over. A run qualifies when it succeeded with processStartedAt set and its admission computed a hand-over: it then carries heldDependencyHandoverAt, the admission time of that computation (a bounded run that carries the key computed and showed its batch, so it qualifies too: the hand-back on only cancelled blockers). A run WITHOUT the key never qualifies: a recovery run the server inserts with a fresh context (the immediate recovery after a release, the review participant's, provider_quota_recovery, the second disposition repair) passed no admission and was shown nothing, and so was a run of before this change (the first hand-over of an issue after the install reads the whole thread, the latest 20 named: one repeat per issue and assignee). The base is the admission, not the start, so a comment held after a queued run's admission stays after the base. A hand-over needs a trace since the base: a hold (the admission's skipped issue_dependencies_blocked request, read on requestedAt, updatedAt and finishedAt because a repeated automatic hold only moves updatedAt; or a run cancelled with that errorCode, at its cancellation time) that carries the mark of this change (heldDependencyTrace, HELD_DEPENDENCY_TRACE_KEY in run-dispatch/domain/wake-context.ts), of any agent since the current assignee's base (the issue may have been held for another assignee meanwhile and moved back by a writer that logs no activity; at worst a repeat); or an activity that reassigned the issue to it (issue.updated or issue.reassigned). The run that can act then carries every agent comment since the base, read from 10 s before it (HANDOVER_CLOCK_MARGIN_MS) and without the comments the latest qualified runs already carried (latest 20 named, the rest counted, heldDependencyReason for the packet text). A wake merged into a run that already started changes neither its bounded mark nor its hand-over. Every writer of a dependency hold sets the mark: the admission in the request payload (a repeated automatic hold also marks the earlier row it is merged into, execution-wait.ts), the claim gate, the retry gate and the stale native replacement cancel in the cancelled run's resultJson (run-dispatch/adapters/postgres.ts). The holds of before carry no mark and count for nothing: studio.21 held assignments and automatic wakes, never an agent's comment (it ran it bounded), so they hide nothing to hand over and the install wakes nobody. For a routed run processStartedAt means the command left for the worker machine (the router passes onSpawn through before the engine starts); succeeded is the real proof, and a run that succeeded without processStartedAt (its write is only logged on failure) does not qualify: at worst a repeat. One function, wakeDependentsAfterDependencyChange (dependency-change-wakes.ts), decides the dependents' wakes: ready dependents get issue_blockers_resolved, dependents left with only cancelled blockers are handed back (a system comment, woken again if its wake is missing, skipped, failed or cancelled), and a blocker cancelled outside the route gets the STUDIO-0029 hand-back. Its callers: the issue routes (PATCH blocker done, every blocker-set edit, the comment route's approval, DELETE of a blocker), the native status decision after commit (done and cancelled), and the decision cards after commit (resolve_blocker, update_issue_status, cancel_issue_tree), through the dependencies_changed post-commit action. After a native decision done the function sends no ready wake (readyAlreadyWoken): the decision's own transaction already woke every ready dependent, a dependent that is also the finished child's parent with issue_children_completed, which the ready-state lookup does not know; only the hand-back of the dependents left with cancelled blockers remains. Each dependent's wake is sent on its own: one that fails is logged and does not stop the others. The PATCH route calls the function only when the blocker set really changed. The route's addWakeup merges the comments of two wakes for the same agent and issue instead of dropping the first. The periodic hand-over backstop (recovery/held-comment-handover-backstop.ts) covers every other writer: plugins (setBlockedBy, issues.update), the runner tools (set_dependencies, update_status), recovery-action resolve, the watchdog fold, stalled review, interaction confirmation, onboarding move, quarantine restore, company import, a direct service write. It runs for each assigned open issue in the stranded-assignment and resolved-dependency recovery queues (recovery/work.ts:33, rebuilt every 30 s and on every notifyIssueRecovery): an issue with a hold trace after its assignee's base, ready or waiting only on cancelled blockers, with no live wake or run of the assignee, no active recovery action and an invocable assignee within budget, is woken (after the hand-back comment when only cancelled blockers are left). It stops when a qualified run moves the base past the trace; a run that fails, never reaches the engine, or was inserted without an admission leaves the issue eligible (the backstop waits for it while it is alive, then wakes). Never a loop: the first re-wake comes at the next pass, then the wait between two backstop wakes of one issue doubles (30 s, 1 min, 2 min, up to 1 h), counted from the backstop's own attempt rows since the base (a skipped request with the reason held_comment_handover_backstop_attempt, written before each wake, so the wait holds when the admission returns without writing a request or throws; read over 24 h at most); an issue whose runs never qualify (a router that refuses for hours, a run that succeeds without a recorded process start) is retried at most hourly, forever. Maximum delay for a forgotten writer: one rebuild (30 s) plus the pass; nothing while scheduling is suppressed, a recovery action is active or the assignee is not invocable, and it resumes after. No age bound on the traces; measured cost of one pass for one issue with 10,000 old skipped requests and 5,000 old runs of the assignee: median 4.0 to 5.0 ms, worst 12.6 to 14.4 ms over two runs (embedded PostgreSQL, WSL). issueService.update itself does not call the function (moved to the next batch, B20). A system note per assignee and per series says that a comment waits (signal only, under a lock on the issue). Why: TR-1258 (15 Nov 2026) and five independent reviews. Origin: studio fork only; to re-apply, keep held-dependency-comments.ts, held-dependency-notice.ts, dependency-change-wakes.ts and recovery/held-comment-handover-backstop.ts, their calls in queue.ts (claim gate with the exception marking, admission gate, handover), heartbeat.ts (the backstop in the stranded and dependencies recovery owners), run-preparation.ts (the held-comment window and text, the bounded mode dropped on a ready merge), issues.ts (the dependencies_changed post-commit action and its executor), decisions.ts and status-decision-committer.ts (the action queued after commit), routes/issues.ts (the calls of wakeDependentsAfterDependencyChange and the merge in addWakeup), and the mark of a dependency hold (wake-context.ts, execution-wait.ts, the two cancels in run-dispatch/adapters/postgres.ts); run dependency-blocked-comment-wake.test.ts and heartbeat-dependency-scheduling.test.ts.

patches.title: The Claude adapter's login markers read only the run's own error surface, and a usage limit outranks them: a run that ends on a limit is never sealed as claude_auth_required and never marks the AI account
patches.problem: Production 17 Nov 2026, run 21529e7e of a claude_local role (Dev Unity): the run ended on the weekly limit (resultJson: api_error_status 429, is_error true, subtype success, terminal_reason api_error, result "You've hit your weekly limit · resets 6am"), but its error code was claude_auth_required. The login-prompt pattern (parse.ts, CLAUDE_LOGIN_PROMPT_RE) contains the bare word 'unauthorized' and was tried on every line of stdout; the run's transcript held 'But was: <System.UnauthorizedAccessException>', the output of a Unity test in a tool result. requiresLogin then outranked the quota classifier (execute.ts). The end of the run (run-lifecycle.ts, classifyAndPersistRunLiveness -> connection-intents.ts requestForRunAuthFailure -> ai-connections.ts markAuthenticationFailed) put the grant in needs_reauthorization and the connection in health error: the role stayed in error until its owner signed in again.
patches.reason: Requested by the studio server pilot as a production blocker (17 Nov 2026).
patches.owner: claude-local adapter failure classification (parse.ts) and the run-end auth repair (connection-intents.ts)

upstreamSearch.details: Queries: gh search prs 'claude_auth_required', 'detectClaudeLoginRequired', 'login prompt tool output unauthorized', 'usage limit classified auth required'. Open PRs, none merged nor in the 2026.1110.0 baseline: #13647 'stop scanning the raw transcript for login prompts' (head 306451274e2a28e497d0f497462c675c61b487a7; the login markers read only the result and error events, the non-JSON stdout lines and stderr; its test is the same incident shape, a 429 result with '401 Unauthorized' in a tool result): adapted here. #15660 'ignore agent output when detecting a Claude login prompt' (head 4abe0e389b; the result text counts only for a failed result): idea adopted. #17229 'classify auth from provider evidence' (head cd85182d12; a 401 status is a login failure, the result of a max-turns stop is excluded): both ideas adopted. #11052 'classify failures from the run's error surface, not its whole stdout' (head e6298463bd; the same reduction for the transient and quota haystack): NOT adopted, it changes the class of most failed runs (today a rate_limit_event line makes them transient) and is too wide for a blocker fix. #14089 'gate claude_auth_required on a failed run' (head d1109d24a4): not adopted, outside this case (the server only handles a failed run). The upstream commit message carries a tool attribution line, so the change is re-applied in a studio commit that cites the source and the commit instead of being cherry-picked.

patches.validation: Linux (WSL), Node 24.22.2, embedded PostgreSQL. Real path (server/src/__tests__/claude-login-detection-scope.test.ts, 12 cases, passed twice in a row: 12/12, 12/12): each case runs the real claude_local adapter against a fake CLI, stores the run as the heartbeat stores it (failed, with the adapter's error code and result, on a role whose Anthropic account is connected through a managed runtime), and calls connectionIntentService.requestForRunAuthFailure, which the end of a failed run calls (run-lifecycle.ts, classifyAndPersistRunLiveness). The heartbeat's own execution loop is not driven. (a) Run 21529e7e replayed in shape (a 429 weekly-limit result, 'System.UnauthorizedAccessException' and 'unauthorized' in a tool result and in a model text): error code provider_quota with its family, no repair request, the grant stays active, the connection health is not error, no ai_connection.authentication_failed activity; the same with a login word on stderr; a failed run without a limit whose transcript quotes login words is not claude_auth_required; a run stored as claude_auth_required with a limit in its result (as fb1ad740 stored it) does not mark the account. (b) Each real form of a login request still gives claude_auth_required, a repair request, the grant in needs_reauthorization, health error and one activity: 'Not logged in · Please run /login' as a plain stdout line, the same in the result field, 'Invalid API key · Please run /login' in the result field and on stderr, a 401 status with a refused bearer token (with the api_retry and assistant events the CLI writes), a 401 status alone, an expired OAuth token in the terminal fields, and a cut stream whose assistant event carries the CLI's error field. Unit cases (packages/adapters/claude-local/src/server/parse.test.ts, 73 cases, pass): the same forms, the answer of a successful run and of a max-turns stop not read, the text of an assistant or user message never read, the cut head of a capped capture not read as plain text, the login URL still found in the transcript. (c) Negative control, the same test files on fb1ad740's code: the server file fails in 6 of 12 (the four cases of the defect, and the two forms that are new evidence: a 401 status alone, the cut stream), the six other login forms pass there too; parse.test.ts fails in 9 of 73. (d) Four mutants: both adapter layers removed (the whole-output scan back and no limit-first, the behaviour of fb1ad740) fails case (a) and two more; the whole-output scan alone fails the no-limit transcript case and three unit cases (case (a) still passes there, the limit-first rule protects it); limit-first removed fails the stderr case and one unit case; the server guard removed fails the stored-run case. Neighbours: the adapter package in full, 26 files and 438 cases: 433 pass, 1 skipped, 4 fail in execute.prepared-process.test.ts, and the same 4 fail on fb1ad740's code in this test tree (its shared adapter-utils link lacks two exports; tsc reports the same two errors in execute.ts on the base). Server files on the auth failure, 17 files and 847 cases (agent-environment-test-status, agent-test-environment-routes, ai-auth-failure, ai-connection-router, ai-connections, claude-local-adapter-environment, claude-local-adapter, claude-local-execute, claude-local-skill-sync, connection-intents-service, provider-failure-classification, run-failure-report, run-liveness, satisfied-connection-intents, stranded-notice, agent-setup-connection-intents, ai-connection-configuration-failure): 846 pass, 1 fails in ai-connections.test.ts ('requires sign-in after the receiver process dies with an exchanged but unsaved token'), and the same case fails on fb1ad740's code on this machine. tsc: no error in a changed file (adapter package: the two errors of the base; server: the 310 of the base). In the test tree the server package links the adapter to a shared base tree; the server runs above were made with that link pointed at the tested tree's adapter and put back after. Limits: the CLI's real output forms are those of the adapter's own characterization cases (acp.auth.test.ts, test.probe.test.ts, parse.test.ts), not captured again here; the fields of run 21529e7e are those the pilot read in production (api_error_status 429, is_error true, subtype success, terminal_reason api_error, the result text), the exact value of its api_error field is assumed ('usage_limit_reached'). Silence in the other direction: a login word that the CLI would write ONLY in the text of a message (no result field, no event error field, no plain line, no stderr) is no longer seen; no such real form was found; such a run stays failed and visible, without a repair request.

patches.retireWhen: Pinned upstream scopes the Claude login markers to the run's error surface, lets a usage limit outrank them, and does not read the cut head of a capped capture as plain text (for example #13647 merged with those two additions), confirmed by claude-login-detection-scope.test.ts.
patches.origin: What: detectClaudeLoginRequired (parse.ts) reads the login-prompt markers only on the run's own error surface: the terminal fields of a FAILED result event (result, error, api_error, the errors list; never the result of a success or of a max-turns stop, which is the model's answer), the stdout lines that are not JSON events (a CLI that refuses to start writes 'Not logged in · Please run /login' as plain text), and stderr. It never reads the content of a tool_result nor the text of an assistant or user message. When the stream has no result event (it was cut), the CLI's own event-level error field (authentication_failed on an assistant or system event) is read, never a message. The capture keeps the last 4 MiB of stdout (MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES), so its first line can be the cut tail of an event: when the capture reached the cap, that first line is not read as plain text (a gap of upstream #13647). A terminal result that reports a usage limit (status 429, an api_error of usage or rate limit, or a quota phrase in the terminal fields of a failed result) outranks every login marker: the run is a limit (provider_quota and its usual wait, or a transient retry), never claude_auth_required. A 401 status on a failed terminal result is a login failure. The login URL keeps its broad scope. Server guard (ai-auth-failure.ts runResultReportsProviderLimit, used by connection-intents.ts requestForRunAuthFailure): a failed run whose own result reports a provider limit (status 429, an api_error of limit, errorFamily provider_quota) never marks the account and never asks for a new sign-in, whatever its error code; points 1 and 2 already make claude_auth_required a proof of a refused sign-in, the guard covers a Claude run stored earlier with the wrong code. It does NOT cover Codex as written here: a Codex result carries only stdout, stderr and the error family, which the login class overwrites; STUDIO-0065 adds a structured limit mark for it. Why: production 17 Nov 2026, run 21529e7e (see problem). Not changed here, described for a later change: codex_local has the same defect (codex-local/src/server/parse.ts:162-175 classifyCodexAuthRefreshFailure over buildCodexErrorHaystack, the whole stdout; evaluated before the quota classifier in execute.ts:1568-1603; refresh_token_* codes mark the account), and so have gemini_local (parse.ts:285-299) and kimi_local (parse.ts:228-236). Origin: adapted from paperclipai/paperclip#13647 (commit 306451274e2a28e497d0f497462c675c61b487a7), with ideas of #15660 and #17229; the limit-first rule, the capped-capture guard, the cut-stream rule and the server guard are studio additions. patches.title: The Codex adapter's login-loss and limit classifiers read only the run's own error surface, recognise Codex's own login-loss sentences, and a usage limit outranks a login loss: a failed run whose transcript quotes an auth error never marks the shared OpenAI account, and a real login loss still does
patches.problem: The same defect as STUDIO-0064, found on 17 Nov 2026 by reading the code after the Claude incident. classifyCodexAuthRefreshFailure (codex-local parse.ts) tried its patterns on buildCodexErrorHaystack: the error message, the WHOLE stdout and stderr. The stdout of `codex exec --json` holds the output of every command the agent ran (command_execution) and the model's text (agent_message). The patterns include a contextual one: a word among oauth, refresh, access token, bearer, credential within 80 characters of 401, unauthorized or invalid grant. On a failed run (non-zero exit) a transcript line such as 'HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized ... bearer token' gave refresh_token_invalidated, evaluated BEFORE the usage limit (execute.ts). The refresh_token_* codes are authentication failures (ai-auth-failure.ts), so the end of the run marked the account as needing a new sign-in. Nearly every role of the studio runs on Codex and shares one OpenAI account: one such run would put all of them in error until the owner signs in again. The ACP lane had the same defect: it matched the patterns on the run's summary, the model's last text (acp.ts, withCodexAuthRefreshFailureClassification). Second defect, found by the independent review of the first version of this patch: the baseline's patterns do not recognise the sentences Codex really writes on a login loss (only 'refresh token has expired' matched); on the baseline a real loss was caught only through the trace Codex writes on stderr ('Failed to refresh token status=401 Unauthorized'). Reading stderr no longer once the protocol started, without patterns for the real sentences, would have left a real login loss unseen at every wake.

patches.validation: Linux (WSL), Node 24.22.2, embedded PostgreSQL. Real path (server/src/__tests__/codex-login-detection-scope.test.ts, 32 cases, passed twice in a row: 32/32, 32/32): each case runs the real codex_local adapter (CLI lane) against a fake CLI that writes the Codex JSONL protocol, stores the run as the heartbeat stores it (failed, with the adapter's error code and result, on a role whose OpenAI account is connected through a managed runtime), and calls connectionIntentService.requestForRunAuthFailure, which the end of a failed run calls (run-lifecycle.ts, classifyAndPersistRunLiveness). The heartbeat's own execution loop is not driven. The login-loss sentences and the stderr trace are Codex's own, read in the installed binaries (codex-cli 0.156.1 on the server, 0.166.0 on the worker machines, Linux x64, read only); the order of the events (thread.started, turn.started, the `error` event, turn.failed) is that of the adapter's parser. (a) A usage limit as the last protocol error, with 'HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized ... bearer token' in a command's output and in the model's text: error code provider_quota with its family and the providerLimitObserved mark, no repair request, the grant stays active, the connection health is not error, no ai_connection.authentication_failed activity. A CLI that failed before the protocol and wrote both a limit and a login loss: a limit. (b) A failed run without a limit whose command output quotes the same words: no refresh_token code, the account is not marked. Login words on stderr once the protocol started (an MCP OAuth line, the MCP 'enterprise grant: invalid_grant' line, a refresh-token line, the three ssh client messages), with and without a terminal protocol error: not marked. The ssh client's messages alone, the CLI never started: not marked. An MCP server's OAuth refusal as the last protocol error, on stderr before the protocol, or as a plain stdout line: not marked. An error of an earlier turn followed by a turn that completed, then a non-zero exit: not classified. A result with a login code and the structured limit mark: not marked; the same output without the mark is marked (the guard reads no text). (c) A real login loss still marks the account. Each of Codex's six sentences in the `error` event and turn.failed, with the trace on stderr, gives its code (refresh_token_reused for 'was already used', refresh_token_expired for 'has expired', refresh_token_invalidated for 'was revoked', 'signed in to another account', 'access token could not be refreshed' and 'authentication session could not be refreshed'), a repair request for openai, the grant in needs_reauthorization, health error and one activity. The same six sentences in a turn.failed alone, without the `error` event and with an empty stderr (the stdout the worker router composes for live steering, if it carried Codex's message): the same. The CLI failing before the protocol with the trace on stderr, with a sentence on stdout, or with a sentence on stderr: marked. A wrapper's JSON object that is not a Codex event does not start the protocol: the trace on stderr is still read and the account is marked. A transcript that quotes a usage limit and ends on 'was already used' still marks the account. The seven code forms of the baseline's tests (refresh_token_reused, refresh_token_expired, refresh_token_invalidated and invalid_grant in the protocol error, 'credential refresh returned 401 Unauthorized', stderr and a plain stdout line before the protocol) still mark the account; Codex does not write these codes, the cases are kept as the baseline's forms. (d) Two cases state a limit rather than a protection: the router's fixed turn.failed text ('Interactive provider turn did not complete successfully.', empty stderr) is not a login loss (seen neither on the baseline nor here); a run that died after the protocol started with the trace only on stderr and no protocol error is codex_harness_crash (transient, retried), not marked. Claude side (server/src/__tests__/claude-login-detection-scope.test.ts, 14 cases, twice: 14/14, 14/14), two cases added here: a claude_local run in a real login loss (status 401 in its result) with a usage-limit line on stderr still marks its account, because the guard reads no output; a claude_local run whose result carries providerLimitObserved is still marked, because the mark is honoured for a codex_local run only. Unit cases (codex-local parse.test.ts, 52 cases, and acp.test.ts, 47 cases, pass): each of the six sentences classifies in the protocol error, with and without stderr, and classifies nothing when only a command or the model quotes it; the stderr trace is read only when the protocol never started; 'Failed to refresh token: <cause>' alone and 'ChatGPT login is required, but an API key is currently being used' classify nothing; an MCP line classifies nothing as the protocol's last error, on stderr or as a plain line, and a sentence of Codex next to it still classifies; the errors of an earlier turn are forgotten at turn.started and turn.completed, for the login and the limit classifiers; only an event of the Codex protocol starts the protocol; quoted login errors in a command output or in the model's text classify nothing; a real limit is a limit although the transcript quotes a login failure; a limit, a transient error or a retry time is not read from the transcript; once the protocol started only its last error is read (not stderr, not a plain line, not the fallback message); no ssh client message matches a pattern; the cut head of a capped capture is not read as plain text, whether the capture was cut by characters or by bytes; on the ACP lane the model's last text never classifies a login loss. (e) Negative control, the same test files on fb1ad740's code: the Codex server file fails in 15 of 32. On the baseline five of the six sentences with the stderr trace DO mark the account (through the trace; 'was already used' gets refresh_token_invalidated instead of refresh_token_reused), and five of the six in a turn.failed without stderr do NOT (only 'has expired' matches a baseline pattern): the baseline saw a real login loss through stderr only. parse.test.ts fails in 21 of 52. The Claude server file fails in 7 of 14 (the cases of STUDIO-0064, and the new 401 case with a limit line on stderr, because a 401 alone is not a login loss on the baseline). (f) Twelve mutants, each on the code of the tested tree. Both adapter layers removed (the whole-output scan and the login loss before the limit, the behaviour of fb1ad740): 7 server cases fail, the limit run among them. The whole-output scan alone: 6 server cases and 20 unit cases (the limit run still passes there, the limit-first order protects it). stderr read once the protocol started: 3 server cases and 3 unit cases. The login loss before the limit alone: the case where the CLI wrote both. The server guard's mark removed: the structured-mark case. The ACP lane reading the model's last text again: its unit case. Codex's own sentences not recognised (the patterns of fb1ad740, the defect of the first version): 12 server cases (five sentences in the protocol error, the same five without stderr, the quoted-limit case, the CLI failing before the protocol) and 9 unit cases. The mark honoured for any adapter: the claude_local case. No reset at a new turn: 1 server case and 1 unit case. Any typed JSON object starts the protocol: 1 server case and 1 unit case. The generic patterns tried on MCP lines: 1 server case and 1 unit case. The capture cut compared in characters only: 1 unit case. Neighbours: the codex-local package in full, 31 files and 621 cases: 620 pass, 1 fails in execute.remote.test.ts ('stops the kept bridge when a prepared run is cancelled without a provider stop receipt'), and the same case fails on fb1ad740's code in this test tree (its shared adapter-utils link lacks two exports; tsc reports the same two errors in execute.ts on the base). Server files, 24 files and 941 cases (the 17 files on the auth failure of STUDIO-0064, the five codex-local server files, claude-login-detection-scope and codex-login-detection-scope): 939 pass, 1 skipped, 1 fails in ai-connections.test.ts ('requires sign-in after the receiver process dies with an exchanged but unsaved token'), the same case as on fb1ad740's code on this machine. tsc: no error in a changed file (adapter package: the two errors of the base; server: the 310 of the base). In the test tree the server package links the adapters to a shared base tree; the server runs above were made with the Claude and Codex links pointed at the tested tree and put back after. Limits. The real CLI was not run in a login-loss state: the sentences come from the binaries (0.166.0 Linux x64, the version that runs the roles according to the infra record, and 0.156.1, the npm Codex of the Paperclip server, which serves no role run; not verified: the exact binary of the roles server, the version on QA-C, the macOS binary), the event shapes from the adapter's own parser. The real-path file drives the CLI lane; the ACP lane has a unit case only (the 18 codex_local agents of the studio all use the CLI engine). Silences in the other direction, accepted by the server pilot: (1) only the last protocol error of the current turn counts (as upstream #15832 chose for the last error): a login loss in an `error` event followed by a turn.failed with another error is not classified; (2) a run that died after the protocol started with a login message ONLY on stderr, without a protocol error, becomes codex_harness_crash (transient, retried) instead of a login loss (upstream #15832 keeps that stderr; here stderr is not read then, because an MCP OAuth line or an ssh message there would mark the account every role shares); the next run meets the login loss through the protocol; (3) a login loss written only in the model's text or in a command's output is not seen; no such real form exists in the binaries; (4) with live steering the adapter reads a stdout composed by the worker router: the detection depends on the message the router carries into turn.failed, and router 0.30.x carries a fixed text (correction in the router's next batch). Still exposed: before the protocol starts, a stderr or stdout line that carries a pattern and does not name MCP still marks the account.
