patches.retireWhen: Pinned upstream scopes the Codex login-loss and limit classifiers to the run's error surface in both lanes (CLI and ACP), recognises Codex's own login-loss sentences in the protocol error, lets a usage limit outrank a login loss, and does not read the cut head of a capped capture as plain text (for example #15832 merged with those additions), confirmed by codex-login-detection-scope.test.ts.
patches.origin: What. (1) Error surface: buildCodexErrorHaystack (parse.ts) reads the run's own error surface, through codexStdoutErrorSurface(stdout). Once the protocol started (an event of the Codex protocol was seen: thread.*, turn.*, item.*, error; another JSON object, a wrapper's, is a plain line and does not start it), only the LAST protocol error of the CURRENT turn counts (an `error` event or `turn.failed`; a recovered earlier error does not; turn.started and turn.completed forget the errors before them, so a non-zero exit after a turn that completed does not classify an old error): stderr, the plain stdout lines and the fallback error message built from stderr are not read, because stderr also carries the words of MCP servers, hooks and the ssh client of a routed run ('401 Unauthorized', an OAuth prompt), which are not about the AI account. That choice stays valid because Codex reports a login loss through the protocol too (the `error` event and `turn.failed` carry its sentence). When the protocol never started, the CLI failed before its stream: the error message the caller passes, the plain stdout lines and stderr are its own words and are read. The content of an item is never read: neither the output of a command or a tool, nor the model's text. The capture keeps the tail of stdout (runChildProcess, adapter-utils server-utils.ts:4783, appendWithCap at :4970, the last MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES = 4 MiB in CHARACTERS; appendWithByteCap is used only for the run-log excerpt, heartbeat/run-log.ts:15): when the capture reached the cap, its first line (the cut tail of an event) is not read as plain text; the comparison is made in bytes, which covers both helpers. (2) Codex's own sentences. Read in installed binaries, read only: codex-cli 0.166.0 (Linux x64, read on the worker machine WIN-02, sha256 b8a11fed..., by the worker router's chat) and codex-cli 0.156.1 (the npm Codex of the Paperclip server, installed with studio.21). Which Codex runs the roles (read in the database by the server pilot, read only, 17 Nov 2026): the non-routed Codex roles run on the roles server through ssh environments PK-OVH-<role>, with the command /srv/paperclip-<role>/bin/codex, in Codex 0.166.0 according to the infra record; Feedback Manager runs on QA-C through ssh with the command `codex`, version not read; Game Tester is routed to the worker machines, in 0.166.0. The npm Codex of the Paperclip server (0.156.1 and 0.160.0) serves no role run, except through the ACP lane, which no role uses. The sentences are therefore verified in the version that counts, 0.166.0 Linux x64, and in 0.156.1 too. Not verified: the exact binary of the roles server, the version on QA-C, and the macOS binary. The same texts in both versions read:'Your access token could not be refreshed because your refresh token was already used. Please log out and sign in again.' -> refresh_token_reused; '... because your refresh token has expired. ...' -> refresh_token_expired; '... because your refresh token was revoked. ...', '... because you have since logged out or signed in to another account. Please sign in again.', 'Your access token could not be refreshed. Please log out and sign in again.' and 'Your authentication session could not be refreshed automatically. Please log out and sign in again.' -> refresh_token_invalidated. The specific sentences are tried first. The binaries hold no refresh_token_reused, refresh_token_expired or refresh_token_invalidated code as text: the code patterns of the baseline are kept, and they are no proof of a real form. The stderr trace 'ERROR codex_login::auth::manager: Failed to refresh token status=401 Unauthorized' is read only when the protocol never started. 'Failed to refresh token: <cause>' alone is not a class (the cause can be the network). 'ChatGPT login is required, but an API key is currently being used. Logging out.' is not a class (not a login loss of the account). (3) MCP: in the binaries invalid_grant appears only in MCP OAuth texts ('The MCP authorization server rejected the enterprise grant: invalid_grant'). The generic patterns (invalid_grant, an auth word near 401 or unauthorized) are not tried on a line that names MCP, wherever Codex writes it; Codex's own sentences still are. (4) One surface for the login-loss, usage-limit, transient and retry-time classifiers: the limit now outranks the login loss, so a transcript that quotes 'usage limit' must not be able to hide a real login loss. execute.ts evaluates the usage limit first and the login loss only without a limit, and writes providerLimitObserved: true in the result when it classified a limit. (5) acp.ts (the ACP lane) no longer matches the patterns on result.summary, the model's last text, and leaves a run already classified as provider_quota alone. (6) Server guard (ai-auth-failure.ts, runResultReportsProviderLimit, introduced by STUDIO-0064): it reads structured fields only, never the run's output; a Codex result carries no status, so the guard reads the adapter's providerLimitObserved mark, and honours it for a codex_local run only (connection-intents.ts reads the adapter type of the run's agent). A Codex run stored before this change with a login code and a limit in its output carries no mark and is not caught if it is processed again. codex-local/src/server/index.ts is not changed (the router pins its built file). This patch is stacked on STUDIO-0064: it extends the same guard function, and it corrects the STUDIO-0064 record, which said that its guard covered the other adapters. Why: see problem. Engine in use (read in the database by the server pilot, 17 Nov 2026): the 18 codex_local agents of the studio all run the CLI engine, none the ACP engine. The ACP lane is corrected with a unit case only. Not changed, to look at in B20: 'Not logged in. Please run `codex login`' in a run's output is not a login-loss class on the baseline (no pattern of parse.ts reads it; only the environment test does) and does not become one; a bare 401 without an auth word is not one either. On the ACP lane classifyCodexTerminalSessionFailure (acp.ts) still gives acpx_auth_required for '401 unauthorized' in the title and details of a terminal failure: not changed, no role uses ACP. gemini_local (gemini-local parse.ts:285-299) and kimi_local (kimi-local parse.ts:228-236) have the same whole-output defect; the studio does not use them, they are not changed. Live steering (experimentalLiveSteering). The adapter itself never starts an app-server for a run: without a codexPreparedProcess hook it runs `codex exec --json` whatever the toggle (execute.ts, the prepared-process branch). The hook is supplied by the worker router's wrapper, for routed runs and, through its direct executor, for non-routed agents whose toggle is on. The adapter then receives a stdout COMPOSED by the router in the `codex exec` format (thread.started, turn.started, turn.completed or turn.failed) and an empty stderr. Router 0.30.x composes turn.failed with a fixed text ('Interactive provider turn did not complete successfully.') and ignores the app-server's error notifications: on that path a login loss is seen neither on the baseline nor here (not a regression; a test shows it). The correction belongs to the router (carry the app-server's message into turn.failed); once it does, this patch classifies it (a test with a composed turn.failed that carries Codex's sentence, without stderr). The detection on that path therefore depends on the message the router transmits. The non-routed roles run through ssh too, so with the toggle on they take the router's direct executor and the same composed stdout (read in a local tree of the router at 4f18ca7: runtime.js:254, direct-interactive.js:7-18, interactive.js:104 and :201). What the adapter sees there on a login loss: if the app-server ends the turn as failed, a turn.failed with the fixed text, an empty stderr and exit code 1 (no class, no error code, the account is not marked); if the app-server refuses a request (initialize, thread/start, turn/start) or asks the client for something (an auth request is answered with an error, router_interactive_client_request_unsupported), the hook throws and the adapter classifies nothing at all. The app-server's `error` notification is not handled by the router. The same on the baseline. Origin: adapted from paperclipai/paperclip#15832 (head 10be54bcba); stderr and the plain stdout lines once the protocol started are not read here (upstream keeps stderr after the protocol started); Codex's own sentences, the turn reset, the protocol event types, the MCP lines, the capped-capture guard, the shared surface for the limit classifiers, the limit-first order, the ACP lane and the structured mark for the server guard are studio additions. To re-apply: keep the patterns and codexStdoutErrorSurface and its use in buildCodexErrorHaystack, the MCP filter in classifyCodexAuthRefreshFailure, the order and the providerLimitObserved mark in execute.ts, the two changes in acp.ts, the mark read by runResultReportsProviderLimit for a codex_local run and the adapter type read in connection-intents.ts; run parse.test.ts and acp.test.ts in the adapter package and codex-login-detection-scope.test.ts and claude-login-detection-scope.test.ts in the server package.

patches.title: A hand-over wake is kept while the previous run's process or environment lease still holds the task, and starts the new assignee once it is gone
patches.problem: Production, 17 Nov 2026, TR-1526. At 16:01:15 the Unity developer handed the task to the CTO in review, by a change of assignee alone; its run 84d24f1c was cancelled with issue_reassigned. At 16:01:18 the CTO's issue_assigned wake met getExecutionBlocker: the stopped run's process was still alive (conversation-continuation.ts, getConversationOwnershipBlocker) and its environment lease was released at 16:01:32 only: execution_owner_active, recoveryActionId null. In heartbeat/queue.ts, deferBlockedExecution kept a blocked wake as deferred_issue_execution only for a durable request, a comment, a card context or a native intent; any other wake went to recordExecutionWait, which writes a skipped receipt that nothing reads again. The CTO had no run until a comment 58 minutes later. Measured since 15 Nov (read only, by the server pilot): nine such wakes; four were saved within 16 to 24 s by another wake, three stayed without a run (TR-1188 33 min, TR-1331 30 min, TR-1526 58 min). The role sheets published on 17 Nov make a role return its machine and hand the task over in the same run, so the hand-over nearly always falls while the process stops.

patches.validation: Linux (WSL), Node 24.22.2, embedded PostgreSQL, on the candidate 67a1a97c (studio.22). Real path (server/src/__tests__/handover-wake-while-process-stops.test.ts, 11 cases, passed twice in a row on the final code: 11/11, 11/11). (a) The real path. A run of the Unity developer is started by the heartbeat; its stand-in adapter starts a real child process, reports it as the run's process (onSpawn, with the start time read from the system) and returns only when the run is stopped. The run is cut by heartbeat.cancelRun with the arguments of the issue update route (issue_reassigned, reassignmentStopConfirmed); the child stays alive; the task goes to the CTO in review. getExecutionBlocker says execution_owner_active, recoveryActionId null, 'The previous provider process is still running'. The route's wake of the new assignee, without a comment, returns no run and is kept as deferred_issue_execution with executionWait {reason: execution_recovery, recoveryActionId: null} and the mark ownershipHandoverWake. A sweep starts nothing while the child lives. Once the child is stopped, the stopped run still holds through a reconciliation action (the stand-in adapter returns no stop receipt): the kept wake waits; past ten minutes one system note tells the thread what holds (the action's own next action), once, and nothing starts. When that action is cancelled, a sweep retires the kept copy and the CTO gets exactly one run, whose context carries neither the wait nor the mark; another sweep starts nothing. (b) The same behind a stopped run's process and behind its environment lease (seeded rows, as in STUDIO-0041). (c) A second and a third hand-over wake are counted on the kept one (coalescedCount 2, updatedAt unchanged, no skipped receipt), and one run starts. (d) Bounded exit: with the process still alive, nothing is written when the wake is nine minutes old; at eleven minutes one system note names the waiting assignee, the previous run and its agent, and what holds; the wake stays kept; two more sweeps write no second note and start no run; when the process stops the assignee starts. (e) Another wake of the assignee, with a comment, gets through first after the owner is gone: its run succeeds, the kept copy is cancelled with 'Served by run ...', and no second run starts. (f) The task is handed on again while the owner still holds: keeping the new assignee's wake cancels the former assignee's kept wake at once; the new assignee starts once the owner is gone; the former assignee never runs. (g) The task is handed on again after the owner is gone: the new assignee starts at once, and when its run releases the task the drain cancels the former assignee's kept wake instead of promoting it; the former assignee never runs. (h) Unchanged: a wake of an agent that is not the assignee is still a skipped receipt; so is a wake behind a remote workspace that has not confirmed its stop, and a wake behind a hold that carries a recovery action. Witness, the same test file on the candidate's code (67a1a97c): 8 of 11 fail, the cases (a) to (g); in case (a) the new assignee's wake is written as a skipped receipt and nothing is kept; the three cases (h) pass there. Fourteen mutants, each on the tested code. The keep branch disabled (the behaviour of 67a1a97c): 8 cases fail. No note at all: cases (a) and (d). The note only for the previous owner's own process or lease (the first frozen head, 72c6df40): case (a). The note written at every sweep: cases (a) and (d). The note written as soon as the wake is kept (limit 0): cases (a) and (d). The release drain promoting a kept wake already served: case (e). The release drain promoting the kept wake of a former assignee (the first frozen head): case (g). Admission leaving the former assignee's kept wake in place: case (f). Every hand-over wake kept in its own row: case (c). Counting a wake moves updatedAt: case (c). Any execution_owner_active hold without a recovery action keeps the wake: the remote-workspace case. A wake of an agent that is not the assignee kept: its case. Any hold keeps the wake: the remote-workspace case and the recovery-action case. One mutant does NOT bite, said plainly: removing only the 'no recovery action' half of the condition changes nothing, because the 'next action' half already excludes a hold that carries a recovery action; the half is a redundancy, kept. Neighbours on the final code, all passing: 21 files and 642 cases (heartbeat/queue.test.ts, ownership-hold-readmission, the ten files of modules/wake-queue, heartbeat-undispatched-execution-wait, pause-pre-dispatch-cancellation, issue-queued-comment-queue, conversation-continuation, deferred-execution-wait, run-cancellation, approved-execution-wait, native-runtime/paperclip-control-plane-port, deferred-execution-receipt-work). On the first frozen head (72c6df40) also: dependency-blocked-comment-wake 58 and explicit-native-continuation 415; not replayed on this head. Not counted: heartbeat-process-recovery.test.ts (about 320 cases) did not finish within the 50 minutes of the test runner on this machine, twice; no result. tsc on the server package: 310 errors, the baseline count, none in a changed file. Limits. The issue update route itself (the PATCH) is not driven: the test calls cancelRun and wakeup with the route's arguments, and changes the assignee in the database. The child is a local process, not a provider process on a worker machine. Whether production leaves a reconciliation action open after a reassignment stop was not established from production data: the note now covers that hold, so the wait is visible either way. Not measured: how long the deferred-receipt worker takes in production to re-read a kept wake (30 s at most by its code). Silences in the other direction. Too early: a kept wake starts only when getExecutionBlocker returns nothing (process stopped or its number recycled, process group stopped, lease released and cleaned, no open recovery hold), and ordinary admission reads the same blocker again; no new start path is added. A former assignee: its kept wake is retired by admission or by the drain and is never promoted. Still lost: a wake of an agent that is not the assignee, without a comment or a card, behind the previous owner (a reviewer of an execution stage who is not the assignee, for example); a wake without a comment or a card behind a remote workspace that has not confirmed its stop, or behind a hold with a recovery action (unchanged, as asked). A cost: a kept wake of a system signal is re-admitted with its first reason once the hold is gone; ordinary admission applies its gates again.

patches.retireWhen: Pinned upstream keeps a hand-over wake blocked by the previous run's process or lease and starts the new assignee once it is gone, with a visible bounded exit (for example #18510 or #19835 merged), confirmed by handover-wake-while-process-stops.test.ts.
patches.origin: What. (1) Admission (queue.ts, deferBlockedExecution). When the blocker is execution_owner_active without a recovery action, held by the previous run's own process or environment lease (the two next actions exported by conversation-continuation.ts), and the wake is for the task's current assignee, the wake is no longer written as a skipped receipt: it is kept as deferred_issue_execution with executionWait {reason: execution_recovery, recoveryActionId: null} and the payload mark ownershipHandoverWake. One kept wake per assignee and task: a later one of the same kind is counted on it (coalescedCount), without touching updatedAt, from which the deferred-receipt worker counts its next check. Not kept: a wake of an agent that is not the assignee (the sweep re-admits the assignee's wakes only), and a wake whose key starts with chat-inbound:, stale-addressee-requeue:, task-retry: or chat-completion: (the sweep leaves those to their own path). (2) Who re-evaluates: the sweep of STUDIO-0041, in resumeDeferredExecutionReceipts (queue.ts). It is called by resumeQueuedRuns at each heartbeat pass and by the deferred-receipt worker (heartbeat/deferred-receipt-work.ts), which re-reads every deferred wake that carries an executionWait every 30 s at most. The exact condition: the wake is deferred without a run, its executionWait reason is execution_recovery with a null recoveryActionId, the task is assigned to the wake's agent, has no execution run and no queued or running run, the agent is not paused, and getExecutionBlocker returns nothing. The kept copy is then retired as skipped and re-admitted through ordinary admission, which applies every gate again. (3) Bounded exit (execution-owner-stall-notice.ts). When a hold still keeps the wake waiting ten minutes after it was asked for, the sweep writes one system note in the thread, once per hold (a marker carries the run id and, for a recovery action, its id; under a lock on the issue row). The hold is the previous owner's own process or lease, or, for a kept hand-over wake, any other hold: a stopped run can leave a reconciliation action open, and the wake must not wait behind it in silence (found by the independent review of 72c6df40). The wake stays kept and starts as soon as the hold is gone. The note wakes nobody. (4) Release drain (wake-queue use-cases.ts, runReleaseDrain). A kept hand-over wake carries nothing a run must read. When the run that releases the task is the same agent's, on this task, and succeeded, it served the hand-over: the kept copy is cancelled with that reason instead of being promoted into a second run (four of the nine production cases were served within seconds by another wake). (5) A kept wake of a former assignee (found by the independent review of 72c6df40). If the task is handed on again before the owner lets go, the first assignee's kept wake is no longer re-admitted by the sweep, and the drain, which reads the oldest deferred wake of the task whatever its agent, would promote it at the next release: a former assignee would run on a task that is no longer its own. Two rules retire it: the drain cancels a kept hand-over wake whose agent is not the task's assignee, and admission, when it keeps a wake for the current assignee, cancels the kept hand-over wakes of the other agents on the task. No code was found that cancels earlier deferred wakes on a reassignment (routes/issues.ts was read for it). Why: see problem. Not changed, as asked by the pilot: a hold that carries a recovery action, and the hold by a remote workspace that has not confirmed its stop (the same cause execution_owner_active, another next action). A wake without a comment or a card is still written as a skipped receipt behind those two; nothing was measured there. Still lost: a wake of an agent that is not the assignee, without a comment or a card, behind the previous owner. Noted by the independent review, not changed. The scope is wider than a hand-over: any wake of the current assignee without a comment or a card is kept behind the hold, also behind its own dying run; a later wake of another reason is counted on the first one and its reason is lost. 'Served by' exists for a succeeded run only: if the new assignee's run fails, the kept wake is promoted into another run, which can add to the retry of the failure. Present since STUDIO-0041: a server stop between the retirement of the kept row and its re-admission leaves it skipped without a run; the sweep reads 50 rows at most, sorted by updatedAt, and rows that stay held do not move, so they can hide newer ones. A kept wake whose task turns done or cancelled stays deferred. Tests still missing: the PATCH route, a served run that fails, a task done or cancelled while a wake is kept, a restart during the re-admission, heartbeat-process-recovery.test.ts. To install alone on studio.22: only the server package changes (four source files, no schema change, no migration, no change in packages/db, packages/shared, the adapters or the UI); the router's pinned adapter files are not touched. Origin: the idea of paperclipai/paperclip#18510 (head 4fe6a94b95), adapted to the sweep of STUDIO-0041; the bounded note, the single kept wake per assignee and task, the two release-drain rules and the retirement of a former assignee's kept wake are studio additions. To re-apply: keep the branch of deferBlockedExecution (with its retirement of other agents' kept wakes), isPreviousOwnerHold and its two exported next actions, the note call in the sweep, execution-owner-stall-notice.ts and the two rules in runReleaseDrain; run handover-wake-while-process-stops.test.ts and ownership-hold-readmission.test.ts.

patches.title: A saturated Codex model, or a stream that ends on Codex's own retry announcement, is a transient error and not a provider quota: the role is retried shortly instead of being held for an hour
patches.problem: Production, 18 Nov 2026 (studio.22, 67a1a97c). The Feedback Manager's run of 07:00:00 UTC failed with the text 'Reconnecting... 2/5 (Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.)' and was classified provider_quota. It is Codex's announcement of its next attempt, and the cause it quotes is a saturated model, not an exhausted account: the account had 49 991 credits and its window stood at 85 %. In the Codex adapter (parse.ts) CODEX_PROVIDER_QUOTA_RE listed 'model is at capacity' with the usage limits. A provider_quota failure without a reset time makes the server wait one hour (native-startup-retry.ts, PROVIDER_LIMIT_DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_MS): deferRunForProviderLimit (heartbeat/provider-limit-wait.ts, called from heartbeat.ts before any dispatch) cancelled the role's later runs with provider_limit_wait, shown as 'Pool exhausted' on the task, until 08:23:32 UTC. No account pool exists on this instance.

(a) The line of 18 Nov, 'Reconnecting... 2/5 (Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.)' as the last protocol error with a non-zero exit: codex_transient_upstream, family transient_upstream, no retry time, no providerLimitObserved mark, and the role's next run is not held. (b) A retry announcement that quotes a usage limit, or a broken stream: the same; the announcement is no verdict. (c) Codex gave up on the saturated model (a final error and turn.failed with the capacity sentence): the same. (d) A real usage limit as the final error still gives provider_quota with its mark and holds the role, until its reported reset, or for an hour when it reports none. (e) A successful turn (exit code zero) that carries recovered error lines before its turn.completed, among them an announcement quoting a usage limit: no error code, no family, no error message, no retry time, its summary kept; nothing is held; stored as succeeded it also clears an earlier limit of the role, like any successful run. Three mutants: capacity back in the quota pattern fails case (c) and two unit cases (case (a) still passes there: the announcement rule covers it); the announcement rule removed fails case (b) and one unit case; capacity no longer transient fails case (c) and two unit cases. Neighbours: the codex-local package in full, 31 files and 625 cases: 624 pass, 1 fails in execute.remote.test.ts ('stops the kept bridge when a prepared run is cancelled without a provider stop receipt'), the same case as on fb1ad740 in this test tree. In the test tree the server package links the adapters to a shared base tree; the server runs above were made with the Claude and Codex links pointed at the tested tree and put back after. Limits. The real CLI was not run against a saturated model: the line is the one read in production on 18 Nov, the event shapes are those of the adapter's own parser. The heartbeat's retry of a transient failure (30 s, then 60 s) is read in the code (retries.ts), not driven here. Silences. A hold lifted wrongly: a retry announcement that quotes a real usage limit no longer holds the role at once; the run is retried after 30 s and 60 s, and the retry ends on the provider's final error, which holds the role then: two short runs at most before the hold. A saturated model that stays saturated: the run fails after its two short retries and follows the ordinary path of a failed run, instead of holding every task of the role for an hour. patches.title: The stop proof of a pausing, terminating or cleaned-up agent reads only the columns it uses, instead of every run of the agent as whole rows
patches.problem: Production, 18 Nov 2026 (studio.22, 67a1a97c). Eleven roles were paused at 10:02 UTC. For an agent in pausing (also terminating and cleaning_up), the lifecycle worker (four agents at once, modules/agent-lifecycle/application/worker.ts) calls stopInvocationsForAgents (heartbeat.ts), which read every run of the agent as whole rows, then agentExecutionsHaveStopped (agent-execution-stop.ts), which read them again while the first list was still held; an unproven stop is asked again after 2 s. Whole rows carry result_json, usage_json and context_snapshot. In the database, compressed: Quality Manager 1 568 runs, 864 MB; CTO 864 runs, 378 MB; Infra Manager 650 runs, 158 MB. The server died with 'JavaScript heap out of memory' (heap limit 4 288 MB) at 10:04:04 UTC and then about 55 s after every start; four roles stayed in pausing, so the read was started again at every start.
patches.reason: Requested by the main session during the incident (18 Nov 2026): the defect returns at every pause of a role with a long history, so at every update.

patches.title: The git-sensitive adapter check does not require .git for a project workspace that is remote-managed, with neither a path nor a repository on this host
patches.problem: Production, 19 Nov 2026 (studio.23). The owner created in the interface the first task of the role '* Super Dev Unity' (TR-2019; claude_local, executed through the worker router). Its run 82620092 failed at once: workspace_validation_failed, 'Issue TR-2019 expected a git workspace for claude_local, but ".../projects/<company>/<project>/_default" has no .git metadata.' The task went blocked with an active workspace_validation recovery action. The interface links a new task to the project's primary workspace (projectWorkspaceId); that workspace is remote_managed, with no cwd and no repository. The host still resolves its own managed directory for it (resolveConfiguredOrManagedProjectCwd, workspaces.ts), an empty folder, and assertGitSensitiveAdapterWorkspaceValid requires .git there. Its only exemption was a configured local path without repository (localPathOnlyWorkspace). Tasks created by the operator's tool or by the roles carry no projectWorkspaceId and use a task directory: the check does not expect a project workspace for them. Released by hand: task_directory selection, then Retry.

patches.title: A plugin job run left outstanding by a stopped server process is settled once no live process can still hold it, and its job runs again, instead of blocking the job for ever
patches.problem: Production, 18 Nov 2026 (studio.22 then studio.23). The server died in a loop (STUDIO-0068). Three periodic plugin jobs were left with a run 'running' in plugin_job_runs, started at 10:09:10-11 UTC by processes that died: amynoox.worker-router retry_waiting, theranchers.prompt-memory settle_cards, theranchers.chat-closer sweep. The scheduler skips a job that has a run 'pending', 'queued' or 'running' (refresh and dispatch in plugin-job-scheduler.ts); only unregisterPlugin settles such runs (plugin disabled or unloaded); nothing does at start; and once every job is skipped the scheduler has no deadline and sleeps. After the restart of 11:02:35 no periodic job of these plugins ran: the router settled no dispatch and delivered no card. It took two gestures by hand: the three runs set to cancelled in the database at 11:17:19 (which did not wake the scheduler: its work signal is inside the server process), then a manual trigger of the three jobs through the application at 11:21:16.

patches.title: A person's request (a message or the Board's Retry) on a run that a pause cut over an ssh lease accepts the stop proof the pause itself accepted, in place of the remote termination receipt
patches.problem: Production, 18-19 Nov 2026. A pause cut the runs of a role; each left its hold legacy_execution_requires_reconciliation, settled 'resolved' with replay blocked, and no run of the role started after the resume (see STUDIO-0070, STUDIO-0071). The product's exit, besides the Board's reconciliation, is a person's request, admitted by admitExplicitNativeContinuation (explicit-native-continuation.ts), which asks for a proof that the cut run stopped. For a run over a remote lease that proof is a remote termination receipt on every lease; the built-in ssh environment driver gives none (STUDIO-0043). A person's request on such a run therefore waited 'remote_cleanup' for ever, although the server already held a stop proof of its own: the agent reaches 'paused' only when the pause's stop proof concluded for all its runs (agent-execution-stop.ts, the ssh client rule of STUDIO-0043).

patches.title: A cut of more than an hour no longer blocks the task: the stop series of the worker router is held twelve hours
patches.problem: Production, 19 Nov 2026. After a cut of the link to a worker machine the run ends router_provider_stop_unverified; the next run waits ten minutes for the proof of the stop and ends router_previous_dispatch_unsettled. Both are declared waits (STUDIO-0046, STUDIO-0059): within their bound stranded-work recovery neither requeues nor blocks. That bound was one hour (ADAPTER_DECLARED_STOP_WAIT_MAX_MS). Past it normal recovery took over: it requeued, each requeued run waited ten minutes for nothing (eleven runs in a row on 19 Nov, 630 s each), then the task was blocked with a Board action. A cut longer than an hour therefore blocked the task, and a person had to act after the link was back. The router (its chat, 20 Nov) keeps the dispatch open without limit, tries the proof every two minutes, and when the link is back settles the dispatch and wakes the assignee (worker_router_dispatch_settled); it agrees to twelve hours.

Leading slashes of a route are removed before the path is built and compared with the taken ones. A contribution without `slots`, an empty item of the list or an empty slot is skipped. None of these can come from a manifest the server accepted: it validates a manifest when a plugin is installed (server/src/services/plugin-manifest-validator.ts:122 applies packages/shared/src/validators/plugin.ts, where a slot's `displayName` is required and non-empty (:395) and a `routePath` is one lowercase segment without a slash (:402)), and the route always returns `slots` as a list. The guard is a second line: an error in this function would take the whole left menu down, for everybody. One destination per plugin, the first page and the first menu entry by `order`; destinations of several plugins are sorted by label. A path already used by a built-in page, by one of the three pages above "More", or by another plugin is skipped. The entry carries that link already prefixed, with the prefix of the company on screen (useActiveCompanyPrefix), because the router's own prefixing (applyCompanyPrefix, ui/src/lib/company-routes.ts:79) only knows the host's roots and reads `/machines` as a company named MACHINES; the host builds its Cases links the same way (caseHref). So a pin made in one company and opened in another leads to `/<other company>/<routePath>`, as the built-in pins do, which hold no company either: this is wanted (what the plugin's page shows in a company where it has nothing is the plugin's matter). While the company on screen is not known (a first render, a page outside any company) there is no plugin entry and no plugin pin at all, since its link could only be the bare path that opened 'Organization not found'; the stored pin is kept and both appear as soon as the company is known. Only the plugin's declaration is read here; its code is not loaded by the menu. Where pins are kept: in the browser, per user, in localStorage under `paperclip.coordinator.pinned-nav.v1:<user id>` (hooks/usePinnedNavigation.ts), not in the database; they do not follow the user to another browser. A pin whose destination is not offered (the plugin is not ready, or the contributions list did not load) is not shown and is kept, so it comes back with the plugin. A limit during an install: a browser tab left open while the plugin is uninstalled and installed again keeps the list it read, so its entry (and a pin) can lead to a page the plugin does not serve at that moment, until the tab reads the list again: when its window regains focus (the app's query defaults, ui/src/main.tsx:73-78) or on a reload. Going back to studio.24 gives the old interface back, pins included: its sidebar already ignores a pin it does not know (pins.flatMap in buildPinnedNavigationItems), so a kept `/machines` pin is not shown and breaks nothing. What is built and served: the `ui` package only (its `dist`, served by the server from `server/ui-dist` in a published build, or `ui/dist` in the repository; `index.html` and the hashed files under `assets/`); no server file changes.

patches.title: claude_local and codex_local return the session their engine announced when a run fails without a final result; the summary of a run that did not succeed is posted under a line that says so
patches.problem: Read in the code by the first server code chat and confirmed in the production database by the server pilot (20 Nov 2026). claude_local: a run cut after Claude announced its session in `system`/`init` (the SIGTERM of a pause, a lost ssh link, the run's own timeout) returned no session. Without Claude's final `result` event the adapter took its unparsed path, or its timeout path, and neither returned one. codex_local returned the session of `thread.started` when its engine was killed or its link was lost (the three `codex_harness_crash` runs of the Feedback Manager on 17 and 18 Nov all have a session after the run), but not when the run reached its own timeout. So the first run of a task, or a run started on a fresh session, lost its conversation when it was cut: the next run started from nothing. The owner's rule: at its return the same role resumes its work where it left it, on the same machine.

patches.title: A callback bridge is stopped by the processes of its own launch, and a launch first stops the whole bridge an earlier run kept in its folder
patches.problem: Production, 20 Nov 2026, confirmed in the server's log by the server pilot and in the run logs by the worker router's chat (drafts/routeur-deux-moteurs/pont-paperclip-coupe.md). A routed role lost PAPERCLIP_API_URL (ECONNREFUSED) in the middle of its run, until the end of that run. TR-2030 on MAC-02: run 65663cf0 ended at 03:00:47 with 'Provider stop not proven; keeping the callback bridge until stop proof, run cancellation or 10 min.'; run 0e7e0a7e launched its own bridge in the same folder at 03:10:15; at 03:10:47 the server logged '[paperclip] Stopping a callback bridge kept after an unproven provider stop (max_delay).'; first refused connection read at 03:23:05. TR-2153 on MAC-01: 1cb0a43d kept at 09:17:19, 5282b80d launched its bridge at 09:26:09, the kept bridge stopped at 09:27:19, first refusal at 09:32:55. The mechanism, read in the code. (1) A steered run ends without proof that its engine stopped: execute keeps its bridge and arms deferOrphanedBridgeStop for ten minutes (STUDIO-0039). (2) The runs of one worker-router reservation share their task folder, on purpose (it is what lets a run resume the conversation and the files), and so the bridge folder under it, with its server.pid and ready.json. The next run's launch removed those two files and wrote its own number in server.pid; it did not stop the old bridge (sandbox-callback-bridge.ts, the launch lines of startSandboxCallbackBridgeServer). (3) At the tenth minute the stop() of the FIRST bridge read server.pid at that moment, killed that number, and removed server.pid and ready.json: it killed the bridge of the run at work. The old bridge stayed alive on the machine. A second defect of the same overlap, read in the code and shown by a trial. A bridge has two halves: its server on the machine, and a worker inside the Paperclip server that polls the folder `requests/` of the bridge and relays each request to the API under its own run. Taking a request is not exclusive: there is no rename and no lock, each worker only guards against handling a request twice with a map of its own (sandbox-callback-bridge.ts, inFlightRequestGuards in startSandboxCallbackBridgeWorker), and the request file carries no token (the bridge server checks the token and does not write it). So while a bridge is kept, its worker and the worker of the next run poll the same folder, and one write of the run at work is relayed twice: once under its own run, once under the run that is over. A real case of that second defect, read in the production database by the server pilot (20 Nov 2026). On TR-2160 the same comment of the Game Tester role was written twice, with the same body: at 09:21:48.874 under run 1dcccc7b, and at 09:21:49.212 under run c9ea7cf5. 1dcccc7b is a run of TR-2154 that was cut at 09:13:05 by router_provider_stop_unverified and whose log says its callback bridge is kept; c9ea7cf5 is the next run of TR-2154, from 09:13:39 to 09:22:37. The two runs have the same bridge folder on the machine QA-C (`<task folder>/work/.paperclip-runtime/codex/paperclip-bridge`). c9ea7cf5 ended before the tenth minute of the kept bridge, so it met no refused connection: only the double write shows. Nothing else was written twice in the window of TR-2030.

upstreamSearch.details: Queries (gh search prs): 'callback bridge pid', 'sandbox callback bridge stop', 'server.pid bridge', 'orphaned bridge', 'bridge ECONNREFUSED', 'callback bridge killed', 'bridge stop pid', 'callback bridge stop pid'. Related, read with its diff: #18724 (open, 'make the callback bridge claim its pid file so stop() kills the server', head 4f3f6084, commits d4b3a0e4 and d0a2f380; fixes issue #18096). Its fact: when `node` on the remote path is a version-manager shim (Volta, fnm), the `$!` recorded in server.pid is the shim and the bridge is its child, so killing the recorded number left the bridge running (192 leaked bridges on one host). Its change: stop() kills the number the bridge reported in ready.json, and reads server.pid only when readiness carried none; it still removes server.pid and ready.json without condition, and it does not touch the launch. Taken alone it would end the wrong kill of this defect, by another road, but it would still remove the files of the run at work and leave the old bridge alive; and its fallback still reads server.pid at the stop. Not merged as it is: its rule (the bridge is known by the number of ready.json) is taken up here, with this source, and extended. No pull request makes the stop leave another bridge's files, nor stops a previous bridge of the same folder at a launch.

patches.migration: None: no stored data, no setting. What changes at runtime, in startSandboxCallbackBridgeServer (the bridge of a remote run: an ssh environment, a sandbox in queue mode; the HTTP/2 path has no such process). A bridge is known by the processes of its own launch: the bridge itself, by the number it reported in ready.json (its own process.pid), and the process the launching shell started and recorded in server.pid (`$!`), which is the same process on a plain POSIX shell and another one when `node` is a version-manager shim that runs the real node as its child (upstream #18724). (1) stop() ends those two numbers and no other, whatever server.pid holds by then; it removes server.pid only while that file still holds one of its two numbers, and ready.json only while that file still reads exactly what this bridge wrote at its launch. So the stop of a bridge kept after an unproven provider stop, up to ten minutes after its run, no longer touches the bridge that the next run of the same reservation launched in the same folder, nor its files. (2) A launch first stops the bridge a previous run left in the folder: it reads the number in server.pid and the number in the ready.json it is about to remove, ends each, then removes the two files and starts its own bridge as before. The start reports the number it stopped (stoppedStalePid, 0 when none). This is what ends the old bridge, which stayed alive on the machine before. It is safe on these terms: the previous run is over (its adapter returned; its bridge was only kept in case its engine, whose stop was not proven, called back), and the worker router does not launch two runs on one reservation, so no engine of a run at work is cut; the engine of the finished run, if it is still there, loses its bridge at the next launch instead of at its tenth minute. (3) Neither ends a process that the system shows to be something else: before ending a number, the shell reads that process's whole command line (`ps -ww -p <pid> -o args=`; `-ww` asks for the whole line from a `ps` that would cut it to a width, since the path of a bridge's entrypoint is long. Read on two of the studio's worker Macs by the server pilot, over ssh with no terminal, Darwin 27.0.0 and 24.2.0: their `ps` gives the whole line without the flag, 9298 and 3490 characters, the same as with it. So `-ww` changes nothing there, harms nothing, and is kept for a `ps` that would cut). A number is ended only when the command line holds the entrypoint of this folder's bridge (`<bridge runtime folder>/server/paperclip-bridge-server.mjs`): that path is under the bridge's own folder (execution-target.ts:4442), the same for every run of the folder and proper to it. This holds for a number another run recorded, at a launch, and for a number of the bridge's own, at a stop. A number reused by another program after a restart of the machine is therefore left alone, and so is the bridge of another task folder, of another reservation on the same machine. One more guard at a stop, for a number reused by the NEW bridge of the same folder, whose command line is the same: before ending its numbers the stop reads server.pid and ready.json again, and when ready.json is no longer what this bridge wrote, a number of its own that server.pid or ready.json now names is left, because the folder's files give it to the bridge of the run at work. The register of rule 4 already stops the old bridge before the new one starts whenever the server still knows it; this guard is for when it does not (a restart of the server and of the machine). When the command line cannot be read at all (no `ps`, or one that does not know these options): a launch ends nothing that another run recorded, which leaves the old bridge as before this patch; a stop still ends its own two numbers when they are alive, which is what the code did before this patch for the number of server.pid. That is not a path of production: read in the run logs since 18 Nov 2026 by the server pilot, every bridge runs under Linux or macOS (the roles' server under /srv, WSL on the PCs under /home, the Macs under /Users and /Volumes), none in a Windows path, and the Infra chat read that the PCs' bridges live in WSL, where `ps` exists. A recorded value that is not a number is ignored. The shared task folder is not changed: it is the worker router's choice. Not changed: the ten-minute bound and deferOrphanedBridgeStop; the host-side worker of a bridge; the HTTP/2 bridge; the readiness wait. (4) The whole bridge an earlier run kept in the folder is stopped before the new one starts, its worker in the Paperclip server too (execution-target.ts, startAdapterExecutionTargetPaperclipBridge, queue path). The server keeps in memory the bridges that are still up, by remote machine and bridge folder (livePaperclipBridgesByFolder; the key is the target's identity, which for ssh is host, port, user and remote folder, with the queue folder). A start that finds one there stops it first, both halves, says so in the run log, then starts its own. A bridge's stop now runs once: the end of its run, a deferred stop and the start of a later bridge may each ask for it. The register lives in the server process: after a restart of the server there is no worker left to stop, and the machine half of an old bridge is stopped by rule 2. Two launches one after the other in the same run (the worker router's tools refresh) are not concerned: the first launch's bridge is stopped at the end of its execute, before the second starts, so the second finds neither a bridge in the register nor a server.pid, and a late or repeated stop of the first cannot touch the second, since it names its own numbers. Why rule 2 and rule 4 are safe for a routed run, by the worker router's own account (20 Nov 2026): its register does not let a new run take the reservation until the stop of the previous engine is proven (router_waiting_for_provider_stop, then router_previous_dispatch_unsettled), so when the new bridge starts the old one has no client left. When the next run may start, against the proof of the old engine's stop: the router does not launch the next run of a reservation before the stop of the previous dispatch is proven; until then that run ends as a declared wait (router_previous_dispatch_unsettled or router_provider_stop_unverified). The server kept the bridge for ten minutes because IT had no proof at the end of the cut run; at the next launch the router has it. So the requests the old worker had in hand when it is stopped, without waiting for them, are those of a dead engine. Were that guarantee missing and the old engine still alive, its calls to Paperclip would be cut at once: it would get ECONNREFUSED and its writes would stop. This is wanted: two engines must not write for one ticket. On 20 Nov 2026 the new bridge started while the old one was kept in the three cases read: at 03:10:15 on MAC-02, at 09:26:09 on MAC-01, at 09:13:39 on QA-C. Where the shared folder comes from: a bridge takes the runtime folder its adapter gives it, and `<remote working folder>/.paperclip-runtime/<adapter>` when none is given (execution-target.ts:4436-4441); the steered path gives none and works in the reservation's task folder. A run that is not steered has a bridge folder of its own (seen on the test bench by the server pilot: `.../runs/<run>/claude/paperclip-bridge`), so neither rule meets a previous bridge there. Not covered: a bridge on the HTTP/2 path has no such process and no register entry.

patches.title: An ssh lease that cannot be acquired during an outage is asked for again for 12 h
patches.problem: Two facts of production, one cause: a cut of the link to a machine lasts longer than the server waits. (L11) TR-2093, Infra Manager, 20 Nov 2026. Run fa0c4bc6 started at 03:26:21 and failed at 03:26:38 with setup_failed, 'Failed to acquire lease for environment "PK-OVH-INFRA" (ssh): Command failed: ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 ...' and no stderr line: the lease probe was killed by its own 15 s local timeout. STUDIO-0052 reads a network code only from ssh's exit 255 and four of its diagnostics, so this failure had none; nothing was retried, the stranded-work sweep blocked the issue one second later with a Board action, and a person clicked Retry at 07:04. Even a failure STUDIO-0052 does classify is retried only twice (about 30 s, then 60 s) before the same block. The cuts of the office link are frequent and of unknown length.
patches.reason: Ordered by the server pilot for the studio.25 lot (point L11), 20 Nov 2026, on the owner's words of that day: the instance resumes by itself when a worker machine loses its link, with no gesture of a person.

patches.validation: Linux (WSL), Node 24.22.2, a tree of 19c312cf with this patch. adapter-utils: ssh-connect-failure.test.ts (existing, extended) and ssh-lease-probe.test.ts (new), 42 cases, passed twice in a row (42/42, twice): the diagnostics mapped to a network code and those that are not (a refused key, an unknown host, another exit code, any output on stdout, the launcher losing the command), and the lease probe killed by its own local timeout with nothing on stdout, the TR-2093 shape pinned with its exact text. Witnesses, the changed source files of 19c312cf under these tests: 20 of the 42 adapter-utils cases fail, 14 of the 19 server cases of the first head fail (TR-2093 among them: nothing is retried and the issue is blocked). Witness of the review's correction, retries.ts of 0035512b under the 21 cases: the accepted-plan case fails (the issue stays at work, nobody is told), the 20 others pass. Mutants, one per rule, each applied alone, each fails at least one case: 27 of 27 (ten on the classification in adapter-utils, seventeen on the lane: the exhaustion of an accepted plan not escalated, any provider taken for ssh, the bound at 11 h or 13 h or none, the clock restarted by each run, ended by a cancelled run, never ended, read on other issues or other providers, flat or uncapped delays, the lane charged to the failure budget, the lane off, and the three of the answered question). Neighbours, on 19c312cf and with the patch: retry and completion, 8 files, 453 of 454 on both, the same failure; run dispatch, 8 files, 245 of 254 on both, the same nine failures; the lease refusal of a sandbox provider, 3/3 on both; the declared waits of the worker router (recovery-adapter-declared-wait.test.ts, which this patch no longer touches), 37 of 38 on both, the TR-1318 case already failing on 19c312cf; ssh in adapter-utils, 6 files, 63/63 on both; environments, 4 files: 323 of 325 on the base and 324 of 325 with the patch, heartbeat-workspace-busy.test.ts having cases that do not always pass in this test tree (one fails on both; another failed on the base only in this run, and a third failed once with the patch under load and not again). tsc: server 310 errors on both, adapter-utils 0 on both. Not proven: no real machine was cut off, the outage is played by the test environment driver; the restart of the server during an outage was read in the code, not tried; the line that admits the lane's retry of a person's explicit continuation (retries.ts) cannot be reached on 19c312cf, where that admission refuses it (see the migration).
patches.migration: None. What changes at runtime. (1) adapter-utils, ssh.ts. sshConnectFailureCode, read by every ssh command, also maps the diagnostics of a connection cut before the key exchange or the authentication ended (kex_exchange_identification or ssh_exchange_identification: Connection reset by peer / closed by remote host; 'Connection closed|reset by <host> port <n>') to ECONNRESET, and 'Could not resolve hostname ...: Temporary failure in name resolution' to EAI_AGAIN. For the lease probe only (ensureSshWorkspaceReady, whose command creates the workspace folder and prints its path, safe to run again), sshLeaseProbeFailureCode also reads a probe killed by its own local timeout with nothing on stdout as ETIMEDOUT: the TR-2093 shape. How a network failure is told from another: ssh's exit 255 with an empty stdout and one of the diagnostics above, or the probe killed by the local timeout with an empty stdout. Not network, today's path unchanged: 'Permission denied', 'Host key verification failed', 'Name or service not known', any other exit code, any output on stdout (the machine answered), the launcher losing the command. (2) Server. The run keeps the code environment_provider_unavailable (STUDIO-0052), so every place that already treats that code as 'nothing started, safe to retry' keeps doing so; an ssh outage is told apart by the provider recorded with the failure (resultJson.providerFailure.provider = 'ssh', the environment's driver). The seven places that know the code, and what an ssh outage meets at each: (i) failRunSetup (heartbeat/run-completion.ts, the code of EnvironmentProviderUnavailableError): the run gets the code; (ii) isTransientWorkspacePreparationCode (heartbeat/retries.ts): the failure is retried at all, and the scheduled-retry gate reads it; (iii) isRetryableInteractionContinuationInfrastructureFailure (heartbeat/retries.ts), the interaction lane's own list: no longer on the path of an ssh outage, unchanged for other providers; (iv) interactionOwnsRetry (heartbeat/run-completion.ts): false for an ssh outage, so the outage lane owns the retry of an answered question's continuation; (v) legacyExecutionNeedsReconciliation (legacy-execution-recovery.ts): no reconciliation hold of the Board for a failure before any provider work; (vi) NON_RETRYABLE_CONTINUATION_ERROR_CODES (recovery/service.ts): the sweep starts no generic continuation of its own on top of the lane, and escalates a spent one; (vii) WORKSPACE_SCAN_NOTICES (recovery/stranded-notice.ts): the notice of that code at the escalation. A new code missing from any one of (ii), (v) or (vi) would have retried nothing, or put a Board hold back in the middle of a cut; one test walks an ssh outage through the seven. Such a run takes its own retry lane (reason ssh_lease_outage_wait, wake reason ssh_lease_outage_retry) in place of the two-attempt budget: the lease is asked for again after 30 s, 60 s, 120 s, 240 s, then every 300 s, until 12 h have passed since the END of the first failed run of the outage. The outage is the latest consecutive series of the agent's runs on the issue that all failed on the ssh lease; it is read from the runs, so a run woken by something else in the middle (a comment, a person's Retry) and failing the same way does not restart the clock, cancelled runs and runs that never started are not part of it, and a run that got its lease ends it. The lane never spends the failure budget. While a retry waits, the issue stays at work, held by that retry, and the sweep leaves it alone; when the link returns, the retry that is due acquires the lease and the run starts by itself. The continuation of an answered question takes the lane too and still carries the question (the interaction lane and its two attempts no longer own it). Past 12 h the lane records the exhaustion on the run and queues nothing more; what follows is today's path for a spent budget. For the continuation of an accepted plan, the exhaustion is escalated as the interaction lane escalated it (escalatePlanApprovalResumeFailureNeedsAttention: the issue blocked with a Board action, the card of the plan marked needs_attention); for any other run, the release of the exhausted run blocks the issue at once by the block of stranded work (escalateStrandedAssignedIssue), with its Board action. Both pass by the one place where STUDIO-0083 wakes the direct manager of the role: with that patch installed, the manager is woken past the 12 h, though the issue is not handed to it. Other providers (sandbox plugins) keep the two-attempt budget. One line is not proven: the lane's reason is added to the list of reasons whose retry of a person's explicit continuation may be admitted (retries.ts, beside transient_failure and the storage lane), so that this path loses nothing; on 19c312cf itself that admission refuses such a retry for a lease failure (admitExplicitContinuationRetry), with this lane or the old one, and the issue is blocked at the failure. That defect is outside this patch and was reported for the patch that owns the continuation after a pause (STUDIO-0074). Not in this patch: the bound of the worker router's stop series (point L8 of the lot, ADAPTER_DECLARED_STOP_WAIT_MAX_MS in recovery/adapter-declared-wait.ts). A first form of this patch carried it; it is in STUDIO-0077, and this patch does not touch that file.

patches.title: A new agent no longer receives by default the rights over other agents, over the company's skills and over another agent's checked-out work
patches.problem: A standard agent receives a fixed list of direct grants when it is activated (NEW_STANDARD_AGENT_DEFAULT_GRANT_KEYS, server/src/lib/agent-permissions.ts; written at a direct hire, at the approval of a pending hire and at an invitation: agent-hiring.ts:92 and :163, invite-grants.ts:51). Five keys of that list reach beyond the agent itself: agents:configure and agents:suggest-changes (change another agent's configuration, model, skills, instructions path, name and title, and resume a paused agent), skills:create and skills:suggest-changes (the company's skills, where the company's skill policy refuses by default), tasks:manage_active_checkouts (write over another agent's checked-out task, ask a follow-up on it, settle its recovery action). So every new role of the studio could rewrite any other role and settle any other role's recovery, whatever its place in the organisation.
patches.reason: The owner's decision of 20 Nov 2026, 13:53 UTC, relayed by the server pilot for the studio.25 lot: a new agent does not receive these five rights; the Board gives them case by case.

patches.validation: Linux (WSL), Node 24.22.2, a tree of 19c312cf with this patch. Nothing is doubled: the real routes of agents, issues and permission grants on an Express app, the real authorization service, an embedded PostgreSQL; the roles are created by the API (POST /api/companies/:companyId/agent-hires, by the Board) and a role speaks with the identity of one of its runs. New test file server/src/__tests__/new-agent-default-grants-routes.test.ts, 13 cases, passed twice in a row with the two existing tests that state the list (agent-default-configure-grants.test.ts, aligned, and invite-join-grants.test.ts, unchanged): 34/34, twice. The 13 cases: a role created by the API holds the ten standard rights and none of the five; the authorization service refuses each of the five for lack of a grant (deny_no_grant, deny_missing_grant), not for lack of a consent; such a role cannot change the model of another role (403, the model unchanged), nor its skills (403), nor write its instructions (403); it changes its own model (200, stored) and its own skills (200); it cannot change its own name or title (403: a protected change) nor resume a role the Board paused (403, still paused); it cannot settle the recovery action of a role it does not manage (403, the action still active) and settles that of a role that reports to it (200, by allow_manager_chain, while holding no grant for it); the Board gives agents:configure and tasks:manage_active_checkouts to one role by PATCH /api/agents/:id/permission-grants and that role then changes another role's model and settles its recovery (200), the other role receiving nothing; a role that already holds the five keeps them when another role is hired, and still configures a peer. Witness, agent-permissions.ts of 19c312cf under the new test: 10 of the 13 fail (the three that pass: its own model, its own skills, the role that already holds the five); under the two existing tests as aligned: 3 of 21 fail. Mutants, one per key given back to a new agent, each alone, each fails at least two cases: 5 of 5 (agents:configure: 8 cases; agents:suggest-changes: 7; skills:create: 2; skills:suggest-changes: 2; tasks:manage_active_checkouts: 4). Neighbours, on 19c312cf and with the patch. Hiring and invitations, 16 files: 431 cases pass on the base; with the patch one case failed, 'reconciles an enabled Reflection Coach bundle with skill sync and a disabled routine' of built-in-agents.test.ts, which stated that the root agent holds the two suggest keys: they came from the list every new agent received. That test is aligned in this patch (the root agent keeps agents:configure and skills:create, given by its own path) and its file was replayed: 46/46 on the base and with the patch. agent-identity.test.ts cannot be loaded in the test tree, on the base as with the patch (a package of the CLI is missing there). Authorization, 8 files: 276 of 278 on both, the same two failures. Agent and skill routes, 8 files: 470 of 476 on both, the same five failures, one skipped. Recovery actions and issue ownership, 4 files: 500/500 on both. At the assembly of the lot (the whole server suite on the assembled tree, then its failed files replayed in the calm on the base and with the candidate), 39 cases of server/src/__tests__/connection-management.integration.test.ts ('connection management with production default agents', 90 cases) answered 403 'Missing permission: agents:configure or agents:suggest-changes' with this patch and 2xx on the base: that suite had not been replayed for the patch. Each case was classified by the first request refused, printed by the test itself. 35 name another agent: 32 give access to a tool connection (POST /companies/:id/tools/apps/:id/finish; the audience is the role and another agent in 29, another agent alone in 3), 1 creates a gateway for another agent (POST /companies/:id/tools/gateways), 2 create a chat endpoint assigned to another agent (POST /companies/:id/chat-endpoints). 4 name no other agent: 2 create an AI connection pool (POST /companies/:id/ai-connection-pools), 1 binds a tool profile to a project (POST /companies/:id/tools/profiles/:id/bind), 1 issues a client token for a gateway the role created itself (POST /api/tool-gateway/gateways/{id}/tokens). The rule stands (the pilot's decision after reading production): the 39 cases are about connection policy, not about the default, and now give the key in their fixture, as the Board gives it case by case. With that, the suite passes 90 of 90 with the patch. tsc of the server: 310 errors on both. Not proven: the other routes that ask for the same rights were read, not each tried; the company's skill policy in production was not read; the path that gives two of the keys to the root CEO is not changed and only its existing test was replayed.
patches.migration: None: no stored data is changed, no setting. Existing roles do not change (not retroactive): the grant rows they hold stay, nothing removes them, and the list is read only when an agent is activated. The Board gives these rights case by case (tool tools/agent-grants.mjs of the studio repository, which writes through PATCH /api/agents/:id/permission-grants, routes/agent-permission-grants.ts). What a role created after the install can no longer do unless the Board gives it agents:configure: any management of tools that names another agent (giving another agent access to a tool connection, a gateway or a chat endpoint for another agent), and three gestures of administration of the company's tools that name no other agent: creating an AI connection pool, binding a tool profile to a project, and issuing a client token for a gateway it created itself. It keeps tools:manage_connections and tools:manage_profiles, which those gestures ask for IN ADDITION to agents:configure. In production no role in service did any of them in thirty days (read by the server pilot, 21 Nov 2026: tool use only, no role creates or configures a connection, none writes on another agent, none created a gateway of its own). What a role activated after the install receives: agents:read, tools:manage_connections, tools:manage_profiles, tools:view_audit, audit:view_agent_actions, tools:use, tools:manage_runtime, inbox:manage (its responsible user's inbox only), tasks:assign, tasks:assign_scope (its own subtree). What such a role still does without the five, because it never came from them: change its own configuration, model and skills (allow_self, authorization.ts:2622-2633; the routes PATCH /api/agents/:id and POST /api/agents/:id/skills/sync ask for nothing more on itself, routes/agents.ts:1796); write the content of its own instructions (authorization.ts:2646-2657) and the other files of its own managed folder (routes/agents.ts:5339, STUDIO-0055); read the configuration of the other agents (agents:read); settle a recovery action, ask a follow-up or write on the checked-out task of an agent that reports to it, directly or not (the reporting chain, authorization.ts:2705-2716); a CEO keeps the same over every agent by its role (authorization.ts:2697). What it no longer does: (1) change the configuration, the model or the skills of another agent, or its instructions path and files (authorization.ts:2659-2664; routes/agents.ts:1796 and :2589); (2) the protected changes, which ask for the right over agents even on itself (routes/agents.ts:2539): its own name, role, title and capabilities (:5823, the fields of change-consent-gate.ts:7), its own instructions path, and the resume of a paused agent, itself or another (:2608, used by POST /api/agents/:id/resume and by a PATCH to status idle); (3) settle the recovery action of an agent it does not manage (routes/issues.ts:7278), change the source task of such a recovery (:7341), ask a follow-up on another agent's task, or write over another agent's checked-out task (:5791; the other rules of that route are unchanged). Not changed, and to know: the single root agent of a company whose role is 'ceo' still receives agents:configure and skills:create by another path, each time an agent is created by the direct route and at each reconcile of the built-in agents (built-in-agents.ts:489 and :849-862, routes/agents.ts:5027): a removal of these two from such a CEO does not last. The built-in Reflection Coach keeps its two suggest keys (built-in-agents.ts:491). Human members keep theirs (company-member-roles.ts). A limit about skills: skills:create does not by itself decide who writes the company's skill library. The skill routes treat a missing grant as no refusal (routes/company-skills.ts:251-264) and ask the company's skill policy; while the company has set no policy, every agent may write the library, with or without the key (company-skill-policy.ts:162-164); the key only counts as a fallback when the policy refuses by default (:140-152, :181-185). Closing the library to new roles is a skill policy to set, not this patch.

patches.title: A pause blocks no task of the paused role, by the sweep or by the settlement of a cut run; a routine keeps its task for a paused assignee; a task that waits on the worker router starts alone when the pause lifts
patches.problem: Production, 18-20 Nov 2026. A pause of a role (for an install) made stranded-work recovery block its tasks within seconds, 'the original assignee is not invokable', each with a Board action; after the resume nothing started them again (the worker router no longer serves a blocked task) until a person acted. TR-2030, TR-2031 (Dev Unity): last run router_waiting_for_resources on 19 Nov at 21:17, a declared wait; role paused at 00:51:30 on 20 Nov; blocked at 00:51:32 and 00:51:42; resumed at 01:19:20; Retry by a person at 01:51. TR-2072, TR-2073 (Game Tester): blocked at 00:51:46 and 00:51:47, their Board action still active. TR-1802 (Dev Unity) and TR-1826 (Game Tester), 18 Nov at 13:18:05 and 13:18:08: last run cancelled by the lifecycle's own stop (code cancelled, source control_plane, 'Agent lifecycle stop requested'). Read in reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues: the check of an assignee that cannot be invoked ran before the exemption of declared waits, and the exceptions for a paused assignee covered only a last run cancelled under agent_paused or by an operator, a native passive wait, and a todo task that never ran under a manual hold (upstream #20281). In review, a paused review participant was escalated as unavailable. Second finding, read in the code: the router's wake for a waiting task can be lost to a pause. A plugin's wake (issues.requestWakeup, plugin-host-services.ts) is refused before the queue, and written nowhere, when budgets.getInvocationBlock returns a block: a reached budget, and also a paused company or project. Only a wake refused for the agent's own pause is written (skipped, agent.not_invokable) and replayed when the pause lifts (STUDIO-0028). The router keeps its request and plays it again every two minutes under the same idempotency key (its contract, 20 Nov), except worker_router_dispatch_settled, asked once (corrected in the router's own lot). Additions of 20 Nov 2026. (a) A second path blocked the tasks of a paused role: the settlement of the hold a cut run leaves (settleUnrecoverableExecutions, execution-recovery-resolution.ts, the executionDisposition queue). About a minute after the cut it moved the task to blocked and settled the hold 'blocked' with replay not_authorized, with no exception for a pause. The runs of routed roles reach it because their cancellation is never acknowledged, so their hold is not a conversation hold (conversation-continuation.ts). Production, read by the pilot: TR-1802 and TR-1733 on 18 Nov at 10:03:45 and 10:03:49 (pause from 10:02:22 to 11:31); TR-1814, TR-1802, TR-1827, TR-1815 and TR-1826 at 13:19:05 after the pause of 13:18; TR-2081 and TR-2069 on 20 Nov at 00:52:30. After the resume, the continuation of the cut run (STUDIO-0074) refuses a blocked task: the work did not start again. (b) A routine request for a paused assignee failed and was lost: dispatchRoutineRun (routines.ts) creates the task, asks the assignment wake with rethrowOnError, and on the queue's refusal ('Agent is not invokable in its current state') deletes the task it just created and settles the request failed. Production, 18 Nov at 13:19 and 17:15: five webhook requests of the routine 'PR TheRanchers — remise et retrait QA' (Quality Manager, paused); no task, nothing replayed, the merge of a pull request lost for the QA. (c) A start refused at the resume (wakeDeclaredWaitsAfterPause) wrote nothing.
