patches.validation: Linux (WSL), Node 24.22.2, embedded PostgreSQL, base studio/lot-24d-candidate (19c312cf). Real path (server/src/__tests__/recovery-adapter-declared-wait.test.ts, 22 new cases under 'a declared wait while the assignee is paused'): the real heartbeat service with a registered stand-in adapter that waits, refuses or finishes the task; the sweep is heartbeat.reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues; the router's wake is the plugin host's issues.requestWakeup; the resume is the lifecycle driver's own ready step (createLifecycleDriver(...).onReady) on the agent row. Cases. During the pause: (1) the real case of TR-2030 and TR-2031 replayed for todo and in_progress: two runs ended router_waiting_for_resources, pause, two sweeps (status kept, no new run, no board action, one note), resume: the task starts alone, once, and finishes; (2) the router still has no machine at the resume: one more waiting run in the same series, nothing requeued behind it, still one note, then the router's wake starts the task; (3) a manual pause: the router's wake is refused, written skipped agent.not_invokable, and the task starts with it at the resume; (4) the bound now bounds the note: within it (machine wait 12 h, stop series 1 h) the task gets the note of its series; past it, no note and still no block while the pause lasts; once the pause lifts the normal path takes the task again; (5) a budget hold and a company hold: kept; (6) a terminated agent and one pending approval: blocked as before; an agent in error can be invoked and is held by the existing rule, as before; (7) to (11) no task of a paused role is blocked, whatever its last run (a process lost, an adapter failure, a timeout, the lifecycle's own stop with and without the pause marker: the forms of TR-2072, TR-2073, TR-1802, TR-1826), under a manual, a company and a budget hold: status, runs, board actions and comments all unchanged; (12) once the pause lifts, a task whose last run failed is taken again by the normal path (a recovery run, or its block); (13) a task whose last run the lifecycle's stop cut is not started by the sweep after the resume, and not blocked: at most the product's hold of a cut run appears (legacy_execution_requires_reconciliation); starting it again is the continuation of STUDIO-0074, not this patch; (14) a paused review participant, with or without a run of its own, stays in review; (15) backlog and blocked: untouched. At the resume: (16) the wake lost to a budget pause and to a company pause (the plugin host refuses before the queue, no wake row exists): the resume starts the task once, and a second resume starts nothing more; (17) a wake kept and replayed: one start, not two; (18) a live wake or a queued run of the agent for the task: no start; without them, one start; (19) a wait past its bound, another failure, a blocked, backlog or in-review task: no start at the resume; (20) a start refused at the resume (the company still paused; a new pause landed before the ready step, where the queue refuses with an error): the step does not fail, nothing is lost, the next resume starts the task once. The router's replay: (21) and (22) for worker_router_group_ready and worker_router_dispatch_settled, under a manual, a budget and a company pause: the wake is refused twice during the pause under one idempotency key; once the role can run again, with no ready step at all (a server stop at the resume), the same key starts a real run; this already held on the base and needed no change. Results on the final head: the 22 cases pass, in both runs of the whole file. Witness, with the four source files of 19c312cf: 16 of the 22 cases fail, the real case first ('blocked' where 'todo' is expected). Fifteen mutants, one per rule, each fails at least one case: the bound of the note ignored; any assignee that cannot be invoked instead of a paused one; no note; a manual hold only; any last run noted as a wait; only a declared wait kept from the block (the rule before L7); the task not skipped; a paused review participant escalated, without and with a terminal run of its own; no call at the ready step; the bound ignored at the resume; a live wake ignored; a live run ignored; tasks not at work started too; a refused start failing the ready step. Neighbours, 16 files, 443 cases, all pass after three existing expectations were changed (see origin): pause-missed-wakes, paused-addressee-card, heartbeat-paused-assignee-new-task, heartbeat-held-comment-wake, issue-recovery-actions, issue-tree-pause-resume-run, heartbeat-refused-assignment-wake, pause-pre-dispatch-cancellation, pause-stop-proof-memory, agent-conversation-delivery, legacy-continuation-authority, companies-service, services/pause-stopped-continuation, and the agent-lifecycle module's lifecycle, driver-scope and resource-wait-stop (recovery-deadline-acceptance skips itself in this tree). Before the change of those expectations, three cases failed: the two of issue-recovery-actions and the one of heartbeat-paused-assignee-new-task named in origin. tsc: the 310 errors of the base, none in a changed file. Whole file: 59 of 60 pass, twice; the one failure is an existing case of STUDIO-0059, 'keeps an in-review issue in review when the router refuses its participant as ended, then closed (TR-1318)', which fails the same way on 19c312cf with its own sources and test file (37 of 38 pass): for an in-review task with no review participant, the refused run is followed by the product's review-path repair wake (issue_review_path_lost), refused in turn, and the task is blocked with a board action 'No follow-up scheduled'. Not caused by this patch and not changed by it; reported to the pilot. Limits: not run against the real router nor a real machine; the pause, the holds and the company's status are written by the test on the rows, and the ready step is called directly (the lifecycle worker is not run); heartbeat-process-recovery.test.ts does not finish in this test tree: its one changed case (an owner pending approval in place of a paused owner) was not run here. While a pause lasts nothing is said on a task of the paused role beyond the note of a declared wait: the pause itself is the signal, on the role. At the resume every waiting task at work of the role gets one run, even when the router's wake was kept: if no machine is free the router refuses it before any reservation and the wait goes on in the same series. A task in review is not started at the resume; it keeps today's path (the router's wake, or the bound). The start at the resume is given by the lifecycle driver's ready step, which the worker runs once after readiness is committed (agent-lifecycle/application/worker.ts): a server stop between that commit and the step skips the start at that resume, as it skips the replay of STUDIO-0028; the task is then neither lost nor blocked: the router's replayed wake starts it (every two minutes for worker_router_group_ready), or the next resume, or the bound. A run that the pause itself cut (cancelled by the pause route or by the lifecycle's stop) is not started again by this patch: that is STUDIO-0074, which continues it when a person resumed the role and, for the lifecycle's own stop reason, only when the run carries the pause marker. A plugin's wake refused for a budget or a paused company is still written nowhere: the start at the resume replaces it for a waiting task of the paused role only; a project-level budget stop that does not pause the role has no resume, and the task then waits for the router's replay or the bound, as before. Additions of 20 Nov 2026 (third head). The settlement: server/src/services/pause-cut-run-settlement.test.ts, 9 cases on the real function settleUnrecoverableExecutions with the forms production recorded (the pause route: agent_paused without the pause marker; the lifecycle's own stop with the marker, the form of TR-1802; a budget's stop): during a pause of five minutes, three settlement passes leave the task at work, its hold active and write no settlement entry, under a manual, a company and a budget hold; after the pause a person's Retry (requestTaskRetry, then heartbeat.resumeTaskRetry) continues the cut run and nothing is left to block; a person's message kept until the stop is proven keeps the task from the block; with nobody asking the settlement takes today's path (task blocked, hold settled 'blocked', the settlement entry written); a run that no pause cut is settled as before even while its role is paused; and the lifecycle's stop writes the pause marker on the run it cuts (through the real lifecycle driver). The routine: server/src/__tests__/routine-paused-assignee.test.ts, 5 cases with the routine service on the real heartbeat service, a webhook trigger fired as a delivery fires it, and the lifecycle driver's own ready step: a webhook received during a person's pause leaves its request issue_created and its task todo, the refused wake is written for a task that exists, and the resume starts the task once; during a budget pause and a company pause the task is kept, the sweep neither starts nor blocks it while the pause lasts, and starts it once the role can run; two webhooks of one pause get one task each and both start at the resume; an assignee that is terminated or pending approval keeps today's failure; a wake refused for another reason than a pause keeps today's failure and the task is removed. The sweep: recovery-adapter-declared-wait.test.ts has 23 cases under 'a declared wait while the assignee is paused', with one more case, one role with three tasks through a pause of three hours (last run succeeded, failed, cut by the lifecycle's stop): none is blocked, and at its end the failed one is taken again by the normal path; the case of a start refused at the resume now reads the server's log (the task, the waiting run, the reason). Results on the final head: the three files, whole, give 74 of 75; the one failure is the existing case of STUDIO-0059 (TR-1318), red on 19c312cf too. Witness with the six source files of 19c312cf: 7 of the 9 settlement cases fail (the task is blocked during the pause), 3 of the 5 routine cases fail (the request fails, no task), 17 of the 23 sweep cases fail. Seven more mutants, each fails: the settlement blocking during the pause; a person's waiting request not keeping the task from the block; every cancelled run left aside instead of a run a pause cut; a routine keeping its task whatever refused the wake; a routine failing for a paused assignee; no log line; a refused start failing the ready step. The fifteen mutants of the second head were run on that head and their code is unchanged, except the catch, covered by the last two. Neighbours: 22 files, 757 cases in one grouped run: 744 pass. The 13 others are not caused by this patch: one case of pause-missed-wakes exceeded its 15 s limit in the grouped run and the file passes alone (11 of 11); 12 cases of execution-control-work fail when they register their work in this test tree, and fail the same way with the six source files of 19c312cf. The files: pause-missed-wakes, paused-addressee-card, heartbeat-paused-assignee-new-task, heartbeat-held-comment-wake, issue-recovery-actions, issue-tree-pause-resume-run, heartbeat-refused-assignment-wake, pause-pre-dispatch-cancellation, pause-stop-proof-memory, agent-conversation-delivery, legacy-continuation-authority, companies-service, routines-service, routines-e2e, routines-routes, execution-control-work, agent-conversations, task-retry, pause-stopped-continuation, and the agent-lifecycle module's lifecycle, driver-scope and resource-wait-stop. tsc: the 310 errors of the base, none in a changed file. Read, with no change: the lifecycle's stop of a pause always writes the pause marker on the runs it cuts, before it cuts them (agent-lifecycle-driver.ts, the pausing step: the marker is written on every run still cancellable, then the stop is issued; a retried step writes it again); only a run created between those two statements could miss it. A case through the real lifecycle driver pins it. Limits added. After the pause the settlement takes today's path again unless a person's request to continue waits for the task; between the moment the role becomes ready and the moment the resume files its request there is a window of milliseconds in which a settlement pass could still block the task. A hold left active during a pause is visible on the task as its recovery action; if the role stays paused, it stays. For a routine, each request received during the pause gets its own task: the routine's concurrency rule looks at a live execution, and a paused role has none; all of them start when the pause lifts. The combination with STUDIO-0074 (the resume files the request by itself) was checked on a local merge of the two branches, not pushed: with both on one tree, a role paused through the real lifecycle whose cut run still has its active hold is left alone by three settlement passes, and the resume then continues the cut run by itself (two cases, the pause route's form and the lifecycle's form; the 39 cases of pause-resume-continuation.test.ts pass on that tree); with the settlement file of 19c312cf on the same tree those two cases fail (task blocked, hold settled). In onReady both calls are kept, the start of the waiting tasks first, the continuation of the cut runs last. Fourth head (21 Nov 2026), two existing cases found red at assembly. Both pass on the base and failed on this patch alone; in both the role of the case IS paused, so what they pinned is the product's rule this patch replaces (a pause blocked the tasks of the paused role). No code changed; the two expectations are aligned. (1) case-handoffs.test.ts, 'retains ordinary sweep recovery after a terminal-intent source crashes before task completion': with its owner paused the sweep no longer blocks the task (escalated 0, skipped 1, the task stays in_progress); the same case by the locked escalation still blocks, unchanged. (2) live-recovery-work.test.ts, 'revalidates parked native session work on ordinary agent eligibility': during the pause of the agent its task is not blocked (asserted now); after the resume the parked work is settled as it is after a released hold (terminal_failure, then the task is blocked), where the product left it parked (retryable_failure) behind the block made during the pause. Both files: 140/140. They were not among the neighbours run for the earlier heads. This makes six existing expectations changed by this patch (four named above, these two).

patches.retireWhen: Pinned upstream leaves the tasks of a paused assignee out of the 'assignee not invokable' block for every hold and every last run, and starts a task that waits on an adapter-declared wait (or replays its owner's wake) when the pause lifts, confirmed by the cases 'a declared wait while the assignee is paused' of recovery-adapter-declared-wait.test.ts.
patches.origin: What. (1) recovery/service.ts, reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues: while the assignee has status paused (any hold: manual, company, budget), a task at work (todo, in_progress) is skipped before the block of an assignee that cannot be invoked, whatever its last run; if that last run is a declared wait still within its bound, the note of the series is posted first (ensureRouterNote), as the existing gate does for an invokable assignee. One reading, liveAdapterDeclaredWaitDeadline, serves both places; the bounds are unchanged and now bound the note only while the pause lasts. In review, a paused review participant is no longer escalated as unavailable (both places of the review branch): the task stays in review until the pause lifts. A terminated agent or one pending approval is not paused and is blocked as before; an agent in error can be invoked and was already held. Once the pause lifts the normal path takes the task again: a failed last run gets its recovery run or its block, as before. (2) recovery/service.ts, wakeDeclaredWaitsAfterPause, called by the lifecycle driver's ready step (agent-lifecycle-driver.ts, onReady) after the replay of STUDIO-0028: each task at work of the agent whose latest started run is a declared wait within its bound is started once (wake reason issue_declared_wait_pause_lifted, idempotency key naming the waiting run), unless a wake (queued, deferred_issue_execution, claimed) or a run (queued, running) of the agent is already live for the task. A start refused at that moment is caught: the task is still a wait within its bound, the next resume starts it, the router's own wake starts it, and past the bound the normal path applies. Why: see problem. Not changed: the list of declared waits and their bounds; the refusal of a plugin's wake before the queue (plugin-host-services.ts); the replay of STUDIO-0028; the product's existing exceptions for a paused assignee (kept above the new rule); a status the sweep never served (backlog, blocked, done). Four existing expectations changed, because they stated the rule this patch reverses (a paused assignee's task is blocked): (a) upstream, heartbeat-paused-assignee-new-task.test.ts, 'still escalates a new task whose assignee is paused by something other than a person' (the limit upstream #20281 kept on purpose): the task now waits under a budget hold too, and starts on resume; (b) upstream, issue-recovery-actions.test.ts, 'escalates an unchanged paused-assignee snapshot and publishes its committed notice': the assignee is now pending approval; (c) STUDIO-0062, issue-recovery-actions.test.ts, 'records the legacy cancellation receipt when stranded recovery blocks a task under the hold of its cut run' (TR-1168): the block of that case can no longer come from a paused assignee, so the assignee is now pending approval and the receipt is unchanged; (d) upstream, heartbeat-process-recovery.test.ts, 'routes a non-invokable source owner to recovery without reassigning the source': an owner pending approval in place of a paused owner. Origin: studio change; no upstream source. To re-apply: keep agentPaused and the skip before the STUDIO-0051 block, the shared reading, and the two paused exemptions of the review branch (search STUDIO-0076 in recovery/service.ts), the function wakeDeclaredWaitsAfterPause and its export through heartbeat.ts, and its call in onReady; run recovery-adapter-declared-wait.test.ts and pause-missed-wakes.test.ts in the server package. Additions of 20 Nov 2026: execution-recovery-resolution.ts, settleUnrecoverableExecutions: for a run a pause cut (isGovernancePauseStop), nothing is settled while its role has status paused, nor afterwards while a person's request (deferred_issue_execution, requested by a user) waits for the task; routines.ts, dispatchRoutineRun: around the assignment wake only, a refusal for an assignee whose status is paused keeps the task and lets the request end issue_created; recovery/service.ts, wakeDeclaredWaitsAfterPause: a start that is refused, or not queued, is logged with its task and waiting run. To re-apply: search STUDIO-0076 in those three files; run pause-cut-run-settlement.test.ts and routine-paused-assignee.test.ts.

patches.title: When an agent resumes after a pause, the runs that pause cut continue by themselves, through the Retry of the person who asked to resume, with activity entries on each task
patches.problem: Production, 18-20 Nov 2026. A manual pause cut the runs of a role; each left its hold legacy_execution_requires_reconciliation, settled 'resolved' with replay blocked, and after the resume no run of the role started until a person asked again on every task (a message, the Board's Retry, or the studio's reconciliation tool). The product continues by itself only the work a budget pause cut (budget-resume-continuation.ts: the Retry of the board member who raised the budget) and leaves a manual pause out on purpose ('A manual pause never does').
patches.reason: Decided by the owner on 20 Nov 2026 ('Oui' to the automatic continuation after a pause, option C; studio journal V658), inside five bounds: the cut runs continue with no gesture; with the stop proof of STUDIO-0073; never a task that waits for a person or a blocker; no double start; a readable record on the task for each continuation and each refusal.

patches.validation: Third head, after two independent reviews (20 Nov 2026); this text replaces the earlier heads'. Linux (WSL), Node 24.22.2, embedded PostgreSQL, on studio/lot-24d-candidate (19c312cf, studio.24 in service). Real path (server/src/services/pause-resume-continuation.test.ts, 30 cases, passed twice on the final content: 30/30, 30/30): each case pauses the agent through the real lifecycle (pauseAgent, the store, the worker, the real driver), writes the cut run as production recorded it on 19 Nov (run 5f24df87: legacy, cancelled agent_paused, the pause's cancellation record and pauseStop marker, a recorded process that is gone, one released lease, its hold settled with replay blocked, a claude_local agent), then resumes the agent through the same lifecycle (resumeAgent with the requester, the worker, the transition to ready and the driver's onReady). No case writes an agent.resumed activity entry. Continues by itself (5 cases; request_filed then continued on the task, both naming the requester and the sign-in source): the run of production with its local lease; the same run over an ssh lease, on the stop proof of STUDIO-0073; a resume with a board key of an instance admin; three cut tasks in one resume; once only, when onReady is called again and after a whole new pause and resume. Files the request and keeps it (8 cases): a stop not proven: kept stop_not_proven, and when the delay has passed the deferred-receipt pass starts it and the continued entry is written at that start; a new pause before the proof: the new pause itself waits for the proof, then cancels the kept request, and its resume files it again (replacesRetryRequestId); a kept request overtaken by a person's message: exactly one run; a pending decision card: kept waiting_for_person, and a second onReady for the same ready state does not take its own kept request for a person's; a kept request whose task its owner then blocks: nothing starts while it is blocked, one kept task_blocked entry after two passes, and it starts once the task is reopened; a kept request whose task then gets a blocker: kept blocked_by_dependency; a kept request a person cancelled while a new pause was starting: the resume does not file it again; a request a pause cancelled: looked at by that pause's resume only (nobody asked: one not_continued; a third pause resumed by a person files nothing). Files nothing and says why (11 cases, one not_continued entry each): a blocked task (a second onReady writes no second entry); an unresolved blocker; a person's message kept during the pause (already_requested_by_person, and exactly one run); a task nothing holds, reconciled or cut before its run started (not_held); a resume no person asked for; the company's resume after a person resumed the agent in an earlier pause; a company pause that lands while the agent is resuming; the reviewer's sequence (holds manual and company_paused, a person resumes and the agent stays paused, someone pauses again on purpose, the company resumes, an agent's resume lifts the last hold: resumed_without_a_person); a resume that names nobody while the company still holds the agent, a hold the company's policy adds (archive), and a resume that names nobody and itself lifts the last hold: each drops the person on record; a board key whose person may not change the task (kept retry_authority_denied by the product's own check); a sign-in source the Retry does not accept, mcp_oauth (resume_source_not_allowed). Does not look at (5 cases): a run a budget pause cut; a run not cut by a pause; a run cut before the pause that is lifted; a ready state that follows no pause; a task on which the agent ran since, a task handed over, a closed task. A record that cannot be written (1 case): no request is filed and the call fails with the number of tasks. Witness, the same file with agent-lifecycle-driver.ts of 19c312cf: 24 cases fail, the 5 'does not look at' and the record-failure case pass. Twenty-nine mutants, each fails at least one case of its own: the hold not required; a blocked task continued; the blocker not read; a person's waiting request not read; the budget cut not excluded; no memory within a ready state; no person required; the sign-in source not checked; 'continued' reported without a started run; any cancelled run taken as cut by a pause; the cut run taken although the agent ran since; a task handed over still looked at; a closed task still looked at; runs cut before the lifted pause looked at; the request filed although its record fails; a failure passing in silence; a cancelled request not filed again; the entries without the sign-in source; the start not recorded where the run is created; a new pause that keeps the person; a pause on a paused agent that keeps the person; a resume naming nobody that keeps the person; an added hold that keeps the person; a resume naming nobody that inherits the person; a kept request starting a blocked task; a kept request starting a task with a blocker; a request a person cancelled filed again; a request an earlier pause cancelled looked at by every later resume; the same wait recorded at every pass. Twenty-three of them were run before three cases were sharpened (code unchanged since); the six that those cases concern were run on the final content. Neighbours, 17 files, 471 cases: agent-cross-tenant-authz-routes, pause-missed-wakes, pause-stopped-continuation, task-retry, budget-resume-continuation, agent-budget-hold-activity, pause-pre-dispatch-cancellation, heartbeat/run-control (8 files, 257 cases) and the nine files of the lifecycle module's tests (214 cases): 470 pass; one case of pause-missed-wakes ('delivers the replayed card wake through the real queue...') timed out once at 15 s in the long run and passes alone (11/11 for its file): load of the test machine, not counted. tsc on the server package: the 310 errors of the base, none in a changed file. Checked and stated. requestTaskRetry called with the caller's transaction: admitTaskRetry (task-retry.ts:264-265) calls writeExecutionControl(input.db, ...), which calls db.transaction on that object (execution-control-notifications.ts:35): on a transaction this opens a nested one, a savepoint of the caller's transaction, so the request and its request_filed entry commit or roll back together; the case 'a record that cannot be written' shows no request row after the failure, and the mutant that lets the record fail leaves one. The transactions at task-retry.ts:489 and :527 belong to reconcileTaskChatRetryReceipts, a chat path this does not call. reportFailure (agent-lifecycle.ts:75-78) writes one warning line, 'Agent lifecycle operation failed', with the stage ('ready'), the agent, the operation and a failure code ('unclassified' here), not the error's message; the worker then drops the error (worker.ts:80). The detail is in this file's own error-level line per task. Limits. Not driven: the HTTP resume route against a real database (its test checks the command the route sends, on a stand-in service), a real cut of a running run by the pause, a real ssh environment; the bench point covers them. Needs a person: only the resume route called by a signed-in person or with a person's board key names one (a board key counts as its person, decided by the server's pilot; every entry says the sign-in source); a resume by an agent, a plugin, the company's resume or the release of a budget hold names nobody. A pause, a resume, then a new pause before the agent is ready, and likewise a company pause or archive on an agent that is already paused and still has an active run: the pause's start is set to now (postgres.ts, pausedAt), and the runs the first pause cut are no longer looked at nor recorded. An error in onReady is dropped by the lifecycle worker and never replayed: nothing is on the task; a server stop between readiness and the hook does the same. A record that cannot be written leaves only a log line (for a filing, nothing is filed; for the continued entry, the run has started and the request_filed entry remains). A kept request has no time limit. A refusal is final until a person's request. A request a pause cancelled is filed again only by that pause's resume, and only if a person asked for it. A run the pause cut before it started leaves no hold: recorded not_held and left to the task's ordinary wakes; that they start it was not verified. When a new pause cancels a kept request nothing is recorded at that moment. The check that a kept request does not start a blocked task reads the task just before the run is queued, not under the dispatch lock: a task blocked in that instant would start. Which engine session the continuation resumes when the cut run had opened a new one is not settled here: it is the subject of the patch that keeps the session of a cut run. Runs beyond the 500 latest cancelled runs of the agent since the pause are not looked at. Silences. Work replayed although finished or taken over: the Retry is accepted only while the cut run is the agent's latest run on the task and is retired by a newer run; the hold must still hold; a person's waiting request wins. A run restarted while the old engine still runs: the stop proof of a person's request is required, unchanged. A continuation in the wrong person's name: the person is saved by the resume command in its own transaction; a later pause, an added hold or a resume that names nobody drops it. A start against the owner's will: a blocked task, a task with a blocker and a request a person cancelled do not start. A request filed without a record: both commit together. A budget cut treated twice: left to budget-resume-continuation.ts. Not seen any more: a second identical entry (same cut run, same reason) is not written; the agent.resumed entry is unchanged. Fourth head, after the third review (20 Nov 2026): one line. In the branch where the state does not change, a person's resume was recorded only while the agent was 'pausing' or 'paused', yet any resume dropped the person on record: a person who resumed again while the agent was already 'resuming' (a second click, or a second person just after the first) erased the requester and recorded none, and the cut runs were then refused resumed_without_a_person. 'resuming' is added to the states in which a person's resume is recorded (postgres.ts). One more case: the resume is committed, the agent is resuming, the same person resumes again, the agent becomes ready: the request is filed in that person's name and the run continues. The file now has 31 cases, passed twice on the final content (31/31, 31/31). The mutant that removes 'resuming' fails that case (the requester is gone after the second resume). The nine files of the lifecycle module's tests pass again (214 cases). tsc: the 310 errors of the base, none in a changed file. The other neighbours and the twenty-nine earlier mutants were not run again: the change is this one line. Limits added, stated by the review and not corrected here. A request whose dispatch ended 'skipped' or 'failed' is not filed again (its retry_not_started entry is written). The 'kept' entry can be written twice when two passes run at the same moment: the check and the write are not one statement. A later resume that meets the same refusal writes no new entry: the first one stands. The reset of the pause's start (see above) also hides the requests cancelled before it. A stop between readiness and the continuation step is not caught up: the task stays held, and visible (executionHold). Two facts asked by the review. The periodic re-dispatch of kept requests: the deferred-receipt work (heartbeat/deferred-receipt-work.ts) rebuilds its list every 30 s and on work signals, and a request that carries a wait is due 30 s after its last update; each check goes through resumeDeferredExecutionReceipts and resumeExecutionWaitComments (run-control.ts), which stamps the request and dispatches it: a kept request is tried again about every 30 s for as long as it is kept, with no upper bound. The ready step after a server restart: not replayed. onReady is called only in the process that made the transition, right after it (worker.ts); after a restart the worker's sweep takes only agents whose state is pending work (preparing, verifying, pausing, resuming, terminating, cleaning_up; policy.ts isLifecycleWorkPending), and 'ready' is not one of them. An agent still 'resuming' at the restart is taken again and its transition to ready calls the hook then. Limit added when the review closed on a9005546 (20 Nov 2026), with no change of code nor of tests. While the agent is 'resuming', a resume that names nobody (an agent, a plugin, the company's resume) that comes just after a person's resume removes the person recorded a moment before: the last resume decides. The runs the pause cut are then refused resumed_without_a_person, and that refusal is on each task. The general rule above (a resume that names nobody drops the person on record) covers it; this is its case during 'resuming', right after a person's resume. Added on 20 Nov 2026, after the bench could not prove the continuation (its cut runs had no recorded process): the forms production recorded for the eight runs a pause cut from 17 to 20 Nov, read in the database by the pilot. All are legacy, cancelled agent_paused, their lease expired and released; seven ran for routed roles under a local lease (a process recorded, no process group, no acknowledged cancellation, the pause marker on four of them only, two cut while dispatching); one ran over ssh (process and group recorded, the cancellation acknowledged, no pause marker). Six cases added through the real lifecycle (37 cases in the file, all pass; tsc 310 as the base): the local form without the pause marker; cut while dispatching, with and without the marker; the ssh form; each is continued by the resume alone. A run cancelled by the direct pause route carries the reason 'Cancelled due to agent pause', which is a governance pause stop without the marker (governance-pause-stop.ts); only the lifecycle's own stop reason needs the marker. The stop recorded for a fresh attempt (recordedLocalExecutionStopped, the gate's freshIntent branch) holds on the local form when the identity is written by the spawn's own writer (persistHeartbeatRunProcessMetadata) for a real process that has exited, without a process group. A started run on which no process was ever recorded (the bench's form, not one of production) is not continued: the request is kept, stop_not_proven, wait process_identity_missing. Not verified in production data by this patch: the cancellation record of the four runs without the marker (expected: reason 'Cancelled due to agent pause', initiator system, expected true). Fourth head (20 Nov 2026), the three points of the review of 79ad9262. (1) A process number given to another program no longer holds a request. When the number the cut run recorded is still in use (the process, or its group), the continuation gate (explicit-native-continuation.ts, local stop proof) asks the product's own proof, recordedLocalExecutionStopped (native-local-process-stop.ts, on proveOwnerGone, owner-proof.ts): it reads the identity the spawn recorded for the run (number, group, birth time of the engine, host and process space) and the birth time of the process that has the number now. The request starts only when that process, or the leader of that group, was born later than the recorded engine. It is kept (process_running), as before, when the live process has the recorded birth time (the engine itself, also when it was started just after its run was cut), when nothing was recorded for the number, when a birth time cannot be read, when the group still has members and its leader is gone, and when the server's process space is not the recorded one. A first version of this change compared the birth time with the end of the run: it took an engine started just after the cut for another program and failed eleven cases of explicit-native-continuation.test.ts; it was replaced before the head was frozen, and one case and one mutant pin that difference. (2) A request kept for more than thirty minutes because the stop is not proven writes ONE system comment on its task and one activity entry (agent.pause_cut_work_kept, reason still_waiting_for_stop_proof); both name the cut run and what is awaited. A request that waits for a person gets none. The kept requests are looked at again by the deferred-receipt work (heartbeat/deferred-receipt-work.ts, about every 30 s), which calls resumeExecutionWaitComments then resumeTaskRetry (heartbeat/run-control.ts); the note is asked for there. (3) The local environment of the cut run not yet released when the role resumes: the request is kept (local_cleanup) and starts once the lease is released; no code changed for it, the case pins it. Who writes the process number the gate reads: the adapter reports its spawn (onSpawn, in each local engine adapter's execute.ts and in adapter-utils server-utils.ts), the server's onSpawn (heartbeat/runtime-execution.ts) calls persistRunProcessMetadata (heartbeat.ts, heartbeat/run-lifecycle.ts), and persistHeartbeatRunProcessMetadata (run-lifecycle.ts) reads the birth time of the process and writes it with the number and the event native.process_identity_recorded in one write. Cases: pause-resume-continuation.test.ts, 45 cases, all pass (45/45); nine are new or extended: the number held by a program born later than the recorded engine (the process; the process and its group), the recorded engine still alive, an engine started just after its run was cut, a number in use with no recorded identity, a group whose leader is gone, the local environment not yet released, the note after thirty minutes, and no note for a request that waits for a person. Eight mutants, each fails a case of its own: a number in use always keeps the request (the head before); it never does; the group is not looked at; a program born after the end of the run is taken for another one; the note at the first look; the note at every look; the note for any kept request; the note never asked for. Neighbours: 26 files, 996 cases, all pass (the gate and the Retry: 8 files, 598 cases, with explicit-native-continuation.test.ts; pause, resume and run control: 9 files, 184; the lifecycle module: 9 files, 214). tsc: the 310 errors of the base, none in a changed file. Limits of this head: where no identity was recorded for the number, or a birth time cannot be read, a reused number holds the request as before, and the task says so after thirty minutes; the note is written once per request, a request that stays kept for days says nothing more. Not corrected at this head: the continuation run that itself fails on a cut (lost link, router cut) gets no automatic retry, because the product makes that continuation a fresh-workspace attempt, which has one try (explicit-native-continuation.ts, readTaskRetryRetryAuthority); read and replayed on 20 Nov 2026; its correction is being decided.

patches.title: A ticket the worker router refuses goes to the direct manager of its role; a block that needs the Board wakes that manager; a recovery action settled by another role says so on the ticket
patches.problem: Production, 20 Nov 2026, 03:33, TR-2030: the CTO's run on TR-1587 was refused router_group_participant_ended. STUDIO-0059 blocks such a ticket at work at once, with a recovery action only the Board can settle; nobody was woken, the manager believed it could not settle it, and a person had to. The same on TR-1261 (15 Nov, router_group_participant_reserved), TR-1552, TR-1814 and TR-1815. Four other refusals the router names permanent (router_request_block_invalid, router_request_system_unknown, router_attempt_already_used, router_ticket_already_completed) were not known to the server at all: they were retried as ordinary failures, then blocked the same way. More generally, every path of the stranded-work sweep that blocks a ticket with a Board action (retries spent after a timeout, 'No live execution path'; an assignee that is not invokable outside a pause) wakes nobody: only the studio's watch warned the operator. Last, a manager can settle the recovery action of a role in its reporting chain (authorization.ts:2705-2716), and nine of the fourteen roles in service hold the direct right to settle anyone's, but nothing on the ticket said who settled what, for which role and in what capacity.

patches.migration: None: no stored data is changed, no setting. One new activity action, issue.handed_to_manager. What changes at runtime. Two gestures, not to be confused: the hand-over (points 1 and 2) CHANGES the assignee, the ticket becomes the manager's; the wake of point 3 does NOT, the ticket stays assigned to its role and blocked, and only a notice wakes the manager. (1) Hand-over, one function for the lot: handIssueToManager (recovery/manager-handover.ts). The ticket is reassigned to the direct manager of its role (the assignee's reportsTo), moved to in_review, a notice says why and what the manager is expected to do, the hand-over is recorded in the activity (cause, code, from, to, the run, its rank in the series) and the manager is woken once (wake reason issue_handed_to_manager, one per source run). No recovery action is created: the manager is the assignee and closes the ticket or gives it back with its own rights. What the reassignment itself does (issueService.update with a new assignee and the status in_review, read in services/issues.ts): it checks that the manager can be assigned work, clears the ticket's checkout and execution locks (as any change of assignee or any status other than in_progress does), and writes the row; it starts no review stage of an execution policy (that transition is made by the issue routes, not by this service, so the ticket's execution state is left as it is), wakes no reviewer and no tester (the only wake is the one of this patch, for the manager), and takes no checkout. The ticket is NOT handed, and the caller keeps today's path, when: the ticket is not at work (todo, in_progress), is hidden, or is no longer assigned to that role; the role itself is paused (a pause, by the Board or any other hold, does not move the role's work to somebody else); the role has no manager, or the manager is not invokable (paused, terminated, an invalid reporting chain); the ticket still holds something on the server (a run of the ticket queued or running; an execution or checkout lock on a run that has not ended; an environment lease of the ticket not released, the lease of the run that caused the hand-over aside, since its own end releases it); the same run already caused a hand-over; or the ticket was already handed twice for the same cause since the role last ran on it for another reason. (2) Router refusals (STUDIO-0059 extended). The four permanent codes named above join the four group refusals: none is retried any more, and each blocks at once where the group refusals do. Where STUDIO-0059 blocked a refused ticket with a Board action (escalateStrandedAssignedIssue, reached from the release of the refused run and from the sweep, which say so by the notice they pass: any other escalation of a ticket whose latest run happens to be a refusal, an assignee that is no longer invokable for one, keeps its block), the ticket at work of a role that has a manager is handed to that manager instead, with the note of its code: the two group refusals whose meaning is fixed say it (ended, closed); the six others quote the refused run's own message, redacted as elsewhere. At the release of the refused run the previous owner's execution is not settled yet, so the queue keeps the manager's wake as a hand-over wake (STUDIO-0066) and its periodic pass admits it. Nothing changes for a role without a manager (the CEO), for a manager that is not invokable, for a ticket in review (TR-1318: the note of STUDIO-0059 for ended and closed, the block for the others), nor after the Board's return. The manager gives the ticket back: the refusal that caused the hand-over is older than it and is not read again (the hand-over counts as the Board's return does); if the router refuses the role again, the ticket is handed a second time, and the note says it will not be a third time; a third refusal in the same series is today's block with its Board action. A run of the role on the ticket that was not refused under that code opens a new series. The manager decides nothing with the ticket it received: the product's own path for a ticket in review that nobody reviews applies, one more wake of the manager (issue_review_path_lost), then a block with a Board action. (3) L16: when the sweep blocks a ticket and creates a recovery action owned by the Board (the first time for that action), the direct manager of the role is woken once. The manager is not the assignee, and the queue starts a run of another agent on a ticket only for a comment (run-dispatch/domain/policy.ts, decideIssueOwnership): the server writes one notice on the ticket, addressed to the manager by name with the cause, and wakes it on that comment. The ticket stays blocked, assigned as it is, and the action stays the Board's. The assignee, the role the router or the engine failed, is not woken by that notice (a comment written by the server wakes nobody by itself; the wake is the one the server enqueues for the manager), so nothing is asked of the router again and no refusal is added to a series; the manager settles it by the reporting chain if the way forward is clear, or tells the operator. Not woken: a role without a manager; a manager that is not invokable; a manager whose own run led to the block. One level only. A provider-quota wait, owned by the system, wakes nobody. This also holds the owner's rule for an ssh lease outage longer than 12 h (STUDIO-0079) in its spirit: past the 12 h that patch blocks the issue with a Board action through this same place, so the direct manager is woken, though the issue is not handed to it (tried on a tree holding both patches). (4) L12, the trace: when an agent settles a recovery action, the activity issue.recovery_action_resolved also carries settledByAgentId, settledForAgentId and settledAs (assignee, recovery_owner, reporting_chain, ceo, direct_right), read in the order the authority check uses; and when the agent is not the assignee of the ticket, a notice on the ticket says who settled it, for which role, in what capacity, with the outcome and the status. The assignee settling its own ticket gets no notice. The rights themselves are not changed.

patches.title: A role that fails three times in a row on the same engine session, leaving nothing behind, starts its next run on a fresh session; if it fails on the fresh session too, the issue goes to its direct manager
patches.problem: Production, 20 Nov 2026, TR-2069. From 05:55 to 06:46 UTC the Dev Unity failed nine times in a row with router_interactive_ack_uncertain, 79 to 104 s each, after a first failure with router_interactive_output_limit: the same engine session before and after each run, a session that no longer reopened. Each failure scheduled a bounded retry, and each retry was cancelled before it started (issue_waiting_for_response: the worker router's card was pending on the ticket). The next run came each time from the manager's answering comment (issue_commented), which is not a retry, so the bounded-retry counter (heartbeat/retries.ts, failedRunRetryBudgetSpent, executionFailureRetryCount) started from zero at every turn. Nothing bounded the cycle. Each failed run left exactly four activity entries (environment.lease_acquired, environment.lease_released, tool_gateway.discovery, cost.reported) and nothing on the ticket. The owner: this must never happen again.

patches.validation: Linux (WSL), Node 24.22.2, a tree of 19c312cf with STUDIO-0083 and this patch, an embedded PostgreSQL. Test file server/src/__tests__/relaunch-loop-guard.test.ts, 93 cases, passed twice in a row (93/93, twice): 42 on the decision (the series, what is counted, passed over or ends it; the timeouts and the three signs of an engine at work; the run log read from its end, the host's lines and the session announcement set aside; the passing failures; the hand-over decision and its note) and 51 on the real run path (the heartbeat service, a test adapter that fails or times out as scripted, the real run log store). TR-2069 is replayed in the exact shape production recorded: a failure, the CTO's answer, a failure, an answer, a failure, each retry cancelled before it started; the fourth run starts on a fresh session, with one note. To its end: the fresh session fails too, and the issue goes to the CTO, in review, with the note word for word, the activity (cause relaunch_loop, the code, the fresh run), no Board action, the CTO woken, and no further run of the role. At length, as the 26 failures production recorded: twenty-six answers of the CTO start the role five times in all (once to open the session, three times on it, once fresh); the 22 others find the issue at the CTO and start nothing. A fresh session that left something behind before it failed is not handed. A role without a manager: the issue is blocked with a Board action. Given back by the CTO: the old failure hands nothing again; a new series goes through the fresh session once more and hands a second time, with the note that says it is the last; a third is the Board's. Asked again later for the same fresh run (a stop of the server at its end): the issue is handed once, under that run. After the independent review of head 892eda04. TR-2069 is replayed as production ran it: the worker router's card wakes the CTO as each run of the role fails, so that a run of the CTO is in the queue on the issue when the server decides what to do with the failure, the fresh session included, with the role's own retry waiting in the queue too; the issue is handed at once, under the fresh run, the CTO's run starts only after the hand-over, and the retry is cancelled without starting. The at-length case runs the same way, a run of the CTO in the queue at each failure. Measured on the way: a wake of the CTO that arrives WHILE the role's run is live is deferred (deferred_issue_execution), is no run and holds nothing; the one that holds is a wake that arrives once the run has failed. A fresh run that fails by an error of the run itself (the server's error branch, not the engine's answer) is handed all the same. Another agent's run on the issue (QA) holds it: nothing is handed, the events of the fresh run say so once, and the issue is handed, once and under the fresh run, at the end of the role's next run, QA's run being over by then (the role failed empty once more meanwhile, which changes nothing). A passing failure of the provider (codex_transient_upstream) between the failures of a series neither counts nor ends it; by decision cases, each of the four codes is passed over, and three in a row keep the session; a hand-over that was held stays due while the role only failed empty again. The hand-over itself (manager-handover.test.ts, 33 cases with this patch, passed twice with the refusal test: 70 of 71, the TR-1318 case aside): by default and with one of the two options only, a ticket with the manager's run and the role's queued retry is held; a run of the role that has started, another agent's run and another agent's lease still hold with both; with both, the ticket is handed with the manager's run running, its lease and its execution lock, and the role's retry in the queue; the lease of a run that has ended, named as the run being closed, does not hold either. The earlier cases hold: three timeouts during which the engine worked keep the session, by output tokens, by a summary, by a last message that is narration and is posted nowhere, by output written after the first five minutes; twenty minutes of router lines alone, or an engine that only announced its session after a long wait, do not; the router's refusals and its failures before any launch are not counted; a server stopped between the note and the clearing is repaired by the next run. Witness, heartbeat.ts of 19c312cf under the 87 cases of the first head (the guard is never called): 27 fail, TR-2069 among them. Witness of the review's correction, the three source files as merged before it (892eda04 on the corrected STUDIO-0083) under the 93 cases: 8 fail (the six new cases; the at-length case, where the CTO's queued run holds the issue and nothing is handed; and the asked-again case, whose expected answer changed from 'left' to 'none'), 85 pass; under the 33 cases of the hand-over: the case of the option fails, the 32 others pass. Mutants, one per rule, each applied alone: 64. On the final content, the eight of the third step (never handed, any empty failure handed, a fresh run that worked handed, a run that says nothing not passed over, no block for the Board, the note without the count, the guard's mark not read, the hand-over not asked at the end of the run), the one that had survived before (the summary of the engine ignored, killed by the narration case added for it) and two whose source lines changed (the runs of other issues read, the run about to start read) were run against the whole file (86 cases, before the at-length case was added): each fails at least one case. The 53 others were run on the content before the third step (76 cases then), by tiers (the decision cases, then a part of the real path, then the whole file): each failed at least one case; they were not run again on the final content, whose earlier cases are unchanged. After the review, on the corrected content, 19 were run, each against the whole file it concerns: the eight of the third step again, and those of the correction (the manager's run holding, the role's queued retry holding, a held hand-over left without a word, not asked again, ended by one more empty failure of the role, the hand-over asked at the normal end of a run only, the passing codes counted, the lease of the run being closed holding; in the hand-over itself, a started run of the role not holding, the manager's lease holding, the manager's lock holding): each fails at least one case. After the review the same suites were run again with the corrected content, and the two suites that go through the hand-over (issue-recovery-actions, 149 cases; case-handoffs, 90 cases): the session suites 251/251, the wake suites 143 of 144 with the same failure as on 19c312cf, run completion and the others 340/340, issue-recovery-actions 149/149, case-handoffs 90/90. tsc of the server: 310 errors, as on 19c312cf. Not proven: nothing was run against the real worker router nor a real engine session that no longer reopens; the hand-over is not replayed after a stop of the server between the end of the fresh run and the hand-over (read in the code: the next series makes it); a run log kept in object storage; the codes the worker router returns for a provider quota or outage of a routed role (the four codes passed over are those the server and the two local adapters use); a held hand-over after a restart of the server (it is kept in memory: read in the code, the role goes on and the next fresh session makes it); the hand-over asked again at the end of the holder's OWN run (the case asks it at the end of the role's next run, the holder being a run row the test ends).
patches.migration: None. What changes at runtime. When a run of an agent on an issue is about to choose its session (heartbeat.ts, executeRunAttempt, one call, whatever woke the run: an assignment, a comment, a retry, a plugin wake), the server reads the started runs of the SAME agent on the SAME issue, newest first. The series is the latest consecutive runs that failed, resumed the same engine session, lasted under 5 minutes and left nothing behind, whatever their error code. Neither counted nor ending the series: adapter-declared waits, the worker router's refusals before any reservation (twelve codes), the failures it returns before it launches any engine (five codes: router_estimate_not_received, router_control_scope_busy, router_secret_read_limited, router_worker_unreachable, router_continuation_deadline_expired; its two other pre-launch codes, router_waiting_for_resources and router_previous_dispatch_unsettled, are declared waits), cancelled and interrupted runs, runs that never started, runs that failed in setup before their adapter was admitted (a lease that could not be acquired: execution stage `preparing`), and the passing failures of the provider or of the host, by their code: provider_quota (the quota and the rate limit of both local adapters), codex_transient_upstream, claude_transient_upstream, and process_lost (a process lost at a restart). Three quick failures during an outage must not drop a sound session. The adapter's error family is NOT used for this: production scheduled a transient_failure retry after each failure of TR-2069, which the server does only for a failure it reads as transient, so the family would take the very failures the guard exists for out of the series. Which codes the worker router returns for a provider quota or outage of a routed role is not known here. Runs of other agents are not read, so another role's run or comment between two failures changes nothing. Ending the series: a success, a failure that left something behind, a failure on another session or on a fresh one, a failure of 5 minutes or more. 'Left something behind' is an activity entry of the product's own progress list (issue-rewake-throttle.ts, ISSUE_PROGRESS_ACTIVITY_ACTIONS) written by the agent itself under that run, on any issue, or a comment of the agent created by that run. A run that ended on a timeout (status timed_out, code timeout or router_interactive_timeout) is counted whatever it lasted, because a session too large to reopen makes every run that resumes it last as long as the timeout itself (STUDIO-0080 returns the session of a timed-out run); such a run counts only when its engine did nothing, read from what the server records of any run: no output tokens of the model, no summary returned by the adapter, and no output of the engine after the run's first 5 minutes. The run row keeps the time of its last log chunk whoever wrote it, and the host writes lines of its own into a run log: the worker router's, each starting with `[paperclip-router] ` (one a minute while it waits before a launch), and Paperclip's diagnostics, each starting with `[paperclip] `. So when that time is late, the run's log is read from its end (pages of 256 kB, 8 pages at most, for the 6 newest such runs) for the last chunk that holds a line of the engine's work, and that chunk's time is the one set against the first 5 minutes. A line of the engine's work is one the host did not write and that is not the engine's session announcement (Codex: `thread.started`; Claude: `system`/`init`): the announcement says a session was opened, not that the engine did anything, and the worker router writes Codex's when the session opens, which can be ten minutes into a run that waited before its launch (the router's own remark, 20 Nov 2026). When the answer is not known (no log, a storage error, a log longer than what is read back with the host's lines only so far, a seventh such run), the late chunk is taken as the engine's and the session is kept: dropping the session of a role at work costs more than one more run on a dead one. No single sign holds for every engine: Codex reports its tokens at the end of a turn only, so a Codex run cut by its timeout has none whether it worked or not, and an engine's tool calls are in the run log, not in the run's events; hence the three signs, any one of which says the engine worked. The worker router (its own account, 20 Nov 2026, router commit 6d298b0) returns neither tokens nor a summary with a failure, and never `timedOut: true` for a steered run: a turn that ran out of time is a failed run under router_interactive_timeout, and the engine's events reach the run log as they come. For a routed role the third sign is therefore the only one, which is why the host's lines must not count in it. router_interactive_ack_uncertain, the code of TR-2069 (a request to the engine left unanswered: 30 s, 180 s for the resume of a session), is short and is counted by the ordinary rule. Where each sign exists. Output tokens: a Claude run that is not steered by the router (a local agent, or a routed one whose engine Paperclip's own adapter launches over ssh) has them even when cut by its timeout, since Claude reports them as its stream goes; a Codex run cut by its timeout has none; a steered routed run that fails has none, whatever its engine, because the router's own envelope builds its whole result. Summary: a Codex run that is not steered returns what it last said with its timeout (STUDIO-0080); a Claude run returns a summary only with its final result, so not on a timeout; a steered routed run that fails has none, even with STUDIO-0080, whose timeout paths it does not go through. Engine output after the first 5 minutes: every run, since the two local adapters and the worker router all write the engine's output into the run log as it comes; it is the only sign of a steered routed run. A trial moves the time of the engine's records in the log file of such runs: last written at minute 15 of 20, the run is not counted; last written at minute 1 (the announcement), with the router's notes after it, the run is counted. A limit: a local Codex that says nothing at all, then runs one silent command for the rest of its timeout, has none of the three signs (no tokens, an empty summary, its last output in the first minutes) and is counted. It is rare: the adapter's own output-inactivity monitor (30 minutes) stops such a run first and returns no session. A Codex that said what it was starting is not counted, because STUDIO-0080 returns what it last said with the timeout. At three, the run about to start drops the session: the kept session of the agent for the issue is cleared, an explicit resume of it is removed, the run is marked (contextSnapshot.relaunchLoopGuard) and starts on a fresh session, one system note is posted on the issue, an activity entry and a run event are written. The guard keeps no counter of its own: it reads the runs at each start, so a cut in the middle of the gesture is repaired by the next run, which reads the same series and finds the note already there. An error inside the guard is logged and never fails the run. N (3) and the duration (5 minutes) are constants of the module. The link with STUDIO-0080, in so many words. With STUDIO-0080 the summary of a run that did not succeed is posted as a comment of the role under a line that gives the run's status. A run that reached its timeout after its engine said something therefore leaves a comment of the role, which is 'left something behind': it does not feed the series. A timed-out run whose engine said nothing posts nothing and feeds it. This is wanted: the guard is for a session that no longer reopens, not for a role that works past its timeout. What then bounds a role that exceeds its timeout at every run while saying something each time is not this guard: a run that ended on a timeout is relaunched by the stranded-work sweep (`timeout` is in TRANSIENT_INFRA_CONTINUATION_ERROR_CODES, recovery/service.ts:557), three times in a row at most (CONTINUATION_RECOVERY_TRANSIENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS, recovery/service.ts:613-615, with a 60 s base backoff); then the issue is blocked with a Board action, and the lot's rule L16 wakes the role's manager at that action (L16 is another patch of the lot). Third step, on STUDIO-0083 (this patch is stacked on it and uses its function handIssueToManager): when the run the guard started on a fresh session ends as an empty failure too (the same reading as for the series: failed, short or on a timeout with an engine that did nothing, nothing left behind), the session was not the cause. The issue is handed to the direct manager of the role: reassigned, in review, with a note that gives the role, the number of failures and the code, the manager woken once, and no Board action. The role is no longer the assignee, so nothing relaunches it on the issue until the manager gives it back, reassigns or closes it. A run that only waited or was refused before any reservation after the fresh run says nothing and is passed over; a fresh run that left something behind, lasted, or succeeded is not handed. The hand-over is made at the end of the fresh run, however it ended (heartbeat.ts, the closing block of executeRunAttempt, once the run is terminal: its normal completion or the server's error branch). What may live on the issue at that moment: the worker router's card wakes the manager as the role fails, and a wake that arrives once the run has failed, while the server is still closing it, is a run of the manager in the queue (a wake that arrives while the role's run is still live is deferred and is no run: measured); the role's own retry may wait in the queue too. Neither holds the issue for this hand-over (an option of handIssueToManager, doesNotHold, set by this patch only and added by it to manager-handover.ts: the role's runs still in the queue, the manager's own runs, with the manager's lease and lock, and the lease of the run at whose end the hand-over is asked, which that end releases): the issue is handed at once, the queue cancels the retry as a run of a former assignee, and the manager's run goes on, on an issue that is now its own. Another agent's run, a run of the role that has started, or a lease still hold the issue. The hand-over is then not made, and never without a word: a warning is logged, a line is written in the events of the fresh run ('the issue is due to the role's manager, but a run or a lease on the issue still holds it'), and it is asked again at the end of each run on the issue, of any agent, until it is made or no longer due (the role did something, the issue left the role or its work). While it is held the role may fail empty again: that changes nothing. The held hand-overs are kept in the server's memory: after a restart the role goes on, and the next fresh session makes the hand-over. A hand-over that is due and not made for a reason that will not change by itself (the role is paused: STUDIO-0083 keeps a paused role's work with the role) is logged the same way and not asked again. It is not asked at the start of the role's next run, because a run that starts holds the issue. Given back by the manager: the fresh run that caused the hand-over hands nothing again; if a new series forms (three more empty failures on the session of that fresh run), the guard goes through the fresh session once more, and a failure there hands the issue a second time, with the note that says it is the last; a third time in the same series is the Board's. Where no manager can receive the issue (the role has none, the manager is not invokable, or the issue was already handed twice), the issue is blocked with a Board action by the block of stranded work (escalateStrandedAssignedIssue), which with STUDIO-0083 wakes the direct manager when there is one. A comment still wakes a role on a blocked issue: a role without any manager (the CEO) is slowed to one fresh session every three failures, not stopped. What stops the relaunches when the machine itself no longer answers. (a) While the router still launches an engine and the run ends router_interactive_ack_uncertain (the 26 failures of TR-2069), each run is an empty failure and is counted: three on the session, one on a fresh session, and at the end of that fourth run the issue goes to the manager. The role is no longer the assignee, so the manager's answers start it no more: it stops at the fourth counted failure, whatever the cause. (b) A run the router fails before it launches anything (router_worker_unreachable, router_estimate_not_received and the three others) or a declared wait is neither counted nor ends the series, by the router's own account that their cause is outside the session: a cycle made only of those is not bounded by this patch, but by the ordinary retry budget and, for a declared wait, by its own bound. (c) After two hand-overs the manager gave back, the third time is a Board block; a comment still starts a role on a blocked issue (measured: a manager that gives the issue back at every answer gets 4 runs, a hand-over, 5 runs, a hand-over, 5 runs, then the block; one more answer starts the role again). From there the guard only renews the session every fourth run: what ends it is the manager no longer answering, or the Board.

patches.title: The access token of a KitWright broker, carried in its local address, is masked by the form of that address when a run's output is written and when a run is read
patches.problem: Production, 20 Nov 2026 (drafts/infra-role/securite-jeton-kitwright-20261120.md, read by counts and equalities, no value copied). The local address of a KitWright broker carries the broker's access token in its path: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/p/<8 characters>/t/<32 characters>/. The Codex MCP client prints the whole address in the error of a failed tool call ('error sending request for url (…)'), and that error reached run logs in clear: 19 appearances in 13 runs of the day, for five brokers (Razer 7, WIN-01 4, MAC-02 4, MAC-01 3, WIN-02 1), all from Codex runs; the Claude engine writes the address already masked (/t/redacted/). Any standard role can read the log of another role's run (read in the code and played on the bench by the server pilot). The token gives the Unity Editor of the machine to whoever already runs something on it, and it lives as long as the broker. The server masked only values it knows exactly (the agent's private key, the registered secrets): it does not know this token.

patches.validation: Linux (WSL), Node 24.22.2, a tree of 19c312cf with this patch. New test file server/src/__tests__/broker-address-redaction.test.ts, 12 cases, passed twice in a row (12/12, twice), with made-up values of the form. At the write (createAgentIdentityRedactor): the line the Codex MCP client writes for a failed tool call (item.error.message of an mcp_tool_call, 'error sending request for url (…)'), with a Mac path and with a PC path, comes out with its token replaced and everything else intact; the same in the events and in the result of a run; the address cut between two chunks at EVERY position of the line, stdout and stderr interleaved with two different tokens, and cut in three chunks at every pair of positions inside the address, is written exactly as the whole line would be; an address interrupted by the end of the output keeps its beginning and gives no character of the token, at every position; the agent's private key is masked as before, and an interrupted key stays hidden. Left as they are: the address the Claude engine already masks (/t/redacted/), the server's own mask, another host or scheme (127.0.0.2, localhost, 10.0.0.5, https), other lengths (a token of 31 or 33 characters, a first segment of 7 or 9, a port of 6 digits, no port), another path; a token ended by something other than a slash is masked all the same. At the read (createRunSecretRedactionRegistry, a database with no registered secret): a line written in clear before the patch is masked in a page of the log, in the events, in the run, in a list of runs and in what is read of an issue; with a first page that ends at every position around each of two addresses, and with every page size from 69 to 400 bytes, the pages put end to end are the whole log with its tokens masked, no page holds three characters of a token, and the reader always advances; a page keeps its byte length (the mask of a page has the length of the token), so the offset a reader computes from what it received is exact; only a page of a run log is shortened, and only before an address that is not closed. A log of 37.5 MB read by pages of 256 kB, with 68 addresses: 0.108 ms a page through the run's redaction with the patch, 0.037 ms without it (the same case on 19c312cf), against 0.2 ms to decode the page. Witness, the two source files of 19c312cf under these tests: the 12 cases fail. Mutants, one per rule, each applied alone: 18, and each fails at least one case (the write not masked, an ending not held, an interrupted address wholly hidden, an interrupted token left in clear; the read not masked, a page not shortened, its next offset not moved, a page mask that changes the length, any object with a content taken for a page; other token lengths, a longer token cut, other segment lengths, a port of six digits, any host, the whole address masked; the beginning of the head not held, an open address that stops early, a window too short). Neighbours, on 19c312cf and with the patch: the redaction and run-read suites (7 files) 164 of 169 on both, the same five failures of agent-live-run-routes; run log, run output, runtime execution and run completion (5 files) 218/218 on both; the native run log and task context suites (5 files, one skipped) 60/60 on both. tsc of the server: 310 errors, as on 19c312cf. Not proven: nothing was run against a real broker, a real Codex engine nor the production logs (no real value was read to write this patch: the form comes from the infra note); the log route itself is not driven end to end (its page is rebuilt in the test as the route builds it); a run log kept in object storage; the native runtime's own writers of a run log.
patches.migration: None. What changes at runtime. The form http://127.0.0.1:<port>/p/<8 characters>/t/<32 characters>/ is masked: the 32 characters after /t/ are replaced by the server's mask (***REDACTED***), the rest of the address stays. One shared function (maskBrokerAddresses, run-secret-redaction.ts), called at two places. (1) At the write: createAgentIdentityRedactor (agent-identity-redaction.ts) masks the form in chunk(), finish() and redact(), which every chunk of a run's output, every adapter event and the run's result go through (heartbeat/run-output.ts, runtime-execution.ts). chunk() keeps back an ending that could begin an address (from the last 'http://127.0.0.1:' not closed, or a part of that head), per stream, as it already does for the private key; finish() returns an interrupted address with what follows /t/ hidden. (2) At the read: redactText, by which redactForRun, redactForRuns and redactForIssue pass, so the log, the events, the detail and the lists of runs, live events, and what is read of an issue. Lines written in clear before the patch are therefore masked at each read. A page of a run log is read by byte offset: redactForRun ends a page just before an address that is not closed and moves its next offset back by as much, so the next page starts at the address; in a page the mask keeps the length of the token (***REDACTED*** padded with stars to 32), because a reader that gets no next offset computes it from the size of what it received. What it costs: 0.108 ms a page through the run's redaction with the patch, 0.037 ms without it (the same case on 19c312cf), against 0.2 ms to decode the page. What this patch does NOT do. It does not erase anything: the lines already written stay in clear in the log files on the server's disk and in the backups, and in the database rows of run events; they are masked when read through the server, not at rest. It does not rewrite a comment, a description or a document a role wrote: they are stored as written; the reads of an issue that already pass through the run redaction (redactForIssue) mask the form, the other reads of a comment (activity, search, notifications, plugins) were not looked at. It does not touch the Codex history on the machines, which keeps the tool's output. It does not change the token: only stopping the broker does. Limits. A reader that picks its own offset can start a page inside an address: that page then begins with the end of the token, which nothing in the page tells from ordinary text; closing this needs the page's offset and the bytes before it, in the log route or the log store, which this patch does not touch. An address that the engine's output had cut between two chunks BEFORE the patch is in two records of the log and is not recognised at the read. A page smaller than an address (under 69 bytes) that lies inside one comes back empty and does not advance. The logs of workspace operations (another route) do not pass through the run redaction. Only this form is masked: the first segment (/p/<8>/) stays, an address written with escaped slashes, over https or to another host is not recognised. Since the function is shared, the form is masked too in what a run receives of an issue (comments, wake payload): a role gets its broker's address from its launcher, not from a comment.

patches.title: The session of a cut run is kept when its result comes after the run was settled, and a person's request after a pause continues in it instead of opening a new conversation
patches.problem: Production, 20 Nov 2026, 03:00 UTC. Two routed runs (claude_local, codex_local) ended router_provider_stop_unverified after the link to their worker machine was lost; their retries opened new conversations in the same remote folder. Read on 19c312cf: the router's failure result named no session, so the server wrote the previous session back; the router returns the session from its version 0.30.19, and such a result is kept while the run is still running (resolveNextSessionState, persistSessionState). Two holes remained. (1) When the run was already settled by another path when its result came (a pause or a stop cancelled it, recovery declared it lost), completeRun skipped the late finalization and dropped the result's session with it. (2) A person's request on an interrupted run (a message, Retry, hence also the automatic continuation of STUDIO-0074) always forced a fresh session (queue.ts, forceFreshSession): after a pause the role started again from a summary, whether or not its session was kept.
patches.reason: The owner's rule of 20 Nov 2026 (studio journal V663): a machine that loses its connection must not lose its work; on its return the same role resumes where it was, on the same machine. Asked by the server's pilot for the next lot, with STUDIO-0074.
patches.owner: run completion (heartbeat/run-completion.ts) and wake admission of a person's continuation (heartbeat/queue.ts)

(4) A late result does not replace the session a later run of the role wrote. (5) A late result that names no session writes nothing. patches.problem: Production, 22 Nov 2026, read by the analysis chat and the server pilot (drafts/analyse-fable-high/COMMANDE-LOT-26.md, drafts/lot-26/pilote.md). TR-2019 (Super Dev Unity) holds the machine MAC-03 and is blocked by TR-2061; TR-2061 (Infra Manager: a maintenance on MAC-03) cannot intervene because MAC-03 is reserved by TR-2019.
