patches.migration: None: no stored data is changed, no setting. THIS PATCH GIVES A NEW RIGHT, to one plugin: the worker router's. What the right allows: the router's plugin may start a run of the assignee of an issue that has a blocker not done, for one of three reasons and nothing else: worker_router_machine_lent (a machine was lent to the maintenance this issue carries), worker_router_loan_requested (the role that holds a machine is asked to lend it), worker_router_loan_returned (the machine is given back to that role). What the right does NOT allow: it lifts no blocker and changes no status (the issue stays blocked); it does not unblock the work (the run is the assignee's own, in the bounded mode of a blocked issue, told that blocker-dependent work is not unblocked); it carries no text (the reason is one of the three, the source is a fixed text of the server: nothing a role or the plugin writes reaches the run through this wake); it serves no other plugin, even one that declares the same field and holds issues.wakeup; it wakes no issue that is backlog, done or cancelled, none without an assignee, no role that is paused or over its budget; it gives no right to a role: an agent's comment on a blocked issue stays held (STUDIO-0063). How it is checked. Today such a wake is refused at three places: the plugin's door (plugin-host-services.ts, requestWakeup and requestWakeups), the admission of the wake and the start of the run (heartbeat/queue.ts), and the gate of a run the server retries (run-dispatch/adapters/postgres.ts, loadGateFacts). With this patch it passes when, and only when: its reason is in the closed list PLUGIN_BLOCKED_ISSUE_WAKE_REASONS; the plugin is one of PLUGIN_BLOCKED_ISSUE_WAKE_PLUGIN_KEYS, by its key (the manifest id, plugin_key, unique on a server: amynoox.worker-router), and its manifest declares blockedIssueWakeups: true (it still needs the capability issues.wakeup, as any wake); and the wake carries the mark pluginBlockedWake: { pluginId, reason }, which the plugin's door writes. Both lists are in one place, packages/shared/src/constants.ts. The doors of the queue never trust the mark alone (services/plugin-blocked-wake.ts, verifyPluginBlockedWake): they check that the wake request was made by the system for that plugin, and they read the plugin in the database again (its key, ready, the field in its manifest). A retry the server itself creates after a resource wait or a passing failure keeps the context and has no request of the plugin: it is admitted on the mark and the plugin's state, as the stalled-blocker wake is. What the server cannot check: which issue a reason may target (the holder's for two, the maintenance's for the third), and that a maintenance is open on the machine the issue holds; it knows nothing of machines and maintenances, which are the router's registry: that bound rests on the router. Why a manifest field and the plugin's key, and not a new capability as first proposed: the host validates a manifest each time it activates a plugin (plugin-loader.ts), and its capabilities are a closed list (validators/plugin.ts): a plugin that declared a capability unknown to a server could not load on it, so a roll-back of the server would stop the worker router. An unknown manifest field is dropped and the plugin loads as before. Server and router can therefore each be installed and rolled back without the other. No company switch: asked for if it fitted in about fifteen lines, it does not. Reading one would be about ten lines, but nothing exists where the Board could set it (no free company setting; the per-company plugin settings have one route only, for local folders): it would take a route with its permission check and a control in the interface. What is reversible without code: disabling the plugin for the company, or removing the field from the router's manifest; wakes already queued then lose the way at once. Limits. The bounded mode tells the run 'respond or triage the human comment; do not treat blocker-dependent deliverable work as unblocked' (packages/adapter-utils/src/server-utils.ts): for the router's wakes there is no person's comment, and that text is not changed here (it is in adapter-utils, whose change moves the adapters' fingerprints), so what the worker router shows the role must tell it what to do. The mark is written whenever the reason and the plugin qualify, also when the issue has no blocker at that moment: a blocker set before the run starts does not lose the wake.

TR-2019 (Super Dev Unity, the host) and TR-2466 (Game Tester, the guest) work together, each on its own task. patches.title: A pause completes when a cancelled run that launched nothing had taken an ssh lease and released it
patches.problem: Production, 22 Nov 2026: the Infra Manager stayed in lifecycle `pausing`. A run of the role had been cancelled without a stop request, had settled, and had launched nothing (no process identity, no session, no execution-start event), but an ssh lease had been taken for it and released. STUDIO-0061 gives such a run its stop proof at pause time only when no remote lease was taken; with a remote lease it leaves the run to the ssh-client rule (STUDIO-0043), which asks for a recorded ssh client proven gone. A run that recorded no ssh client can never meet that rule, so the pause never ended. It was lifted by a Board gesture that wrote the proof by hand (tools/stop-proof-before-launch.py).
patches.reason: Lot 26, a server piece listed by the server pilot (drafts/lot-26/pilote.md) and ordered by the main session on 22 Nov 2026, after the pieces of the lot: accept the run when its lease is ssh, released, without a failed cleanup, and the run recorded no ssh client, no start event, no session. These are the conditions of the Board tool, proven on the bench and in production. One condition is added here from that tool and from the ssh-client rule: the run must have finished for 10 minutes.
patches.owner: the stop proof of a pause (server/src/services/pre-dispatch-cancellation.ts, server/src/services/agent-execution-stop.ts)

The three new cases, on a run cancelled without a stop request, settled, legacy, with no process, no session and no execution-start event, for which an ssh lease was taken: (1) the lease was released (status expired or released, cleanup not failed) and the run finished 15 minutes ago: outside a pause nothing changes and no marker is written; the pause records the stop (preDispatchCancellation, source stopped_before_process_launch) and completes, also through the lifecycle worker (a role in `pausing` completes its pause); the same run finished 5 minutes ago still waits (the delay is the ssh-client rule's, 10 minutes); a local lease keeps its shorter delay. (2) Refused, no marker: the run recorded its ssh client (a pid, alive), a process group, a session, an execution-start event (adapter.invoke, session.started, provider.event), or its adapter control has not settled. (3) Refused, no marker: a lease of another remote provider, a lease not released (marked active or expired), released but still marked active, cleanup pending, cleanup failed; two leases of which one is refused; a cleanup status never written is not a failed cleanup. patches.title: The worker router's wake on a blocked issue (STUDIO-0086) never merges with another wake: it keeps its own run and its own request, in either arrival order
patches.problem: Review of lot 26 (22 Nov 2026), defect 3 on STUDIO-0086, and the design page conception-R17.md. A wake that arrives while a run of the same agent waits or runs on the same issue is merged into that run: the incoming context replaces the present one, the wake reason included. The router's mark is read only while the wake reason is still the mark's reason, and the requester is read on the wake request of the run. So: (A) the router wakes the assignee of a blocked issue and the run waits to start; another role comments; the comment is merged, the reason becomes `issue_commented`, the mark no longer counts, the role's comment is held as usual and the run is cancelled `issue_dependencies_blocked`: the router's signal never arrives and the server does not replay it. (B) an ordinary run of the assignee waits to start; the router's wake is merged into it: the mark is written, but the run's request is not the plugin's: refused, cancelled, signal lost. The same two cases exist for wakes that WAIT behind a run at work (two waiting wakes for one issue are merged into one request). Found while coding, by the tests: a wake that waits behind a run cancelled at its START for the blocker is promoted by nothing (that cancellation ends no run, and the periodic pass takes up only waiting wakes that carry comments, a card's answer or a resolved dependency); and a new run takes in the comment wakes that wait for the issue.
patches.reason: Ordered by the analysis chat on the owner's decisions of 22 Nov 2026 (21:29 UTC), for the second install of the server that evening; the owner's words: 'Fait le coder maintenant'. Way A of the design page (the server lets no wake mix with the router's), the rule the server already applies to cards.

patches.title: A wake that waits behind a scheduled retry is promoted when the retry's gate cancels it, and a card's wake left waiting on the addressee's own task is taken up by the periodic pass
patches.problem: Production, 22 Nov 2026, TR-2562 (during the trial of STUDIO-0089/0094). A role ended two runs on its task, in progress, without a disposition; the server scheduled a disposition repair (run 560051b6, scheduled_retry, issue_disposition_repair, created 23:36:29 UTC). At 23:36:57 a card of the Board on another task (TR-2561) named TR-2562 for its wake (STUDIO-0087): the wake (request 8a95a33b) waited behind the scheduled retry, status deferred_issue_execution. At 23:37:34 the retry came due and its gate cancelled it as superseded (issue_disposition_repair_superseded): a disposition repair is superseded when the task has another execution path, and the waiting wake is one. Nothing then promoted that wake: the task had no run and no lock, the role was idle, and the wake waited for ever; a Board comment (an explicit wake) was the remedy. Read in the code: (1) the gate's cancellation (run-dispatch adapters/postgres.ts, cancelSuppressedRetryInTx) clears the task's lock and calls no release; (2) the release itself would promote nothing behind that run: before it looks at the waiting wakes it treats a cancelled legacy run as one whose actions may need reconciliation (wake-queue adapters/postgres.ts, the pre-drain facts), and a retry that never left scheduled_retry carries none of the proofs that exempt a run that never started; (3) the periodic pass over waiting wakes (heartbeat/queue.ts, resumeDeferredExecutionReceipts) selects this wake and then leaves it, because it looks for the card on the wake's task and with STUDIO-0087 the card is on another task; and that pass ends in the same release as (2). The path is the same in the tree installed before (1f8c468f): the two files of (1) and (2) are identical in both, and STUDIO-0087 was already there.

patches.title: An agent on a local engine is steerable by default: written at its creation, and kept through a change of engine (experimentalLiveSteering)
patches.problem: Live steering (a person's message handed to the run at work) is switched by a free key of an agent's adapter configuration, `experimentalLiveSteering`, read as exactly `true` where a run is dispatched (services/adapter-interactive-control.ts, heartbeat/runtime-selection.ts, heartbeat/runtime-execution.ts) and by the two local engines (claude_local, codex_local). Absent, it reads as off. Nothing writes it: no schema, no default, no field on the screen. A role created through the screen or the API was never steerable until someone set the key by hand; on 23 Nov 2026 four roles were still without it and were set one by one. And a role that was steerable lost it without a word at a change of engine: the route that changes an agent's engine keeps eight engine-agnostic keys of the old configuration (ADAPTER_AGNOSTIC_KEYS: env, promptTemplate, instructionsFilePath, cwd, timeoutSec, graceSec, bootstrapPromptTemplate, paperclipSkillSync) and drops the rest, this key included. Production, 22 Nov 2026: two roles moved from Codex to Claude came out not steerable and were switched on again by hand. The studio's roles get their engine by that change, not by their creation.

WHAT A STEERABLE AGENT CHANGES AT A PAUSE (production, 23 Nov 2026, read by the worker router's chat on the roles switched that night): the steerable process is supplied by the worker router's plugin, also for an agent that is not routed to a worker; its runs carry no process group, and a pause that cuts such a run is not acknowledged as the stop of an ordinary run is. The task then keeps its hold, the resume of the role files the resume's Retry (STUDIO-0074), and that Retry keeps the conversation and the folder under the checks of STUDIO-0075. An agent created with this patch follows that path from its first pause. What the server cannot read there: whether the engine stops when the steering link ends (the stop proof of a local lease is that the recorded pid is gone). Not reached, on purpose or by the product's own rules: (1) an agent that already exists and whose engine does not change, whatever else is changed on it; (2) an agent the server stores on its NATIVE LAUNCHER (`paperclip_runner`): without `runner: "legacy"` in the request, a creation that names claude_local or codex_local is stored on that launcher (services/agent-runner-selection.ts: the default choice is `auto`), which does not read this key and has its own steering. A role created from the screen without that choice is on the native launcher and is not covered by this patch.

patches.title: A person who puts an assigned task to work wakes its assignee, and a person's wake refused by a pause leaves its row and is replayed at the resume
patches.problem: Production, 23 Nov 2026 (studio.29): three tasks already assigned to the CEO (TR-2456, TR-2462, TR-2523) were put in progress by the Board at 02:26-02:27 UTC while the CEO was `pausing`; at 02:34 none had a wake request, and nothing was replayed when the role resumed. Two holes, read in the code of the tree in service. (1) A change of status wakes the assignee only when it leaves backlog, goes from blocked or from a closed status to todo, or when a person sends a task in review back to todo (routes/issues.ts): todo -> in_progress on a task that is already assigned wakes nobody, pause or not. patches.migration: None: no table, no column, no setting. What changes at runtime. A recovery action of cause legacy_execution_requires_reconciliation that is SETTLED with replay blocked no longer holds a task when ALL of this is true: the action is not open (its status is neither active nor escalated); neither its evidence nor its run's result carries a workspace restore failure, a workspace restore recovery or (on the action) a system recovery; its run is a legacy run in a terminal status (cancelled, failed, timed out, interrupted) with an end recorded; every environment lease of that run is released, none active or pending cleanup, none with a failed cleanup; the task has an owner (an agent or a person), and the run's agent is neither the task's assignee nor the agent a pending review waits on. It is read at three places: the two reads of getExecutionBlocker (so the task shows no executionHold, and admission sees no blocker) and the read of the actions a person's request is checked against (so a person's message on the task starts the new assignee like any message, instead of being refused as `source_unavailable`). The action itself is not changed: it stays settled, with its evidence, and it holds the task again if the task returns to the run's agent. An action still open holds the task as before; so does a run whose process is still alive or whose lease is not released, through the ownership blocker. The deferred-wake sweep (resumeDeferredExecutionReceipts, the sweep of STUDIO-0041) also takes the wakes whose execution wait names such a released hold, whatever the wait's reason (a person's message waits as `source_unavailable`): once the task has no execution blocker, each is retired and re-admitted through ordinary admission, one task at a time, as for STUDIO-0041; a second held wake of the same task is re-admitted in its turn or folded into the wake already on its way. To know. (a) The release is for the whole task: every wake of the new owner, not one request. (b) It asks for no proof that a process is gone beyond the ownership blocker, which watches the process of conversation engines only (claude_local, codex_local and the like); for another engine nothing checks that the former assignee's process ended, beyond its run being ended and its leases released. (c) On TR-165 the three wakes held since 23 Nov are re-admitted one after the other: between one and three successive runs of the new assignee, depending on whether a later one is folded into the wake already on its way; the sweep has no limit of age in service. (d) What the former assignee's run did before it was cut stays unverified; the run stays there to inspect. Not covered: an action still open; native runs' holds (cause native_continuation_requires_reconciliation); holds with a folder to repair (they keep their own release).

patches.title: The hand-over backstop leaves alone a ready issue whose assignee's latest started run ended in a wait the adapter declared, while that wait is within its bound and the adapter is the one that ends it; past the bound, and in every other case, it wakes as before
patches.problem: Production, 23 Nov 2026, 04:18 to 05:25 UTC: 32 of the 33 runs that failed `router_waiting_for_resources` in two days were one burst on four tasks of the same role (TR-2613, TR-2616, TR-2619, TR-2620, seven to nine runs each). Each was started by the periodic hand-over backstop of STUDIO-0063 (`recovery/held-comment-handover-backstop.ts`), under its own doubling wait (30 s, 1 min, 2 min... up to 1 h). A run that ends in a declared wait never qualifies, so the issue stayed eligible and was woken again and again. The worker router refused each run without launching anything, kept the request, and woke each task itself once a machine was free. The backstop reads no declared wait: it only skips a live wake or run, an active recovery action, an assignee that is not invocable. The stranded-work recovery, the wake queue, the relaunch guard and run completion all read the closed list of declared waits and its bound; this pass did not.
patches.reason: Decided by the studio on 24 Nov 2026, after a short reading of where the backstop decides (no code before it): a small guard, with the closed list and the bound the other passes already read, without copying the rule; four tests, among them the negative control that past the bound the backstop wakes again, so that no issue is left with nobody. After the independent review of the first head (25 Nov 2026): the guard stands on the ready path only (when only cancelled blockers are left, the adapter's wake is refused at the plugins' gate and the hand-back is the only way back), not for router_ticket_blocked once the issue is no longer blocked (the router promises no wake for it: the server's dependency wake, of which this backstop is one, ends it), never for router_readmission_not_drained (the router keeps nothing and wakes nobody for it), and a reading that throws leaves the pass as before.

patches.title: The stop of a steered run's engine is proven by the server's own observation of the machine: a pause concludes in seconds and the work goes on in the same conversation and folder; without that proof no later run of the task, whatever started it, continues in them
patches.problem: A steered run (live steering, adapter_interactive_v1) is driven through a link. The process the server records for it (onSpawn) is that link, an ssh client on the server, with no process group: never the engine on the machine. When a pause cuts the run the link ends; the engine ends only when its input closes. The pause's stop proof for a run over the role's own ssh environment is the absence of that ssh client ten minutes after the run ended (STUDIO-0043): the role stays in `pausing` for those ten minutes, and work given to it meanwhile waits. The request that continues the work accepts the same proof (STUDIO-0073), and the run that continues a pause-cut run then keeps the conversation and the task's folder (STUDIO-0075). Production, 23 Nov 2026: nothing the server reads says that the engine, or something it started, stopped; the continuation could start in the same conversation and the same folder while the engine was still writing there. The receipt a launcher may keep on the machine is written under the role's own account, and what the adapter hands with the stop callback of its own execution is said by code that runs for that same run: neither is a proof the server can stand on.
patches.reason: Decided by the studio on 23 Nov 2026, under the owner's delegation: what concludes is the server's own reading of the machine, not what the run says of itself. The server asks the adapter that drives the engine to look, after the run ended, with the server's own connection to the role's environment, at the processes of the session's account (program name, process number, start time; never arguments); it stops a living engine under written conditions (the role's account, the process number checked by its start time and its program's name, after the grace the agent is given) and says so in an activity line; and no continuation without the proof, on ANY path that resumes a task (the resume's Retry, a person's message, an assignment, a timer, a replayed wake). The gain is that a pause concludes in seconds when the machine answers, and the conversation is kept. The form of the announcement and of the observation was agreed with the worker router (its adapter modules for the two local engines carry `readProviderStop` and announce the engine; worker router 0.30.26). After the independent review of the head c4a23d4d (25 Nov 2026): a pause asks the machine only of a run it cut, and only once the ssh client rule does not already stop it; before, every reading of every later pause asked again of every earlier cut run without a proof, each question a connection to the role's account whose service manager could still be alive at the look of this pause's run, which then never proved anything. Also: a process name is never a command line, `absent` carries its lists, and the spacing counts from the end of a call.
patches.owner: the stop proof of a pause (server/src/services/agent-execution-stop.ts), the start of every run of a task (heartbeat.ts, the workspace selection), the workspace readiness of a run (fresh-workspace-continuation.ts), the session reset reason (heartbeat/run-state.ts), the adapter events a run may write (heartbeat/run-output.ts), the host callbacks of a legacy adapter execution (heartbeat/runtime-execution.ts), and the process callbacks of the two local engine adapters

patches.title: A `project_commenter` agent API key scope: the key may find, read and comment on the tickets of the projects it names, and nothing else; it needs no run (its own cap of 20 comments an hour), and a server without the scope refuses its token
patches.problem: The studio needs an agent that relays outside events (a pull request, a build) onto the ticket that follows them: find the ticket by its text or its work products, read its comments, and write one comment that wakes the holder. That agent never runs an engine. The only keys an agent can hold today are `standard` (everything the agent may do), `task_bridge` and `skill_test`: a standard key gives far more than the relay needs, and a stolen one would too. And a key without a run cannot comment on another agent's ticket at all: `assertCrossIssueInfluenceWithinRunCap` (routes/issues.ts) refuses every agent write without a run with `cross_issue_influence_run_context_required`, because the cross-issue cap counts writes per run. Last, `normalizeAgentApiKeyScope` reads an unknown scope as `standard`: a new scope added to the key's row alone would be read as a full key by a server that does not know it (a rollback).
patches.reason: Decided by the studio on 25 Nov 2026, after a note written before the code: deny by default, in two locks (a route guard and the authorization service), reduced answers, and six points of a code reading taken without widening the scope (the search runs over comments as today but not over documents, the tickets of every holder of the project, the exact fields, whole bodies, the product's cursor, the product's bounds of 50 and 100). On the cap, option (a): the key needs no run, but it keeps a cap of its own, 20 comments an hour and per key, each one written to the activity log, the 21st refused clearly; a stolen key cannot wake the roles without bound (each comment wakes the holder, an engine, a cost). On the rollback, the simple way: a token of its own prefix kept under a hash separated by a domain, so that a server without the scope finds no key and answers 401, never `standard`. The key and its agent are created only after the install, by a Board user, through today's route.

patches.migration: None: no table, no column, no setting. A new value of the existing `agent_api_keys.scope_config` (jsonb): `{ kind: "project_commenter", projectIds: [one to ten project ids of the agent's company] }`, checked at the key's creation. Such a key gets a token `pcc_...` (not `pcp_...`), kept in `key_hash` as sha256("paperclip.project_commenter.v1\n" + token) instead of sha256(token). The authentication looks a `pcc_` token up under that hash only, and requires the key found to carry the scope; a key of the scope found by the ordinary hash is refused. Such a key has no run: a request of it that carries `X-Paperclip-Run-Id` is refused (below, reason `run_header_not_allowed`), and the authentication never takes a run id into its actor, so that its comment is never tied to another agent's run. A route guard mounted right after the actor is resolved, before every route (app.ts, after the cloud control middleware), lets such a key reach four requests only, and answers 403 `project_commenter_route_denied` to every other: GET /api/companies/:companyId/issues (its company, `projectId` one of its projects, only `q`, `projectId`, `limit`); GET /api/issues/:id (no query); GET /api/issues/:id/comments (only `order`, `limit`, `afterCommentId`); POST /api/issues/:id/comments (a body of `body` and `reopen: false` or absent). The authorization service admits only `issue:read` and `issue:comment` on a ticket of its projects, whatever route asks, and refuses connection management to the scope. The answers: the list gives `id`, `companyId`, `projectId`, `assigneeAgentId`, `status` of each ticket, and its search (`q`) does not read documents for this key; the detail gives the same fields and the work products' `type`, `provider`, `externalId`, `url`; the comments give `id`, `authorAgentId` and the whole `body` (after the product's secret redaction). A comment of such a key needs no run: it is counted on the key (the key's row locked), 20 in any hour, each one written to the activity log as `issue.cross_issue_influence_observed` with `keyId` where a run's id would be; the 21st is refused (429) and written as `issue.cross_issue_influence_cap_rejected`. Every other key and actor: unchanged. To recognise such a key in the database without reading a secret (read-only, works on a database without one): `select count(*) from agent_api_keys where scope_config->>'kind' = 'project_commenter' and revoked_at is null`.
patches.rollback: Revoke every `project_commenter` key first (the count above must be 0), then switch cli/current back to the previous install folder. Even if one is left, a server without this patch hashes the `pcc_` token as an ordinary one, finds no key and answers 401: it never reads the key as a standard one. Nothing else is written by this patch but the cap's activity entries, which an older server ignores.
patches.retireWhen: Upstream gives a key limited to reading and commenting on the tickets of named projects, with a cap of its own when it has no run (the narrow credential of #4403); or the studio no longer relays outside events onto tickets. Until then the scope and its cap stay as written.
patches.origin: What: in packages/shared/src/validators/agent.ts, `projectCommenterAgentKeyScopeSchema` in the scope union, and its type exported (validators/index.ts, index.ts). In server/src/middleware/project-commenter-scope.ts, `projectCommenterScopeOf`, `projectCommenterRouteRefusal` (the four requests and their parameters; no run id header) and `projectCommenterRouteGuard`, mounted in app.ts after `cloudControlMiddleware()`. In lib/agent-records.ts, `PROJECT_COMMENTER_TOKEN_PREFIX`, `createProjectCommenterToken`, `hashProjectCommenterToken`; in services/agents.ts the key's creation checks its projects and uses that token and hash; in middleware/auth.ts the lookup by that hash, the match between the token's prefix and the key's scope, and no run id in such a key's actor. In services/authorization.ts, the project_commenter block before the trust resolution, and connection management refused. In routes/issues.ts, the three reduced answers, `excludeDocumentSearch` on the list, and the run-less branch of `assertCrossIssueInfluenceWithinRunCap`; in services/issues.ts and task-search.ts the `excludeDocumentSearch` filter and `includeDocuments` parameter; in services/cross-issue-influence-limit.ts `observeProjectCommenterInfluence` and `PROJECT_COMMENTER_HOURLY_CAP`. Why: see `problem` and `reason`. To re-apply after an upstream update: re-add each of these (search STUDIO-0102); if upstream changed `normalizeAgentApiKeyScope`, the token's own prefix and hash stay, so that a server without the scope never reads the key as standard.

patches.title: A task that the hold of a run cut by a pause blocked gets its status back at the role's resume, on the server's own proof of the stop, and continues once; any other block or cut keeps the Board's reconciliation
patches.problem: Production, 26 Nov 2026, pose windows of studio.32 (pause 22:35) and of the worker router 0.30.29 (pauses 23:19 and 23:31): the Board paused every role, then resumed it. The runs the pause cut (cancelled agent_paused, or the lifecycle stop) left their hold legacy_execution_requires_reconciliation; the hold's settlement (settleUnrecoverableExecutions) or stranded-work recovery then blocked the task and wrote the receipt legacyCancellationBlock. At the resume the continuation of STUDIO-0074 refused every blocked task ('task_blocked', pause-resume-continuation.ts, continueOne), whoever had blocked it: eleven tasks (TR-3388, TR-3389, TR-3393, TR-3394, TR-3395 among them) waited for the Board's reconciliation (POST /api/issues/:id/recovery-actions/resolve, tools/reconcile-cut-run.mjs), lifted by hand from 23:22 to 00:08 UTC, while the CTO and the Infra Manager, who cannot make that gesture, circled around it (TR-3435).
patches.reason: The rule (studio, 27 Nov 2026), chosen because it adds no authority to anyone: the server undoes only its own block, on facts it reads itself, and files the continuation the owner already ordered (STUDIO-0074); opening the resolution to the role's manager would have given roles a gesture that needs the Board's attestation today. At the resume, a task blocked by the cut run's own hold (the hold is the legacy hold of that run, neither reconciled nor kept for a workspace, and its receipt names the run with the task's current status version) gets its previous status back once the server proves the stop on the checks of the Board's reconciliation (validateExecutionReconciliation: run cancelled and owned by the assignee, no live process of it on this server, no coordinator lease nor linked continuation, no unreleased environment lease); the restore, its activity entry agent.pause_cut_work_unblocked and the resume's Retry commit in one transaction, or nothing does. The Retry then follows its own gate (stop proof, pending decisions, one continuation, the same conversation) and its run lifts the hold. A run cut by a failure or by a person's cancel is not looked at; a block the role set after the hold's (status version moved), a task waiting on a blocker, and a pause-cut run without that proof keep the hold and the Board path (refusal task_blocked_stop_not_proven names what is missing).
patches.owner: the continuation at the resume of runs cut by a pause (server/src/services/pause-resume-continuation.ts, STUDIO-0074)

patches.title: A new agent is born without the right to create agents unless its creation request asks for it
patches.problem: defaultAgentPermissions (server/src/lib/agent-permissions.ts) gave canCreateAgents: true to every new agent outside the low-trust preset: prepareAgentHire (server/src/services/agent-hiring.ts) normalizes the requested permissions in the "create" context and persists the result, so a hire or a creation whose request said nothing about canCreateAgents stored true. The legacy creator allow of the authorization service (canCreateAgentsLegacy, server/src/services/authorization.ts) then let that agent hire and create agents. Seen in production: the Quest Writer, hired by the Super RH role, was born with canCreateAgents: true (removed by hand after approval). STUDIO-0084 had removed the other default rights of a new agent, but only from the grant list (NEW_STANDARD_AGENT_DEFAULT_GRANT_KEYS); canCreateAgents is a flag of the agent's permissions record, not a grant key, so it stayed.
patches.reason: The owner's decision: creating roles is reserved to the Super RH. A new agent therefore does not receive the right by default; it receives it only when the creation request carries canCreateAgents: true, which only an actor that already passes agents:create can send (the hire and create routes ask agents:create before anything else).
patches.owner: new-agent default permissions (server/src/lib/agent-permissions.ts, defaultAgentPermissions)

The default is upstream's choice: #12814 (merged 2026-09-04, 'grant new agents hire permission by default') made canCreateAgents default to true for new standard-trust agents so that agent teams grow without per-agent toggling. Related, unchanged by this patch: #20041 (merged, honour an explicit hiring denial on CEO agents, the ceoHiringDeniedBy record kept here), #15904 (open, canCreateAgents gates several capabilities), #14830 (open, an import parsing defect that resets agent permissions to true). No upstream change returns to a disabled default: this is a studio policy, not an upstream defect.

patches.title: At the resume of a role, a pending card addressed to it whose run the pause cut wakes it once again
patches.problem: Production, 26 Nov 2026, TR-3106: the task's assignee (CTO) created an ask_user_questions card (continuation_policy wake_assignee) addressed to the Feedback Manager. The card's wake was promoted to a run (issue_execution_promoted, payload issueId, mutation interaction, interactionId, interactionKind, sourceRunId). A Board pause of the Feedback Manager (POST /api/agents/:id/pause) cancelled that run (error_code agent_paused); the wake request was left cancelled, error "Cancelled due to agent pause", with its runId set. At the resume nothing woke the addressee and the card stayed pending. A manual wake (POST /api/agents/:id/wakeup with payload.issueId) was cancelled within the second as issue_assignee_changed, because the addressee does not own the task.
patches.reason: replayWakesMissedDuringPause (STUDIO-0028, server/src/services/pause-missed-wakes.ts) replays a wake the pause refused or cancelled before it had a run (runId null), and STUDIO-0038 a pending card with no wake recorded; a card wake whose run had already been created fell between the two. continueRunsCutByPause (STUDIO-0074) continues cut runs only on tasks the agent owns. Now a card wake cancelled by a pause stop with its run counts as a lost card wake for an addressee that does not own the task, and is replayed with the shape of the card's own wake (mutation interaction, wakeReason interaction_pending), which dispatch verifies (verifyAddresseeInteractionWake) instead of cancelling it as issue_assignee_changed. Same guards as the other lost wakes: the card is still pending and addressed to the agent, no wake of the agent for the task is live, no run of the agent on the task since the loss (a run dispatch cancelled as issue_assignee_changed did nothing and does not count), one wake per loss by its idempotency key. On the agent's own task the cut run stays with STUDIO-0074.
patches.owner: the replay of wakes lost to a pause (server/src/services/pause-missed-wakes.ts), called by the lifecycle driver when the agent is ready again

patches.validation: pause-cut-card-wake.test.ts reproduces the production sequence on an embedded database (the card's promoted wake and its run, the pause route's cancelActiveForAgent, the resume) and checks: the addressee is woken once with the card's wake; through the real queue the replayed wake is not refused nor cancelled as issue_assignee_changed and a second resume adds nothing; a manual wake cancelled as issue_assignee_changed does not stop the replay; no wake when one for the task is queued, when the card is answered or addressed to another agent, or on the agent's own task. The test fails on the base and passes with the change; pause-missed-wakes.test.ts and paused-addressee-card.test.ts still pass. At the bench: pause the addressee during its card run, resume, the card's addressee runs once.
